en: APEC COOPERATION ARRANGEMENT FOR CROSS-BORDER PRIVACY ENFORCEMENT
cn: APEC 跨境隐私执法合作安排
summary: 第 1 部分 本框架目标 2015 年 APEC 领导人核准修订版《APEC 隐私框架》，认识到应当制定有效的隐私保护规则，避免对信息流动设置障碍，保障 APEC 地区贸易持续开展与经济增长。 本合作安排目标如下： 促进 APEC 各经济体隐私执法机构之间的信息共享； 建立机制，推动隐私执法机构之间就隐私法律开展有效的跨境合作，包括案件移送、平行调查、联合调查或者联合执法行动； 推动隐私执法机构就执行跨境隐私规则开展合作； 鼓励与 APEC 域外隐私执法机构开展隐私调查与执法的信息共享与合作，保障本合作安排可与经合组织建议等域外同类安排无缝衔接。 第 2.1‑2.3 款 2.1 本合作安排建立一套可落地的多边机制，供隐私执法机构开展跨境隐私执法合作；在该框架之下，隐私执法机构可自愿开展信息共享、提出协助请求、提供协助。 2.2 APEC 任一经济体的隐私执法机构均可参与本合作安排。 2.3 一个经济体可以有多家参与本安排的隐私执法机构，前提是各该公共机构均满足第 4.1 款关于隐私执法机构的定义标准。 第 4.1 款 定义 “隐私执法机构”：指负责执行隐私法律，有权开展调查或者提起执法程序的公共机构。 “隐私法律”：指 APEC 经济体的法律法规，执行该等法律法规能够实现与《2015 APEC 隐私框架》相一致的个人信息保护效果。 “协助请求” 包括但不限于： （一）移送与隐私法律执行相关的案件； （二）请求就隐私法律执行开展合作； （三）请求就涉嫌违反隐私法律行为的调查开展合作； （四）移交隐私投诉。 第 6.1‑6.2 款 6.1 解读本安排应当与《2015 APEC 隐私框架》保持一致。 6.2 本合作安排无意： （一）创设具有约束力的义务，不改变国际法、国内法项下既有义务，不为参与方经济体创设法律义务； （二）不妨碍参与方依据其他协定、条约、安排或实践，向其他参与方或者非参与方执法机构寻求或提供协助； （三）不影响隐私执法机构依据法律，向位于另一参与方经济体境内的主体调取信息的权限；亦不禁止该主体自愿向隐私执法机构提供信息； （四）不妨碍为维护国家安全、公共安全、主权或其他公共政策，依据法律实施的政府行为； （五）创设超出参与方权限与管辖范围的合作义务或合作预期； （六）为其他非参与政府机构创设义务； （七）不影响请求方、接收方政府之间依据司法协助条约或其他国际协定使用信息的权限。 第 7.1 款 协助的限制 7.1 参与方拥有自主裁量权，可随时拒绝受理、拒绝推进协助请求，或限定合作范围，包括但不限于如下情形： （一）该事项与国内法律或政策相抵触； （二）该事项不在参与方权限、管辖范围之内； （三）请求事项所涉行为，不属于请求方与接收方依据各自隐私法律均有权调查、执法的行为； （四）资源受限； （五）与其他工作优先级冲突； （六）双方对该事项不存在共同利益； （七）事项超出本合作安排适用范围； （八）其他机构（含私营机构）更适合处理该事项； （九）其他导致参与方无法开展合作的情形。参与方可书面告知拒绝理由。 第 8.1‑8.2 款 参与与退出 8.1 隐私执法机构向管理人提交书面通知，即可参与本合作安排；参与申请应当附经济体 ECSG 代表团或其他有权政府代表的确认函，证明申请机构符合 4.1 款隐私执法机构定义。管理人正式书面接受通知之后参与生效，同时满足 5.3 (ii) 的核验要求。 8.2 参与机构向管理人提交1 个月书面通知，即可退出本合作安排。 第 9.1‑9.3 款 跨境合作 9.1 在遵守第 6、7 款前提下，参与方应当受理其他参与方的协助请求、案件移送，开展信息共享，就隐私法律的调查、执法相互协助。 9.2 跨境合作工作复杂且消耗资源，参与方可单独或共同对案件划分优先级；优先级主要参考个人信息隐私被非法侵害的严重程度、实际或潜在损害及其他相关因素。请求优先处理某协助请求的，应当在协助请求表中写明理由。 9.3 在 7.1、9.2 款约束下，各参与方确认：执行 APEC 跨境隐私规则（CBPR）属于本安排项下合作优先事项。 第 10 款 保密（核心节选） 10.1 在遵守 9.10、10.3 款，且符合请求方、接收方适用法律的前提下，参与方之间依据本安排开展的磋商、沟通与信息共享内容属于保密信息，不得对外披露。 10.2 各参与方应当在本国法律允许范围内尽最大努力，对另一方以保密方式提供的信息予以保密，尊重另一方提出的保密保障要求。 10.3 若请求方国内法律强制要求向第三方（其他执法机构等）披露保密信息，则本安排不禁止该类披露。 10.5 机构退出本合作安排之后，仍然应当对从其他参与方处获取的保密信息承担保密义务。
summaryEn: Para 1 Objectives of this framework In endorsing the updated APEC Privacy Framework in 2015, APEC leaders recognised the importance of developing effective privacy protections that avoid barriers to information flows and ensure continued trade and economic growth in the APEC region. The goals of this Cooperation Arrangement are to: facilitate information sharing among Privacy Enforcement Authorities in APEC economies; establish mechanisms to promote effective cross‑border cooperation between Privacy Enforcement Authorities on the enforcement of Privacy Law, including through referrals of matters and through parallel or joint investigations or enforcement actions; facilitate Privacy Enforcement Authority cooperation in enforcing Cross‑Border Privacy Rules; and encourage information sharing and cooperation on privacy investigation and enforcement with privacy enforcement authorities outside APEC, including by ensuring this Cooperation Arrangement can work seamlessly with similar arrangements such as those developed under the OECD Recommendation. Para 2.1‑2.3 2.1 This Cooperation Arrangement creates a practical multilateral mechanism for Privacy Enforcement Authorities to cooperate in cross‑border privacy enforcement. It does this by creating a framework under which Privacy Enforcement Authorities may, on a voluntary basis, share information and request and render assistance in certain ways. 2.2 Any Privacy Enforcement Authority in an APEC economy may participate in this Cooperation Arrangement. 2.3 An Economy can have more than one participating Privacy Enforcement Authority provided each public body meets the criteria established in the definition of Privacy Enforcement Authority as contained in paragraph 4.1. Para 4.1 Definitions ‘Privacy Enforcement Authority’ means any public body that is responsible for enforcing Privacy Law, and that has powers to conduct investigations or pursue enforcement proceedings. ‘Privacy Law’ means laws and regulations of an APEC economy, the enforcement of which have the effect of protecting personal information consistent with the 2015 APEC Privacy Framework. ‘Request for Assistance’ includes, but is not limited to: (i) a referral of a matter related to the enforcement of a Privacy Law; (ii) a request for cooperation on the enforcement of a Privacy Law; (iii) a request for cooperation on the investigation of an alleged breach of a Privacy Law; and (iv) a transfer of a privacy complaint. Para 6.1‑6.2 6.1 This arrangement is to be read consistently with the 2015 APEC Privacy Framework. 6.2 Nothing in this Cooperation Arrangement is intended to: (i) Create binding obligations, or affect existing obligations under international or domestic law, or create obligations under the laws of the Participants’ economies. (ii) Prevent a Participant from seeking assistance from or providing assistance to another Participant or another non‑participating enforcement authority of an APEC member economy, pursuant to other agreements, treaties, arrangements, or practices. (iii) Affect any authority or right of a Privacy Enforcement Authority or non‑participating authority to seek information on a lawful basis, including in law enforcement matters, from a person located in the territory of another Participant’s economy, nor is it intended to preclude any such person from voluntarily providing information to a Privacy Enforcement Authority or non‑participating authority. (iv) Impede governmental activities authorized by law when taken to protect security, public safety, sovereignty or other public policy of an APEC member economy. (v) Create obligations or expectations of cooperation that would exceed a Participant’s scope of authority and jurisdiction. (vi) Create obligations or expectations for other, non‑participating government agencies. (vii) affect any authority or right to use information pursuant to a mutual legal assistance treaty (MLAT) or other applicable international agreements between the Requesting and Receiving Authorities' governments. Para 7.1 Limitations on Assistance 7.1 At its sole discretion, a Participant may at any time decline to accept or proceed with a Request for Assistance, or limit its cooperation including, but not limited, under the following circumstances: (i) The matter is inconsistent with domestic law or policy. (ii) The matter is not within the Participant’s scope of authority or jurisdiction. (iii) The matter is not an act or practice of a kind that both the Requesting Authority and Receiving Authority are authorized to investigate or enforce against under their Privacy Laws. (iv) There are resource constraints. (v) The matter is inconsistent with other priorities. (vi) There is an absence of mutual interest in the matter in question. (vii) The matter is outside the scope of this Cooperation Arrangement. (viii)Another body (including a private sector body, consistent with paragraph 9.4) is a more appropriate body to handle the matter. (ix) Any other circumstances that renders a Participant unable to cooperate. The Participant may notify the basis of these circumstances in writing. Para 8.1‑8.2 Participation / Cease participation 8.1 A Privacy Enforcement Authority may participate in this Cooperation Arrangement by giving written notice to the Administrator. The participation should be supported by a written letter of confirmation from the economy’s ECSG delegation, or other appropriate governmental representative, that the applicant is a Privacy Enforcement Authority within the meaning of the definition in paragraph 4.1. The participation will take effect after the Administrator has formally accepted the Participant’s written notice, subject to the outcomes of paragraph 5.3(ii). 8.2 A Participant may cease participation in this Cooperation Arrangement by giving one month’s written notice to the Administrator. Para 9.1‑9.3 Cross‑border cooperation 9.1 Subject to paragraphs 6 and 7, Participants should assist one another by considering other Participants’ Requests for Assistance and referrals for investigation or enforcement, and share information and cooperate on the investigation or enforcement of Privacy Laws. 9.2 Given that cross‑border cooperation can be complex and resource‑intensive, Participants may individually or collectively prioritize those matters that are most serious in nature based upon the severity of the unlawful infringements of personal information privacy, the actual or potential harm involved, as well as other relevant considerations. Participants requesting prioritisation of a particular Request for Assistance should specify the reasons in the Request for Assistance form. 9.3 Subject to paragraphs 7.1 and 9.2, Participants recognize the enforcement of APEC Cross‑Border Privacy Rules as a priority for cooperation under this Arrangement. Para 10 Confidentiality 10.1 Subject to paragraphs 9.10 and 10.3, and in accordance with any laws applicable to the Requesting and Receiving Authority, consultations, other communications or information shared between Participants pursuant to this Cooperation Arrangement, are confidential and will not be disclosed. 10.2 Each Participant should, to the fullest extent possible and consistent with its economy’s laws, use best efforts to maintain the confidentiality of any information communicated to it in confidence by another Participant and respect any safeguards sought by the other Participant. 10.3 Nothing in this Cooperation Arrangement prevents disclosure of confidential information to third parties, such as other law enforcement agencies, if such disclosure is required by the law of the Requesting Authority’s economy. 10.5 Upon ceasing participation in this Cooperation Arrangement, a Privacy Enforcement Authority should maintain the confidentiality of any information provided to it in confidence by another Participant.

en: ANNEX A: APEC CROSS-BORDER E-COMMERCE FACILITATION FRAMEWORK
cn: 附件A：APEC跨境电子商务促进框架
summary: 目标 9. 考虑到上述因素，本框架旨在通过以下方式促进 APEC 范围内的跨境电子商务： - 创建有利的电子商务监管生态系统，以促进可预见性、透明度、安全性、公平竞争和一致性； - 推动信息和通信技术基础设施的发展，以便利跨境电子商务； - 鼓励和促进企业更广泛地参与全球商业，特别是中小微企业； - 加强公共部门和私营部门之间的合作，包括在消费者保护方面的合作； - 促进本地区贸易和投资便利化，支持实现茂物目标和 2020 年后愿景。 工作支柱 10. 为实现上述目标，APEC 应重点关注以下工作支柱。每一支柱均应包括用于评估绩效的具体活动： (i) 促进透明、可预见、商业友好且协调一致的法律和监管方法及措施，以便利本地区跨境电子商务 11. 电子商务政策和法规缺乏协调一致性，一直是跨境电子商务面临的障碍之一。 12. 应努力协助 APEC 经济体，特别是发展中经济体，理解并建立透明、可预见的跨境电子商务监管和法律框架，以促进整个地区各经济体之间更好地协调一致。 13. 因此，继续努力分享本地区电子商务监管最佳实践，仍是创造有利环境、便利跨境电子商务和促进在线消费者保护的优先事项。 14. 可考虑在本支柱下开展以下活动： - 审查与跨境电子商务有关的现有法律和监管问题，包括但不限于数字产品； - 考虑现有国际标准和指南； - 从法律和监管角度识别跨境电子商务的瓶颈和措施，同时考虑供应链框架行动计划第二阶段； - 促进政府机构和其他相关利益攸关方之间就新的法律和监管问题开展对话和互动； - 促进电子商务法规实施中的透明度和可预见性； - 分享最佳实践，将其作为政策制定者能力建设的有用工具； - 鼓励 APEC 经济体审查其国内电子商务政策； - 研究电子商务中新兴技术和监管趋势； - 更新 2008 年通过的《数字繁荣清单》。 (ii) 加强能力建设，使 APEC 经济体能够帮助中小微企业提高其参与全球和区域市场跨境电子商务的能力 17. 有必要减少阻碍中小微企业在本地区扩张的壁垒，同时加强面向各经济体的能力建设计划，以帮助中小微企业参与跨境电子商务。 18. 可考虑在本支柱下开展以下活动： - 识别企业，特别是中小微企业参与跨境电子商务的瓶颈和措施； - 识别、分享并形成各经济体之间的最佳实践，特别是中小微企业参与跨境电子商务方面的最佳实践； - 识别供应端缺口，例如支持本地区使用跨境电子商务所需的市场专业知识、贸易规则、标准和服务质量方面的知识； - 积极鼓励公共部门和私营部门在适当的 APEC 论坛中制定并实施项目，以解决与中小微企业参与跨境电子商务有关的问题； - 鼓励公共部门和私营部门之间开展合作与协作，例如围绕跨境电子商务现有和新兴问题开展公私伙伴关系和公私对话； - 支持各经济体内部开展能力建设活动，以便利中小微企业从跨境电子商务中获益。 (iii) 通过加强实施 APEC 现有项目，强化跨境数据隐私保护 19. 我们认识到，有效保护信息和数据隐私，同时维持亚太地区各经济体之间及其贸易伙伴之间的信息和数据流动的重要性。 20. 我们重视 APEC 在隐私方面正在开展的努力和项目。我们认识到 APEC 跨境隐私规则（CBPRs）体系和处理者隐私认可（PRPs）体系的重要性，这些是参与方寻求扩大参与范围的自愿机制；我们支持在这一领域加强合作，包括通过促进能力建设来加强合作。 21. 可考虑在本支柱下开展以下活动： - 在考虑《APEC 隐私框架》的基础上，促进对个人信息的适当国内数据隐私保护； - 鼓励 APEC 经济体更新其《数据隐私个人行动计划》； - 鼓励便利有意愿的 APEC 经济体参与 APEC 的 CBPRs 和 PRPs； - 促进围绕《APEC 隐私框架》和国内法规开展讨论，以确保在数据隐私法规方面采取协调一致的方法； - 支持 APEC 成员之间开展能力建设，以加强其国内数据隐私法规，并使其考虑《APEC 隐私框架》； - 分享跨境数据隐私法规和政策相关问题的经验和最佳实践； - 加强并深化旨在促进隐私框架之间互操作性的国际合作； - 持续监测本地区跨境隐私问题和倡议的发展，并与其他国际论坛共享信息。 (iv) 促进本地区跨境无纸化贸易 22. 电子化提交和处理文件的无纸化贸易，是贸易便利化的重要基础。APEC 认识到，持续努力加强无纸化贸易，对于电子商务货物的高效处理和清关至关重要。 23. 我们鼓励成员结合商业界，特别是本地区中小微企业，考虑跨境无纸化贸易便利化方法。 24. 此外，我们鼓励 APEC 经济体实施《WTO 贸易便利化协定》（TFA），特别是其中旨在使海关程序相关信息可在互联网上获取的条款（第 1 条、第 7 条和第 10 条）。 25. 鉴于贸易便利化的重要性，我们鼓励在相关论坛和分论坛中开展持续和额外工作，以进一步便利跨境无纸化贸易。 26. 可考虑在本支柱下开展以下活动： - 识别瓶颈并开展能力建设，以进一步便利跨境无纸化贸易，包括企业对消费者（B2C）、企业对企业（B2B）和政府对企业（G2B）； - 通过简化货物运输和清关，同时支持风险管理，建立有利环境以便利跨境无纸化贸易； - 识别瓶颈并努力加强电子支付系统的使用，同时确保安全； - 分享跨境无纸化贸易监管方法方面的最佳实践并支持能力建设，包括单一窗口建设和边境管理； - 与相关分论坛合作，探索其他技术和创新，以在支持有效风险管理的同时进一步便利跨境无纸化贸易； - 鼓励 APEC 成员更新其《APEC 无纸化贸易个人行动计划》； - 与本领域其他国际论坛和组织开展合作，例如联合国国际贸易法委员会（UNCITRAL）、亚洲及太平洋经济社会委员会（ESCAP）、世界海关组织（WCO）、万国邮政联盟（UPU）或国家邮政运营商（NPO）、世界贸易组织（WTO）以及 APEC 以外的其他相关组织。 (v) 处理跨境电子商务中的新兴和交叉问题 27. 需要认真考虑与跨境电子商务有关的现有和新兴交叉问题。这将要求各工作组和 APEC 论坛密切协作，以找到最合适的解决方案。 28. 我们支持促进跨境电子商务的信息自由流动，同时尊重合法公共政策利益，包括适用的国内和/或国际隐私和数据保护法律框架。 29. 此外，在本地区促进跨境电子商务过程中，已出现若干重要问题，包括边境管理、税收、知识产权、在线消费者保护以及 ICT 使用中的安全问题，这些问题被认为对参与跨境电子商务的企业尤为重要。 30. 我们鼓励制定促进跨境电子商务参与者之间信任和信心的政策和框架，并确保消费者和企业均可获得跨境电子商务的利益。 31. 可考虑在本支柱下开展以下活动： - 研究、学习并理解与跨境电子商务有关的新的和新兴的交叉问题； - 识别障碍，并鼓励分享关于便利跨境电子商务跨境信息流动的最佳实践； - 鼓励分享关于在线消费者保护、跨境电子商务经营者税收问题的最佳实践； - 识别并分享促进电子认证方法，包括电子签名的最佳实践； - 识别障碍，并鼓励分享边境管理方面的最佳实践，包括但不限于边境货物检查流程； - 与 UPU 或 NPO 以及参与跨境投递和配送的其他利益攸关方协调，以保障和改善跨境电子商务的可持续性； - 提高对网络犯罪以及在跨境电子商务中强有力、有效地保障 ICT 使用安全之必要性的认识； - 维持新兴信息通信技术和产业的实施，确保本地区跨境电子商务领域的互操作性； - 推动更好地测度跨境电子商务，并分析其经济影响，包括测度相关保护主义措施和反竞争做法的负面影响； - 通过聚焦电子商务并纳入新兴问题，推动 ECSG 职权范围现代化； - 继续与其他工作组和 APEC 论坛密切合作，包括但不限于海关程序分委员会（SCCP）、中小企业工作组（SMEWG）、电信工作组（TELWG）、贸易投资委员会（CTI）以及经济技术合作指导委员会（SCE）等。
summaryEn: Objectives 9. Taking into account the above considerations, the Framework aims to promote cross- border e-commerce across APEC by: - Creating a favorable regulatory eco-system for e-commerce to promote predictability, transparency, security, fair competition and consistency; - Promoting development of Information and Communication Technology infrastructure for facilitating cross-border e-commerce; - Encouraging and facilitating greater participation of businesses in global commerce, in particular MSMEs; - Enhancing cooperation between public and private sectors, including on consumer protection; - Contributing to trade and investment facilitation in the region, supporting the achievement of the Bogor Goals and post 2020 vision. Working Pillars 10. To achieve the above objectives, APEC should focus on the following working pillars. Each pillar should include specific activities to assess the performance: (i) Promoting transparent and predictable legal and regulatory approaches and measures that are business friendly and coherent to facilitate cross-border e- commerce in the region 11. Lack of coherent policies and regulations on e-commerce has been one of the obstacles for cross-border e-commerce. 12. Efforts should be made to assist APEC economies, especially developing economies, to understand and develop transparent and predictable regulatory and legal framework for cross-border e-commerce, with the aim of promoting better alignment among Economies throughout the region. 13. Consequently, working towards sharing best practices in e-commerce regulations in the region remains apriority to create a favorable environment to facilitate cross-border e- commerce and promote online consumer protection. 14. The following activities could be considered under this pillar: - Review existing legal and regulatory issues related to cross-border e-commerce including but not limited to digital products; - Consider existing international standards and guidelines; - Identify choke points and measures to cross-border e-commerce from legal and regulatory perspective, taking into account Phase II of the Supply Chain Framework Action Plan; - Promote dialogue and interaction on new legal and regulatory issues among government agencies and other related stakeholders; - Promote transparency and predictability in implementation of e-commerce regulations; - Share best practices as useful tools for capacity building of policymakers; - Encourage APEC Economies to undertake reviews of their domestic e-commerce policies; - Conduct research on emerging technological and regulatory trends in e-commerce; - Update the Digital Prosperity Checklist endorsed in 2008. (ii) Enhancing capacity building so that APEC Economies can assist MSMEs to increase their cross-border e-commerce participation in global and regional markets 17. It is necessary to reduce barriers that impede MSMEs expansion in the region, in parallel with efforts to enhance capacity building programs for Economies to assist MSMEs participation in cross-border e-commerce. 18. The following activities could be considered under this pillar: - Identify choke points and measures for businesses, especially MSMEs, to participate in cross-border e-commerce; - Identify, share and develop best practices among economies, especially MSMEs to participate in cross-border e-commerce; - Identify supply side gaps such as knowledge of market expertise and trade rules, standards and service quality required to support the use of cross-border e- commerce in the region; - Actively encourage public and private sectors to develop and implement projects in appropriate fora to address issues related to MSMEs’ participation in cross-border e- commerce; - Encourage cooperation and collaboration between public and private sectors such as Public Private Partnership (PPP), Public-Private Dialogue (PPD) on existing and emerging issues in cross-border e-commerce; - Support capacity building activities within Economies to facilitate MSMEs’ gain on cross-border e-commerce. (iii) Strengthening cross-border data privacy protection through increased implementation of existing APEC programs 19. We recognize the importance of effective protection of information and data privacy, while still maintaining information and data flows among economies in the Asia-Pacific region, and among their trading partners. 20. We value APEC’s on-going efforts and programs on privacy. We recognize the importance of the APEC Cross-border Privacy Rules (CBPRs) System and Privacy Recognition for Processors (PRPs) System, voluntary mechanisms whose participants seek to expand the participation, and we support enhanced cooperation in this area, including through promoting capacity building. 21. The following activities could be considered under this pillar: - Promote appropriate domestic data privacy protection for personal information taking into account the APEC Privacy Framework; - Encourage APEC economies to update their Data Privacy Individual Action Plan; - Encourage facilitation of interested APEC economies’ participation in CBPRs and PRPs in APEC; - Facilitate discussion on the APEC Privacy Framework and domestic regulations to ensure a coherent and consistent approach to data privacy regulations; - Support capacity building efforts among the APEC members to enhance their domestic data privacy regulations which take into account the APEC Privacy Framework; - Share experience and best practices on issues related to cross-border data privacy regulations and policies; - Enhance and strengthen international collaboration aimed at promoting interoperability between privacy frameworks; - Continue regional monitoring developments in and share information with other international fora on cross-border privacy issues and initiatives. (iv) Facilitating cross-border paperless trade in the region 22. It is recognized that paperless trade, the advanced electronic submission and processing of documents are a key foundation of trade facilitation. APEC recognizes that continued efforts to strengthen paperless trade are critical to the efficient processing and clearance of e-commerce shipments. 23. We encourage members to consider approaches to cross-border paperless trade facilitation in cooperation with the business community, particularly with MSMEs in the region. 24. In addition, we encourage APEC Economies to implement the WTO Trade Facilitation Agreement (TFA), particularly those provisions which aim to make more information related to customs procedures available on the Internet (Article 1, Article 7 and Article 10). 25. In recognition of the importance of trade facilitation, we encourage ongoing and additional ways to further facilitate cross-border paperless trade, working with relevant fora and sub- fora. 26. The following activities could be considered under this pillar: - Identify chokepoints and build capacities for further facilitating cross-border paperless trade including business-to-consumer (B2C), business-to-business (B2B) and government-to-business (G2B); - Establish a favorable environment to facilitate cross-border paperless trade through streamlined shipments and clearance goods while supporting risk management; - Identify chokepoints and work towards strengthening the use of e-payment systems while ensuring the security; - Share best practices and support capacity building on cross-border paperless trade regulatory approaches including single window development and border management; - Working with the relevant sub-fora, explore other technologies and innovations to further facilitate cross-border paperless trade, while supporting effective risk management; - Encourage APEC members to update their APEC Paperless Trading Individual Action Plans; - Conduct collaboration with other international fora and organizations in this area such as the United Nations Commission on International Trade Law (UNCITRAL), The Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (ESCAP), World Customs Organization (WCO), Universal Postal Unit (UPU) or National Postal Operators (NPO), World Trade Organization (WTO) and other relevant organizations outside of APEC. (v) Addressing emerging and cross-cutting issues in cross border e-commerce 27. Existing and emerging cross-cutting issues related to cross-border e-commerce needs to be taken into serious consideration. This would require working groups and APEC fora to collaborate closely to find the most suitable solution for such issues. 28. We support the free flow of information for promoting cross-border e-commerce while respecting legitimate public policy interests includingapplicable domestic and /or international legal frameworks for privacy and data protection. 29. Besides, several issues have emerged as significant in the promotion of cross-border e- commerce in the region including border management, taxation, Intellectual Property Rights, online consumer protection and security in the use of ICTs, which are considered to be of particular importance for businesses participating in cross-border e-commerce. 30. We encourage the development of policies and frameworks that promote trust and confidence among cross-border e-commerce participants, and which ensures the benefits of cross-border e-commerce are available for consumers and businesses alike. 31. The following activities could be considered under this pillar: - Research, study and understand new and emerging cross-cutting issues related to cross-border e-commerce; - Identify barriers and encourage best practices sharing in facilitation of cross-border information flows for cross-border e-commerce; - Encourage sharing best practices on online consumer protection, taxation issues on cross-border e-commerce operators; - Identify and share best practices for the promotion of electronic authentication methods, including electronic signatures; - Identify barriers and encourage best practice sharing in border management, including but not limited to goods inspections processes at the border; - Coordinate with the UPU or NPO and other stakeholders involved in cross-border delivery and distribution to safeguard and improve the sustainability of cross-border e-commerce; - Raise awareness of cybercrimes and the need for strong, effective security in the use of ICTs for cross-border e-commerce; - Maintain implementation of emerging information communication technologies and industries ensuring interoperability in the sphere of cross-border e-commerce in the region; - Promote better measurement of cross-border e-commerce and analysis on its economic impacts, including measurements examining negative impacts of relevant protectionist measures and anti-competition practices; - Modernize the TOR of ECSG by focusing on e-commerce and capturing emerging issues; - Continue close collaboration with other working groups and APEC fora, including but not limited to the Sub Committee on Customs Procedures (SCCP), Small and Medium Enterprises Working Group (SMEWG), Telecommunication Working Group (TELWG), CTI, and Steering Committee on Economic and Technical Cooperation (SCE) etc.
impact: 引言 5. 今天，全球经济的快速数字化为 APEC 中小微企业开辟了新的增长机会。跨境电子商务是 APEC 中小微企业国际化的有力推动因素，使其无需实体商业存在即可向世界营销和销售其产品。认识到这一点，2014 年 APEC 领导人通过了《APEC 跨境电子商务创新与发展倡议》。在 2015 年 APEC 部长级会议上，部长们欢迎了“促进电子商务以推动中小微企业全球化”的提议。2016 年，部长们同意鼓励进一步开展工作，交流关于实施《WTO 贸易便利化协定》以及促进对跨境电子商务进行海关监管的经验，以实现更好的互联互通、进一步的区域经济一体化以及中小微企业现代化。这些指示需要 APEC 经济体作出回应。 6. 注意到这一关键领域已经形成的基础和工作流，并认识到捕捉与 APEC 及当今全球贸易环境相关问题的重要性，APEC 于 2017 年建议建立一个框架，以指导全面且协调一致的应对。
impactEn: Introduction 5. Today, the rapid digitalization of the global economy has opened up new growth opportunities for APEC’s Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs). Cross-border e-commerce is a powerful enabler for the internationalization of APEC’s MSMEs, who no longer need physical, commercial presence to market and sell their products to the world. Recognizing this, in 2014 APEC Leaders endorsed the APEC Cross-border E-commerce Innovation and Development Initiative. At the APEC Ministerial Meeting (AMM) in 2015, Ministers welcomed the proposal to Promote E-commerce to Globalize MSMEs. And in 2016, Ministers agreed to encourage further work to exchange experience on the implementation of the WTO Agreement on Trade Facilitation and promotion of customs control over cross-border e-commerce for better connectivity, further integration of regional economy and modernize MSMEs. These are instructions that need a response from the APEC Economies. 6. Noting the foundation and work streams that have begun in this critical area, and recognizing the importance of capturing issues relevant to APEC and today’s global trading environment, in 2017 APEC recommends establishment of a framework to guide a comprehensive and coherent response.

en: Guidebook on APEC Privacy and Trustmark
cn: APEC 隐私与信任标志指南
summary: 1. APEC 各经济体认识到，在亚太地区各经济体之间及其贸易伙伴之间保护信息隐私和维持信息流动的重要性。正如 APEC 部长们在通过 1998 年《电子商务行动蓝图》时所承认的，如果没有政府和企业合作“开发并实施能够在安全、可靠的通信、信息和交付系统中建立信任和信心，并处理包括隐私在内的问题的技术和政策”，电子商务的潜力就无法实现。消费者对在线交易和信息网络的隐私与安全缺乏信任和信心，是可能阻碍成员经济体获得电子商务全部利益的因素之一。APEC 各经济体认识到，提高消费者信心并确保电子商务增长的关键工作之一，必须是在亚太地区通过合作平衡并促进有效的信息隐私保护和信息自由流动。 3. 随着技术和信息流动性质的变化，商业运营和消费者预期持续转变，企业和其他组织需要全天候同步输入和访问数据，以满足客户和社会需求，并提供高效且具有成本效益的服务。不必要地限制这种流动或给其施加负担的监管体系，会对全球商业和经济产生不利影响。因此，在促进和执行合乎伦理的信息实践时，也有必要建立能够适应全球环境中新现实的信息隐私保护体系。 8. 最后，制定本信息隐私保护框架，是基于对以下重要性的认识： - 为个人信息制定适当的隐私保护，特别是防止不必要侵扰和个人信息滥用造成的有害后果； - 认识到信息自由流动对于发达和发展中市场经济体维持经济和社会增长均至关重要； - 使在 APEC 成员经济体中收集、访问、使用或处理数据的全球性组织，能够在其组织内部制定和实施统一方法，以实现对个人信息的全球访问和使用； - 使执法机构能够履行保护信息隐私的职责；以及 - 推进国际机制，以促进和执行信息隐私保护，并维持 APEC 各经济体之间及其贸易伙伴之间信息流动的连续性。 第二部分：范围 12. 鉴于各成员经济体在社会、文化、经济和法律背景方面存在差异，在实施这些原则时应保持灵活性。 对于电子商务而言，APEC 内部所有法律和实践在所有方面完全一致并非必要，包括个人信息覆盖范围在内；但是，APEC 各经济体之间在信息隐私保护方面采取兼容的方法，将极大便利国际商务。这些原则承认这一事实，同时也考虑到各经济体之间的社会、文化和其他差异。它们重点关注对国际商务最为重要的隐私保护方面。 第四部分：实施 29. 认识到各经济体有意最大化其公民和企业可获得的经济和社会利益，个人信息的收集、持有、处理、使用、转移和披露，应当以保护个人信息隐私并使其能够实现境内和跨境信息流动利益的方式进行。 30. 因此，作为建立或审查其隐私保护的一部分，各成员经济体应在符合《APEC 隐私框架》和任何现有国内隐私保护的情况下，采取一切合理和适当步骤，识别并消除对信息流动的不必要障碍，并避免造成任何此类障碍。 32. 如第 31 段所述，落实本框架的方式可能因成员经济体而异，个别经济体可以决定不同的 APEC 隐私原则需要不同的实施方式。在特定情况下无论采取何种方法，总体目标都应是在尊重各经济体自身要求的基础上，发展 APEC 区域内隐私保护方法的兼容性。 二、调查与执法中的跨境合作 43. 各成员经济体应指定并向其他成员经济体公布其本辖区内负责促进与隐私保护有关的跨境合作和经济体间信息共享的公共机构。 44. 建立合作安排：在考虑现有国际安排以及现有或正在发展的自律方法的基础上，并在国内法律和政策允许的范围内，成员经济体应考虑制定合作安排和程序，以促进隐私法执法中的跨境合作。此类合作安排可以采取双边或多边安排的形式。本段应结合成员经济体的权利来理解，即成员经济体可以基于以下理由拒绝或限制对特定调查或事项的合作：遵守合作请求将不符合国内法律、政策或优先事项；资源限制；或有关调查缺乏共同利益。 45. 在隐私法的民事执法中，跨境合作安排可以包括以下方面： a）建立机制，迅速、系统和高效地通知其他成员经济体指定公共机构有关调查或隐私执法案件，这些调查或案件针对的是在这些经济体中造成违法行为或对个人造成损害的行为； b）建立机制，有效共享成功开展跨境隐私调查和执法合作所需的信息； c）建立隐私执法案件中的调查协助机制； d）建立机制，根据个人信息隐私违法侵害的严重程度、实际或潜在损害以及其他相关考虑因素，确定与其他经济体公共机构合作案件的优先顺序； e）采取措施，对合作安排下交换的信息维持适当程度的保密。 三、跨境隐私规则的合作发展 46. 各成员经济体将努力支持在 APEC 区域内发展、认可或接受组织的跨境隐私规则，同时认识到组织仍有责任遵守当地数据保护要求以及所有适用法律。此类跨境隐私规则应遵守 APEC 隐私原则。 47. 为使此类跨境隐私规则生效，各成员经济体将努力与适当的利益攸关方合作，在各经济体之间制定相互认可或接受此类跨境隐私规则的框架或机制。 48. 各成员经济体应努力确保此类跨境隐私规则以及认可或接受机制能够促进负责任和可问责的跨境数据转移及有效隐私保护，同时不对跨境信息流动造成不必要障碍，包括不给企业和消费者造成不必要的行政和官僚负担。 APEC 跨境隐私规则体系 CBPR 体系的发展 1. APEC 通过推动一项政策框架，在亚太地区发挥关键作用，该框架旨在确保个人信息跨境持续自由流动，同时为个人信息的隐私和安全建立有意义的保护。 2. 2004 年 11 月，21 个 APEC 经济体的部长通过了《APEC 隐私框架》。该框架由九项指导原则和实施指南组成，旨在协助 APEC 各经济体制定一致的国内个人信息隐私保护方法。它也构成了发展区域性方法的基础，以促进 APEC 各经济体之间负责任和可问责的个人信息转移。 6. 在制定 APEC 数据隐私路径时，识别出以下利益攸关方考量： - 组织应当信任并有信心认为，与其进行涉及个人信息交易的组织已经建立适当政策和程序，这些政策和程序符合 APEC 原则，并尊重适用的隐私和数据安全法律，以及在收集个人信息时向个人作出的隐私和安全说明； - 消费者应当信任并有信心认为，其个人信息在跨境传输过程中受到传输和安全保护；以及 - 政府应确保不存在对跨境数据转移的不合理障碍，同时在国内保护其公民个人信息的隐私和安全，并通过与外国政府合作在国际层面进行保护。 CBPR 体系与国内法律法规 43. CBPR 体系不取代或改变某一经济体的国内法律法规。如果某一经济体没有适用的国内隐私保护要求，CBPR 体系旨在提供最低水平的保护。 44. 参与 CBPR 体系并不取代参与组织的国内法律义务。组织为参与 CBPR 体系而作出的承诺，与可能适用的任何国内法律要求相互独立。凡国内法律要求高于 CBPR 体系预期要求的，相关国内法律法规的全部范围将继续适用。凡 CBPR 体系要求高于国内法律法规要求的，组织需要自愿履行此类额外要求以参与该体系。尽管如此，该经济体的隐私执法机关应有能力依据适用的国内法律法规采取执法行动，以产生按照 CBPR 项目要求保护个人信息的效果。
summaryEn: APEC privacy and trustmark 1. APEC economies recognize the importance of protecting information privacy and maintaining information flows among economies in the Asia Pacific region and among their trading partners. As APEC Ministers acknowledged in endorsing the 1998 Blueprint for Action on Electronic Commerce, the potential of electronic commerce cannot be realized without government and business cooperation “to develop and implement technologies and policies, which build trust and confidence in safe, secure and reliable communication, information and delivery systems, and which address issues including privacy...”. The lack of consumer trust and confidence in the privacy and security of online transactions and information networks is one element that may prevent member economies from gaining all of the benefits of electronic commerce. APEC economies realize that a key part of efforts to improve consumer confidence and ensure the growth of electronic commerce must be cooperation to balance and promote both effective information privacy protection and the free flow of information in the Asia Pacific region. 3. As both business operations and consumer expectations continue to shift due to changes in technology and the nature of information flows, businesses and other organizations require simultaneous input and access to data 24-hours a day in order to meet customer and societal needs, and to provide efficient and cost-effective services. Regulatory systems that unnecessarily restrict this flow or place burdens on it have adverse implications for global business and economies. Therefore, in promoting and enforcing ethical information practices, there is also a need to develop systems for protecting information privacy that account for these new realities in the global environment. 8. Finally, this Framework on information privacy protection was developed in recognition of the importance of: - Developing appropriate privacy protections for personal information, particularly from the harmful consequences of unwanted intrusions and the misuse of personal information; - Recognizing the free flow of information as being essential for both developed and developing market economies to sustain economic and social growth; - Enabling global organizations that collect, access, use or process data in APEC member economies to develop and implement uniform approaches within their organizations for global access to and use of personal information; - Enabling enforcement agencies to fulfill their mandate to protect information privacy; and, - Advancing international mechanisms to promote and enforce information privacy and to maintain the continuity of information flows among APEC economies and with their trading partners. Part II. Scope 12. In view of the differences in social, cultural, economic and legal backgrounds of each member economy, there should be flexibility in implementing these Principles. Although it is not essential for electronic commerce that all laws and practices within APEC be identical in all respects, including the coverage of personal information, compatible approaches to information privacy protection among APEC economies will greatly facilitate international commerce. These Principles recognize that fact, but also take into account social, cultural and other differences among economies. They focus on those aspects of privacy protection that are of the most importance to international commerce. Part IV. Implementation 29. Recognizing the interests of economies in maximizing the economic and social benefits available to their citizens and businesses, personal information should be collected, held, processed, used, transferred, and disclosed in a manner that protects individual information privacy and allows them to realize the benefits of information flows within and across borders. 30. Consequently, as part of establishing or reviewing their privacy protections, Member Economies, consistent with the APEC Privacy Framework and any existing domestic privacy protections, should take all reasonable and appropriate steps to identify and remove unnecessary barriers to information flows and avoid the creation of any such barriers. 32. As set forth in Paragraph 31, the means of giving effect to the Framework may differ between Member Economies, and it may be appropriate for individual economies to determine that different APEC Privacy Principles may call for different means of implementation. Whatever approach is adopted in a particular circumstance, the overall goal should be to develop compatibility of approaches in privacy protections in the APEC region that is respectful of requirements of individual economies. II Cross-border Cooperation in Investigation and Enforcement 43. Member Economies should designate and make known to the other Member Economies the public authorities within their own jurisdictions that will be responsible for facilitating cross-border cooperation and information sharing between economies in connection with privacy protection. 44. Developing cooperative arrangements: Taking into consideration existing international arrangements and existing or developing self-regulatory approaches (including those referenced in Part B. III., below), and to the extent permitted by domestic law and policy, Member Economies should consider developing cooperative arrangements and procedures to facilitate cross-border cooperation in the enforcement of privacy laws. Such cooperative arrangements may take the form of bilateral or multilateral arrangements. This paragraph is to be construed with regard to the right of Member Economies to decline or limit cooperation on particular investigations or matters on the ground that compliance with a request for cooperation would be inconsistent with domestic laws, policies or priorities, or on the ground of resource constraints, or based on the absence of a mutual interest in the investigations in question. 45. In civil enforcement of privacy laws, cooperative cross-border arrangements may include the following aspects: a) mechanisms for promptly, systematically and efficiently notifying designated public authorities in other Member Economies of investigations or privacy enforcement cases that target unlawful conduct or the resulting harm to individuals in those economies; b) mechanisms for effectively sharing information necessary for successful cooperation in cross-border privacy investigation and enforcement cases; c) mechanisms for investigative assistance in privacy enforcement cases; d) mechanisms to prioritize cases for cooperation with public authorities in other economies based on the severity of the unlawful infringements of personal information privacy, the actual or potential harm involved, as well as other relevant considerations; e) steps to maintain the appropriate level of confidentiality in respect of information exchanged under the cooperative arrangements. III. Cooperative Development of Cross-border Privacy Rules 46. Member Economies will endeavor to support the development and recognition or acceptance of organizations’ cross-border privacy rules across the APEC region, recognizing that organizations would still be responsible for complying with the local data protection requirements, as well as with all applicable laws. Such cross-border privacy rules should adhere to the APEC Privacy Principles. 47. To give effect to such cross-border privacy rules, Member Economies will endeavor to work with appropriate stakeholders to develop frameworks or mechanisms for the mutual recognition or acceptance of such cross-border privacy rules between and among the economies. 48. Member Economies should endeavor to ensure that such cross-border privacy rules and recognition or acceptance mechanisms facilitate responsible and accountable cross-border data transfers and effective privacy protections without creating unnecessary barriers to cross-border information flows, including unnecessary administrative and bureaucratic burdens for businesses and consumers. APEC CROSS-Border Privacy Rules System POLICIES, RULES AND GUIDELINES The purpose of this document is to describe the APEC Cross Border Privacy Rules (CBPR) System, its core elements, governance structure and the roles and responsibilities of participating organizations, Accountability Agents and Economies. This document is to be read consistently with the APEC Privacy Framework. Nothing in this document is intended to create binding international obligations, affect existing obligations under international or domestic law, or create obligations under the laws and regulations of APEC Economies. DEVELOPMENT OF THE CBPR SYSTEM 1. APEC plays a critical role in the Asia Pacific region by promoting a policy framework designed to ensure the continued free flow of personal information across borders while establishing meaningful protection for the privacy and security of personal information. 2. In November 2004, Ministers for the twenty-one APEC Economies endorsed the APEC Privacy Framework. The Framework is comprised of a set of nine guiding principles and guidance on implementation to assist APEC Economies in developing consistent domestic approaches to personal information privacy protections. It also forms the basis for the development of a regional approach to promote accountable and responsible transfers of personal information between APEC Economies. 6. In the development of the APEC Data Privacy Pathfinder, the following stakeholder considerations were identified: - organizations should have trust and confidence that organizations with which they enter into transactions that involve personal information have appropriate policies and procedures in place that are consistent with the APEC principles and respect applicable privacy and data security laws, as well as the privacy and security representations made to the individual when the personal information was collected; - consumers should have trust and confidence that their personal information is transmitted and secured across borders; and - governments should ensure that there are no unreasonable impediments to cross-border data transfers while at the same time protecting the privacy and security of their citizens’ personal information domestically and, in cooperation with foreign governments, internationally. THE CBPR SYSTEM AND DOMESTIC LAWS AND REGULATIONS 43. The CBPR System does not displace or change an Economy’s domestic laws and regulations. Where there are no applicable domestic privacy protection requirements in an Economy, the CBPR System is intended to provide a minimum level of protection. 44. Participation in the CBPR System does not replace a participating organization’s domestic legal obligations. The commitments which an organization carries out in order to participate in the CBPR System are separate from any domestic legal requirements that may be applicable. Where domestic legal requirements exceed what is expected in the CBPR System, the full extent of such domestic law and regulation will continue to apply. Where requirements of the CBPR System exceed the requirements of domestic law and regulation, an organization will need to voluntarily carry out such additional requirements in order to participate. Nonetheless, Privacy Enforcement Authorities in that Economy should have the ability to take enforcement actions under applicable domestic laws and regulations that have the effect of protecting personal information consistent with the CBPR program requirements.
impact: APEC经济体认可基于原则的APEC隐私框架，视其为推动制定适当信息隐私保护和确保亚太地区信息自由流通的重要工具。 该框架旨在为APEC经济体的企业提供明确的指导和方向，了解常见的隐私问题及其对合法企业运营方式的影响。它通过强调现代消费者合理的期望，即企业将以符合本框架原则的方式认可其隐私权益。
impactEn: APEC economies endorse the principles-based APEC Privacy Framework as an important tool in encouraging the development of appropriate information privacy protections and ensuring the free flow of information in the Asia Pacific region. The Framework is intended to provide clear guidance and direction to businesses in APEC economies on common privacy issues and the impact of privacy issues upon the way legitimate businesses are conducted. It does so by highlighting the reasonable expectations of the modern consumer that businesses will recognize their privacy interests in a way that is consistent with the Principles outlined in this Framework.

en: Global Cross-Border Privacy Rules (CBPR) Framework (2023)
cn: 全球跨境隐私规则框架（2023年）
summary: 第一部分 序言 认识到日益增长的互联网连接和全球经济数字化导致跨境收集、使用和传输数据快速增加，且这一趋势持续加速； 意识到可信的跨境数据流动不可或缺——不仅对大型跨国技术公司如此，对经济各行业的企业以及微型、小型和中型企业、劳动者和消费者同样如此； 承认监管壁垒在企业日益依赖数字技术和创新以维持业务运营和经济复苏之际，威胁着数字经济所创造的机遇； 承认亚太经济合作组织在开发亚太经济合作组织跨境隐私规则系统以促进跨境数据流动和互操作性方面所做的重要贡献； 1. 本框架基于《亚太经济合作组织隐私框架》，并与经济合作与发展组织《关于保护隐私和个人数据跨境流动的指南》的核心原则保持一致。 2. 本框架专门阐述保护个人信息和隐私同时维持信息流动的重要性。其实用且独特的方法是关注一致而非完全相同的数据保护和隐私方式。 15. 全球跨境隐私规则隐私原则的例外情况，包括与国家主权、国家安全、公共安全和公共政策相关的例外，应当： a) 有限且与实现相关例外所涉目标相称；以及 b) (i) 向公众公开；或 (ii) 依法进行。 29. 个人信息控制者应负责遵守使上述原则生效的措施。当个人信息将被传输给另一个人或组织时，无论是在国内还是国际，个人信息控制者应获得个人的同意或进行尽职调查并采取合理步骤，确保接收方个人或组织将按照这些原则保护信息。 32. 个人信息的收集、持有、处理、使用、传输和披露方式应当(a)保护个人的数据和隐私，(b)允许个人和各成员最大化跨境数据流动的益处。 33. 因此，作为建立或审查其数据保护和隐私方法以落实全球跨境隐私规则框架的一部分，各成员应采取一切合理和适当的步骤，识别并消除信息流动的不必要壁垒，并避免创建此类壁垒。 36. 各成员在使框架原则生效和保护个人免受该成员管辖范围内发生的数据保护和隐私违规行为方面，应采取非歧视性做法。例如，各成员应确保使框架中的保护生效的法律或其他方法不会妨碍居住在其他司法管辖区的个人从这些保护中受益。 62. 各成员认识到在维持跨境个人信息自由流动的同时保护个人信息和隐私的重要性，并鼓励实施本框架以提供信息可以安全、负责任地流动的条件，例如通过使用全球跨境隐私规则和隐私处理者认可系统。 63. 各成员应努力支持跨境数据传输和隐私机制的发展和认可或接受，供组织在全球范围内传输个人信息使用，同时认识到组织仍有责任遵守当地数据保护和隐私要求以及所有适用法律。此类机制应与全球跨境隐私规则隐私原则保持一致。 64. 为落实第62段，各成员参与全球跨境隐私规则系统，该系统提供了在国际跨境背景下实施全球跨境隐私规则框架的实用机制，并为组织提供了一种跨境传输个人信息的方式，使个人可以信任其个人信息隐私得到保护。 66. 当(a)另一成员已实施使本框架生效的立法或监管文书，或(b)存在充分的保障措施，包括有效的执法机制和由个人信息控制者采取的适当措施（如全球跨境隐私规则系统），以确保持续的保护水平与本框架及实施框架的法律或政策一致时，一成员应避免限制其与另一成员之间的跨境个人信息流动。 67. 对跨境个人信息流动的任何限制应与传输所呈现的风险相称，同时考虑信息的敏感性以及跨境传输的目的和背景。 68. 各成员应促进全球跨境隐私规则系统和隐私处理者认可系统与其他使本框架实际生效的数据保护和隐私框架的互操作性。 69. 提高数据保护和隐私框架的全球互操作性可以带来改善个人信息流动的益处，有助于确保在个人信息流向各成员之外时维持数据保护和隐私要求，并简化个人信息控制者和处理者的合规工作。全球互操作性还可以帮助个人在全球环境中主张其个人信息和隐私权，并帮助当局改善跨境隐私执法。
summaryEn: Part I. Preamble Recognising that growing Internet connectivity and the digitisation of the global economy have resulted in the rapid increase in the collection, use, and transfer of data across borders, a trend that continues to accelerate; Conscious that trusted cross-border data flows are indispensable – not just for big, multinational technology companies, but for companies across all sectors of the economy, and for micro, small- and medium-sized businesses, workers, and consumers as well; Acknowledging that regulatory barriers threaten to undermine opportunities created by the digital economy at a time when companies are relying increasingly on digital technologies and innovations to continue business operations and recover economically; Acknowledging the important contribution made by the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) in developing the APEC CBPR System to foster cross-border data flows and interoperability; 1. This Framework is based on the APEC Privacy Framework and is consistent with the core principles of the OECD's Guidelines on the Protection of Privacy and Trans-Border Flows of Personal Data (OECD Guidelines). 2. The Framework specifically addresses the importance of protecting personal information and privacy while maintaining information flows. Its practical and distinctive approach is to focus attention on consistent rather than identical approaches to data protection and privacy. 15. Exceptions to the Global CBPR Privacy Principles, including those relating to national sovereignty, national security, public safety and public policy, should be: a) limited and proportional to meeting the objectives to which the exceptions relate; and b) (i) made known to the public; or (ii) in accordance with law. 29. A personal information controller should be accountable for complying with measures that give effect to the Principles stated above. When personal information is to be transferred to another person or organization, whether domestically or internationally, the personal information controller should obtain the consent of the individual or exercise due diligence and take reasonable steps to ensure that the recipient person or organization will protect the information consistently with these Principles. 32. Personal information should be collected, held, processed, used, transferred, and disclosed in a manner that (a) protects individuals' data and privacy, and (b) allows individuals and Members to maximize the benefits of data flows within and across borders. 33. Consequently, as part of establishing or reviewing their data protection and privacy approaches to give effect to the Global CBPR Framework, Members should take all reasonable and appropriate steps to identify and remove unnecessary barriers to information flows and avoid the creation of any such barriers. 36. Members should adopt non-discriminatory practices in giving effect to the Framework's principles and in protecting individuals from data protection and privacy violations occurring in that Member's jurisdiction. For example, Members should ensure that laws or other approaches that give effect to the protections in the Framework do not impede individuals living in other jurisdictions from benefitting from those protections. 62. Members recognize the importance of protecting personal information and privacy while maintaining the free flow of personal information across borders and encourage the implementation the Framework to provide conditions in which information can flow safely and accountably, for instance through the use of the Global CBPR and PRP Systems. 63. Members should endeavor to support the development and recognition or acceptance of cross-border data transfer and privacy mechanisms for use by organizations to transfer personal information globally, recognizing that organizations would still be responsible for complying with the local data protection and privacy requirements, as well as with all applicable laws. Such mechanisms should be consistent with the Global CBPR Privacy Principles. 64. To give effect to paragraph 62, Members participate in the Global CBPR System, which provides a practical mechanism to implement the Global CBPR Framework in an international, cross-border context, and to provide a means for organizations to transfer personal information across borders in a manner in which individuals may trust that the privacy of their personal information is protected. 66. A Member should refrain from restricting cross border flows of personal information between itself and another Member where (a) the other Member has in place legislative or regulatory instruments that give effect to the Framework or (b) sufficient safeguards exist, including effective enforcement mechanisms and appropriate measures (such as the Global CBPR System) put in place by the personal information controller to ensure a continuing level of protection consistent with the Framework and the laws or policies that implement it. 67. Any restrictions to cross-border flows of personal information should be proportionate to the risks presented by the transfer, taking into account the sensitivity of the information, and the purpose and context of the cross-border transfer. 68. Members should promote interoperability of the Global CBPR System and PRP System with other data protection and privacy frameworks that give practical effect to this Framework. 69. Improving the global interoperability of data protection and privacy frameworks can bring benefits in improved personal information flows, help ensure that data protection and privacy requirements are maintained when personal information flows beyond Members and can simplify compliance for personal information controllers and processors. Global interoperability can also assist individuals to assert their personal information and privacy rights in a global environment and help authorities to improve cross-border privacy enforcement.

en: APEC Survey on E-Commerce Regulations
cn: APEC 电子商务监管调查
summary: 该调查由APEC经济体自愿提交并每年更新，按经济体分别列示与电子商务相关的多个国家（19国）国内法律法规、监管措施和政策。文件100多页，不逐条摘抄各经济体内容；如需查阅某一经济体具体规则，可直接访问右侧网址，在PDF中定位对应经济体章节。
impact: 透明度是推动电子商务的关键。在《APEC跨境电子商务便利化框架（2017）》的第一支柱中，各经济体同意“推动透明且可预测的法律和监管方法及措施，这些措施应对企业友好且一致，以便利跨境电子商务。”《APEC互联网与数字经济路线图（2017）》也把“便利电子商务和推动数字贸易合作”列为其重点关注领域之一。在这一领域下，各经济体被要求“制定和推广旨在有效发展电子商务的措施和政策，包括通过可预测、透明且一致的政策和监管环境”。
impactEn: Transparency is key to promoting E-Commerce. In Pillar One of the APEC Cross-border E-Commerce Facilitation Framework (2017), economies agreed to “promote transparent and predictable legal and regulatory approaches and measures that are business friendly and coherent to facilitate cross-border ecommerce.” The APEC Internet and Digital Economy Roadmap (2017) also identified the “Facilitation of E-commerce and Advancing Cooperation on Digital Trade” as one of its key areas of focus. Under this area, economies were asked to “elaborate and promote measures and policies aimed at effective development of e-commerce including through policy and regulatory environments that are predictable, transparent and consistent”.

en: Regulations, Policies and Initiatives on E-Commerce and Digital Economy for APEC MSMEs' Participation in the Region
cn: APEC中小微企业参与区域电子商务和数字经济的监管、政策与倡议
summary: 第三章：电子商务及数字经济相关贸易的政策与举措 1. 电子交易与电子签名立法 电子交易法通常被定义为通过承认电子通信、电子记录和电子签名的法律确定性，促进电子商务发展的法律。 在开展包括电子支付在内的在线商业交易时，企业需要遵守书面形式与电子形式交换之间的法律等同性。 相关立法以UNCITRAL 1996年《电子商务示范法》和2001年《电子签名示范法》为基础。 2. 电子交易立法的基本原则 电子交易不歧视，即不得仅因通信采用电子形式而否认其有效性。 技术中立，即符合一定条件的电子通信应与传统纸质通信具有相同功能和法律权利。 功能等同，即平等对待不同技术方式，包括电子邮件、互联网、即时通信、传真等。 3. 电子商务消费者保护立法 消费者保护在维护企业与消费者之间的信任和关系方面发挥重要作用。 消费者保护立法旨在确保消费者免受误导性、欺诈性和不公平商业行为的侵害。 线上买卖双方之间的信任，是电子商务和相关数字贸易发展的关键因素。 有效的消费者保护立法有助于促进消费者信任，并提升消费者以安全、知情方式更多参与跨境电子商务交易的能力。 4. APEC隐私、数据保护和网络犯罪立法 近年来，随着全球线上消费者数量增加，产生了若干与隐私和网络安全有关的问题。 提高处理隐私和网络安全相关问题的能力，已经成为全球政府以及APEC经济体政府需要开展的一项重要工作。 APEC领导人努力加强APEC在提升基础设施保护，包括电信基础设施保护方面的活动。 APEC还鼓励成员考虑《网络犯罪公约》，并制定一整套与网络安全和网络犯罪有关的法律，使其与国际法律文书保持一致。 5. APEC争议解决机制 争议解决与前文所讨论的消费者保护密切相关。 参与跨境贸易的小企业缺乏有效的争议解决机制。 APEC中小微企业需要一种能够促进无缝贸易的法律环境，而争议解决是其中重要组成部分。 在线争议解决机制已经在其他场景中取得成功。 第五章：未来方向 1. 更新数字经济国内立法 虽然APEC成员的电子商务立法已经得到更多更新和整合，但数字经济立法在未来仍应得到更多关注。 新的数字技术创造了现有立法尚未规制的新平台。 APEC成员需要迅速回应新的事实和趋势，以最大化数字经济带来的收益。 适当的政策将成为政府促进数字经济发展的有效解决方案。 2. 提高消费者和企业认知 还需要提高消费者和企业的认知，帮助受益者和利益相关方理解相关政策和法规。 政府、主管机关和相关组织应加快能力建设项目，以教育和培训所有利益相关方了解电子商务和数字经济方面的新政策或新法规。 政府和主管机关还应开展政策宣传，并提供指引，鼓励消费者和企业确保互联网交易安全。 3. 促进不同立法之间的协调性和互操作性 APEC成员在法律采纳方面已经取得许多进展，这也形成了区域内电子商务立法多样化的局面。 有必要在区域内建立协调且可互操作的立法环境，以弥合数字鸿沟，并促进相关领域国内法律法规的发展。 APEC成员可以考虑推动国际标准、电子签名互认、电子合同互认，尤其是跨境数据隐私方面的规则协调。 APEC跨境隐私规则体系，即CBPR体系，可以被视为一种有助于促进区域数据保护、并可进一步完善的机制。 4. 国内法与国际标准对接 APEC经济体应使国内法律与国际标准保持一致，例如OECD指南和联合国消费者保护指南，这些文件是主要的国际参考框架。 对于仍缺乏电子商务立法、无法提供适当线上法律保护的经济体，应尽快采纳所需的法律工具，以支持电子商务发展，并增强企业和消费者对线上交易的信任。 5. 加强国际合作的必要性 推动跨境电子商务并迈向数字经济，需要APEC成员之间以及各经济体执法机关之间开展强有力且有效的合作。 国际合作框架也为APEC成员在发展电子商务和数字经济过程中应对跨境问题提供准备平台。 各经济体应考虑加入APEC在线争议解决框架，并鼓励其企业充分使用该框架。 APEC成员之间应加强能力建设，使更多经济体能够制定和修改其国内立法。
summaryEn: Chapter 3: Policies and Initiatives for E-Commerce and Trade Relating Digital Economy 1. Electronic Transaction and Electronic Signature Legislation > Electronic transactions law is often defined as laws that facilitate e-commerce by providing legal certainty for the recognition of electronic communications, electronic records and electronic signatures. > While conducting commercial transactions online, including e-payment, enterprises need to obey and follow the legal equivalence between written and electronic form of exchange. > The legislation is based on the UNCITRAL 1996 Model Law on Electronic Commerce and 2001 Model Law on Electronic Signatures. 2. Fundamental Principles of E-Transaction Legislation > Non-discrimination among E-transactions, meaning that a communication shall not be denied the validity in term of the electronic form on the sole ground. > Technology neutrality, allowing electronic communications that have met certain criteria to have the same function and legal right as the traditional paper-based ones. > Functional equivalence, where equal treatment of different technologies, means (e-mail, Internet, instant messaging, fax, etc.). 3. Consumer Protection Legislation in E-commerce > Consumer protection plays an important role on maintaining trust, and relationship between businesses and consumers. > Consumer protection legislations aim to ensure adequate protection for consumers from misleading, fraudulent and unfair commercial conduct. > Matter of trust between online buyers and sellers is a vital factor for the development of e-commerce and relating digital trade. > An effective consumer protection legislation could help to promote consumer trust as well as to enhance consumers’ capacities to engage more in cross-border e-commerce transactions in safe and informed manner. 4. Privacy, Data Protection and Cyber-crime Legislation in APEC > With the increased number of online consumers around the globe recently, it leads to several issues related to privacy and cybersecurity. > Enhancing the capacity to deal with privacy and cybersecurity related problems is now one of the most important jobs that government around the world as a whole and in APEC economies in particularly need to conduct. > APEC leaders have tried to strengthen APEC activities in the field of upgrading infrastructure protection, including telecomunications. > APEC also encouraged its members to take into account the Convention on Cybercrime and enact a comprehensive set of laws relating to cybersecurity and cybercrime that are consistent with international legal instruments. 5. Review of Dispute Resolution in APEC > Dispute resolution is also very much related to the consumer protection discussed in the previous section. > Small businesses engaged in cross-border trade have no effective resolution mechanism. > APEC MSMEs are in the need of a legal environment that enhance a seamless trade and dispute resolution is an essential part of this. > Online Dispute Resolution (ODR) is already successful in other context. Chapter 5: Way Forwards 1. Update Domestic Legislations for Digital Economy > While e-commerce legislation has been more updated and consolidated among APEC members, it is well recognized that digital economy legislation should be more focused in coming time. > New digital technologies have been created new platforms that are not regulated in the present legislation. > APEC members should have quick responses to the new facts and trends with the aim of maximizing benefits of digital economy. > Appropriate policies will be served as a good solution for Government to facilitate digital economy. 2. Raise Consumer’s and Business’s Awareness > Enhancing awareness of consumers and companies is also needed to support beneficiaries and stakeholders to understand about policies and regulations. > Capabilities building programs should be accelerated by Government, authorities and relevant organizations in order to educate and train all stakeholders about new policies or regulations on e-commerce and digital economy. > Government and authorities should embark raising awareness about policies as well as providing guidelines to encourage consumers and business to ensure safe transaction on Internet. 3. Promote Coherency and Interoperability among Different Legislations > APEC members have been made a lot of progress in adoption of laws as mentioned in the previous chapters, which have been creating a diverse picture of e-commerce legislation in the region. > It is necessary to create a coherent and interoperable legislation environment in the region to bridge the digital divide as well as facilitate domestic laws and regulations on relating issues. > APEC members can consider to promote international standards, mutual recognition of e-signatures, electronic contracts and particularly cross-border data privacy. > APEC Cross-Border Data Privacy Rules (CBPR) system can be referred as a helpful mechanism to be further improved to facilitate data protection in the region. 4. Align Domestic Laws with International Standards > APEC economies should align domestic laws with international standards such as OECD guidelines and UN guidelines on Consumer Protection which serve as main international reference framework. > Economies still lacking the e-commerce legislation to provide appropriate online legal protection should soon adopt those required legislative instruments to support ecommerce and enhance trust in online transactions among business and consumers. 5. The Need for a Greater International Collaboration > Promoting cross-border e-commerce, towards digital economy, requires a strong and effective cooperation among APEC members and between each economy’s enforcement authorities. > International cooperation framework is also a place for APEC members to prepare at best to cope with cross border issues while developing e-commerce and digital economy. > Economies should consider opting into the APEC ODR Framework and encourage their enterprises to make good use of the APEC ODR Framework. > Capacity building efforts among the APEC members should be strengthened so that more economies are able to develop and modify their domestic legislation.
impact: 本报告旨在提供关于发展电子商务及贸易相关数字经济的政策、举措和最佳实践信息。报告基于广泛的案头研究，并采访了发达经济体的专家和政策制定者，以发掘成功政策，帮助并鼓励中小微企业通过电子商务及贸易相关数字经济参与区域市场。
impactEn: This report aims to provide information on policies, initiatives and best practices to develop the e-commerce and trade related digital economy. The report draws on wide ranging desk research and interview with experts and policymakers in developed economies to uncover successful policies to assist and encourage MSMEs to participate in the regional market via e-commerce and trade related digital economy.

en: APEC Internet and Digital Economy Roadmap
cn: APEC互联网与数字经济路线图
summary: 引言 《APEC互联网与数字经济路线图》建立在此前倡议基础之上，是一个框架性文件，旨在为重点领域和行动提供指导，促进成员经济体之间的技术和政策交流，推动创新、包容和可持续增长，并弥合APEC区域内的数字鸿沟。 该路线图是一份动态文件，将为APEC各工作组提供潜在合作领域方面的指导，并为进一步促进APEC互联网与数字经济的发展和增长作出重要贡献。 1. 发展数字基础设施 基于互联网协议的网络构成互联网与数字经济的基础；这不仅适用于互联网企业，也包括所有使用互联网或基于互联网协议网络的经济部门，并应考虑包括信息通信基础设施运营商在内的行业意见。 APEC鼓励所有成员经济体营造有利且竞争性的环境，并通过促进投资的政策发展数字基础设施，以支持互联网与数字经济。 2. 促进互操作性 APEC承认互操作性在互联网与数字经济中的关键重要性，因为所有经济和社会发展部门都越来越依赖底层数字基础设施。 通过开放互联的互联网以及互联网平台和应用之间的选择与竞争，数字技术有潜力使本地个人和企业获得更大的规模经济和范围经济。 3. 实现普遍宽带接入 如今，宽带接入已成为互联网与数字经济发展的根本基石，这意味着接入应是无处不在、可负担和普遍的。同时，接入质量与接入本身同等重要。 这意味着要确保速度、可用性、质量和可负担性达到基本水平。 4. 制定互联网与数字经济整体性政府政策框架 鉴于互联网与数字经济具有跨领域性质，政府政策框架应以整体方式制定，并纳入传统上不被视为"技术"部门的机构，例如农业和渔业、制造业、竞争、人力资源等部门。 APEC鼓励各经济体制定促进互联网与数字经济增长的政策，包括与公共和私营利益相关方协调并让其参与，使所有部门都有机会参与政策制定。 5. 促进影响互联网与数字经济的监管方法之间的协调与合作 大型企业和中小微企业共同面临的核心问题，是如何应对法律和程序上的不确定性，并确保遵守大量一般性和部门性法律法规、行为准则以及法律判决。 为加快互联网与数字经济发展，成员经济体应在监管方法方面促进相互理解并加强合作，包括国际标准和技术标准方面的合作，同时尊重各经济体符合其国内情况和国际法律义务的政策选择。 6. 促进创新以及使能技术和服务的采用 数字基础设施的发展，包括第四次工业革命，为监管者和企业带来了新机遇和新挑战，正在改变APEC中监管和商业合作的传统方式。 各经济体应利用使能数字技术和互联网，推动产品、服务、流程、组织和商业模式的创新。 各经济体还需要通过实施促进互联网与数字经济创新的政策框架，改善营商环境。 7. 增强信息通信技术使用中的信任和安全 虽然连接性是数字服务成功的关键，但隐私和安全同样是建立互联网与数字经济信任和信心的核心考虑因素。 APEC经济体认识到，需要为信息通信技术的使用建立可访问、开放、可互操作、可靠和安全的环境，这是经济增长和繁荣的重要基础。 公共部门、私营部门以及包括学术界在内的其他利益相关方，应共同努力增强信息通信技术使用中的信任和安全，同时充分利用现代数字系统带来的益处。 8. 在尊重适用国内法律法规的同时，促进信息和数据自由流动，以推动互联网与数字经济发展 在当今信息驱动型经济中，隐私和个人数据保护框架十分必要，因为这些框架对于增强数字经济中的信心和信任，同时保持互联网的全球性至关重要。 建立可互操作的系统可能有助于创新和创业增长。 APEC经济体将开展合作，推动一种监管方法，在提供适当、合法消费者保护的同时，促进信息和数据流动。 9. 改善互联网与数字经济基线测量 由于互联网与数字经济发展迅速，APEC成员经济体在测量和监测其发展方面面临挑战。 APEC鼓励各经济体在参考相关国际机构和利益相关方正在开展的改善互联网与数字经济测量工作的基础上，就互联网与数字经济形成共识并改善基线测量。 10. 增强互联网与数字经济的包容性 互联网与数字经济能够也应当促进更强的包容性，包括通过APEC区域内的能力建设，确保在社会和地理层面没有人被落下。 APEC经济体应推动政策措施和技术手段，以弥合经济体之间及其内部、区域之间和群体之间的数字鸿沟，同时推动普遍宽带接入。 应推动相关政策，支持中小微企业和个体创业者利用信息通信技术提高生产率、培育创新、提升竞争力，并应对进入新市场的挑战。 11. 促进电子商务便利化，并推进数字贸易合作 APEC承认成员经济体对电子商务和数字贸易采取不同的方法。 APEC鼓励各经济体制定并推动促进电子商务有效发展的措施和政策，包括建立可预见、透明和一致的政策与监管环境。 APEC将继续促进电子商务便利化，包括使用无纸化海关清关、电子交易文件、数字认证以及电子和在线支付等电子化方式。 随着商品和服务越来越多地以数字方式交易，数字贸易已成为全球贸易增长最快的领域之一，并有潜力为亚太地区增长和贸易提供重要推动力。 APEC鼓励各经济体探索数字贸易及相关问题领域潜在经济增长新领域的举措，包括识别基础构件并营造有利的数字生态系统。 实施 高级官员将对《APEC互联网与数字经济路线图》下的进展监测和评估承担总体责任，包括由相关论坛和次级论坛落实上述重点领域。 鉴于互联网与数字经济不断演变，高级官员将定期向部长报告进展，并寻求进一步指导。
summaryEn: INTRODUCTION The APEC Roadmap on Internet and Digital Economy builds on previous initiatives and is a framework that provides guidance on key areas and actions to facilitate technological and policy exchanges among member economies and to promote innovative, inclusive and sustainable growth, as well as to bridge digital divide in the APEC region. This Roadmap is a living document that will advise APEC working groups on potential areas of cooperation and an important contribution to further promote the development and growth of the Internet and Digital Economy in APEC. 1. Development of digital infrastructure IP-enabled networks form the foundation of the Internet and Digital Economy; not just for Internet-based companies, but inclusive of all sectors of the economy that make use of the Internet or IP-enabled networks, taking into account views from the industry, including ICT-infrastructure operators. All member economies are encouraged to promote an enabling and competitive environment with pro-investment policies for the development of digital infrastructure so as to support the Internet and Digital economy. 2. Promotion of Interoperability We acknowledge the key importance of interoperability in the Internet and Digital Economy, where all sectors of economic and social development are increasingly enabled by underlying digital infrastructure. Digital technologies have the potential to provide local individuals and businesses with access to greater economies of scale and scope, through an open interconnected Internet and choice and competition among Internet-based platforms and applications. 3. Achievement of universal broadband access Today, broadband access has become the fundamental building block for the development of the Internet and Digital economy, and this means ubiquitous, affordable and universal, access. It also means that quality of access is as important as access itself. This means ensuring basic levels of speed, availability, quality and affordability. 4. Development of holistic government policy frameworks for the Internet and Digital Economy Given the cross-cutting nature of the Internet and Digital Economy, government policy frameworks should be developed holistically including agencies that are not traditionally seen as 'tech' agencies such as agriculture and fisheries, manufacturing, competition, manpower, and so on. APEC economies are encouraged to pursue policies that promote the growth of the Internet and Digital Economy including, by coordinating with and involving public and private stakeholders so that all sectors have the opportunity to contribute to policy development. 5. Promoting coherence and cooperation of regulatory approaches affecting the Internet and Digital Economy A core problem facing both large enterprises and MSMEs is how to address legal and procedural uncertainties and to ensure compliance with an alphabet soup of general and sector-specific laws and regulations, as well as codes of practice and legal judgments. To accelerate the growth of the Internet and Digital Economy, member economies should promote mutual understanding and strengthen cooperation in approaches to regulation including international and technical standards, while respecting each economy's choice of policies which are consistent with domestic situations and international legal obligations. 6. Promoting innovation and adoption of enabling technologies and services The development of the digital infrastructure, including the Fourth Industrial Revolution opens new opportunities and brings new challenges for regulators and businesses, transforming traditional approaches to regulatory and business cooperation in APEC. Economies should take advantage of enabling digital technologies and the internet to promote innovation in products, services, processes, organizations and business models. Economies also need to improve the business environment through implementing policy frameworks that promote innovation in the Internet and Digital Economy. 7. Enhancing trust and security in the use of ICTs Whilst connectivity is key to the success of digital services, privacy and security are also a central consideration for building trust and confidence in the Internet and Digital economy. APEC economies recognize the need for an accessible, open, interoperable, reliable and secure environment for the use of ICTs as an essential foundation for economic growth and prosperity. Public and private sectors, and other stakeholders, including academia, should work together to enhance trust and security in the use of ICTs, while taking advantage of the benefits of modern digital systems. 8. Facilitating the free flow of information and data for the development of the Internet and Digital Economy, while respecting applicable domestic laws and regulations In today's information-driven economy, it is essential to have frameworks for privacy and personal data protection, as they are crucial to strengthening confidence and trust in the digital economy while preserving the global nature of the Internet. Creating interoperable systems may contribute to innovation and entrepreneurial growth. APEC economies will collaborate to promote a regulatory approach that provides appropriate legitimate consumer protection to enable the flow of information and data. 9. Improvement of baseline Internet and Digital Economy measurements It is a challenge for APEC member economies to measure and monitor the development of the Internet and Digital economy simply due to its fast growth. APEC economies are encouraged to develop common understandings and improved baseline measurements for the Internet and Digital Economy with reference to the ongoing work by the relevant international bodies and stakeholders to improve measurement of the Internet and Digital Economy. 10. Enhancing inclusiveness of Internet and Digital Economy The Internet and Digital Economy can and should contribute to better inclusiveness, including through capacity building in the APEC region to ensure that no one is left behind both in terms of social and geographic perspectives. APEC economies should promote policy measures and technical means to bridge the digital divides between and within economies, regions and groups, in addition to promoting universal broadband access. Policies should be promoted to support and globalize MSMEs and individual entrepreneurs to use ICTs to enhance productivity, nurture innovation, improve competitiveness, and to address challenges to access new markets. 11. Facilitation of E-commerce and Advancing Cooperation on Digital Trade APEC recognises the different approaches toward e-commerce and digital trade amongst member economies. APEC economies are encouraged to elaborate and promote measures and policies aimed at effective development of e-commerce including through policy and regulatory environments that are predictable, transparent and consistent. APEC will continue to facilitate e-commerce, including through the use of electronic means such as paperless customs clearance, electronic transaction documents, digital authentication, and electronic and online payments. Digital trade is among the fastest growing segments of global trade and has the potential to provide an extraordinary stimulus to the growth and trade of the Asia Pacific region as goods and services are increasingly transacted digitally. APEC encourages economies' initiatives to explore new areas of potential economic growth in the area of digital trade and related issues, including identifying building blocks and creating a favourable digital ecosystem. IMPLEMENTATION Senior Officials will have overall responsibility for monitoring and evaluating progress under the APEC Internet and Digital Economy Roadmap including implementation of the above Key Focus Areas by the relevant fora and sub-fora. Senior Officials will report periodically to Ministers on progress and seek further guidance given the evolving nature of the Internet and Digital Economy.
