en: 2026 APEC Ministers Responsible for Trade Joint Statement
cn: 2026年APEC贸易部长联合声明
summary: 4. 我们重申共同致力于以市场驱动的方式推进亚太地区经济一体化，包括通过亚太自由贸易区议程方面的工作。亚太经济合作组织可以在帮助各经济体提升参与高标准和全面承诺的能力方面发挥作用。我们将继续共同努力加强成员之间的经验分享、能力建设、商业参与和技术合作，包括通过能力建设需求倡议。正如《伊奇马声明》所确定的，我们支持推动高标准和扩大贸易协定中趋同领域的努力，包括就国有企业、贸易与劳工、贸易与环境、贸易数字化、数字贸易、贸易便利化、微型小型和中型企业以及竞争政策进行重要且富有意义的对话，以改善我们企业和人民的贸易和投资环境。 6. 我们支持在亚太经济合作组织内应对供应链问题的努力，以增强供应链韧性、促进可持续经济增长，并加强全球和区域价值链。我们认识到就可能影响贸易或扰乱供应链的措施保持透明度的重要性。我们欢迎供应链互联互通框架行动计划第三期（2022-2026年）在应对本地区供应链瓶颈方面的贡献，特别是在推动贸易程序数字化转型和无纸化贸易转型方面。我们指示官员在今年11月前完成供应链互联互通框架行动计划第三期的最终审查。我们鼓励私营部门更多参与亚太经济合作组织的供应链讨论，包括通过公私对话。我们认识到亚太经济合作组织现有平台在促进供应链互联互通和贸易便利化方面的协作作用。 9. 我们重申实质性改革和合作倡议对于实现开放和可预测的创新、竞争和有韧性的服务部门环境的重要性。为进一步推进这一目标，我们支持参与成员在亚太经济合作组织服务指数方面继续开展工作，通过将数字贸易纳入亚太经济合作组织服务指数来识别服务贸易壁垒。在此方面，我们欢迎《亚太经济合作组织创新、竞争和有韧性服务路线图》（附件），该路线图旨在识别和减少服务贸易壁垒、推动经济增长和促进就业创造。我们支持减少不必要壁垒和促进数字服务的工作。 15. 我们欢迎17个亚太经济合作组织经济体接受《世界贸易组织渔业补贴协定》，并呼吁其余经济体尽快完成国内程序，鼓励所有世界贸易组织成员尽快完成额外纪律的谈判。我们认识到在世界贸易组织就农业进行建设性参与的必要性。我们支持电子传输免征关税暂免令，该暂免令有助于保持数字市场的开放和可预测性，并注意到一些经济体为达成电子传输永久免征关税协定所做的努力。 16. 我们认识到世界贸易组织诸边谈判（包括联合声明倡议）在推进成员利益议题、应对当代贸易议题、培育新理念、促进经济增长和推动多边成果方面的积极作用。我们注意到世界贸易组织联合声明倡议参与成员为将《投资便利化促进发展协定》和《世界贸易组织电子商务协定》纳入世界贸易组织法律框架所做的努力。我们还注意到各经济体参与和实施《服务国内规制联合声明倡议》的努力。 17. 我们重申致力于发展数字经济，确保数字化转型惠及所有人，包括通过弥合数字鸿沟、拓宽和加强数字互联互通。我们期待继续实施《互联网与数字经济路线图》，以应对快速演变的数字格局中出现的新机遇和挑战。我们鼓励各经济体加强可负担和有韧性的数字基础设施，推进能力建设，加快互操作性，应对在线危害，提升数字素养和技能以促进数字化转型。认识到数据对数字经济日益增长的重要性，我们将继续合作促进跨境数据流动，增强消费者和企业在数字交易中的信任，同时确保数据保护和隐私。 18. 我们认识到数字化作为推动整个地区创新、生产力和经济增长的重要驱动力的作用，以及其在加强和便利贸易方面的益处。我们重申致力于通过推动电子贸易相关文件（包括电子提单和电子发票）的跨境认可以及通过能力建设努力，促进本地区无纸化贸易。我们欢迎在制定贸易数字化合作框架方面取得的实质性进展，以培育有利于贸易数字化的生态系统。我们鼓励各经济体确保以审慎和深思熟虑的方式采用贸易数字化新技术，并呼吁亚太经济合作组织就政府贸易数字化决策制定政策建议。我们鼓励公私部门之间进一步合作以推进本地区无纸化贸易，包括通过亚太经济合作组织无纸化贸易卓越中心。我们鼓励亚太经济合作组织各经济体在注意到各经济体准备程度和能力不同的情况下，致力于使我们的法律框架与联合国国际贸易法委员会《电子可转让记录示范法》的原则保持一致，以及与电子签名和电子认证使用方面的其他相关国际公约保持一致。 19. 回顾《亚太经济合作组织人工智能倡议》并认识到人工智能重塑国际贸易的潜力，我们致力于利用人工智能对贸易的益处并扩大本地区人工智能相关货物和服务贸易。我们还呼吁继续努力增强安全性、可及性、可信度和可靠性，以实现人工智能惠及所有人，包括促进人工智能在国际贸易和区域信息通信技术生态系统发展中的采用，重点放在信息交流、合作和能力建设上。我们期待在2026年亚太经济合作组织数字周期间继续讨论人工智能。 20. 我们认识到通过使用人工智能和技术创新加强供应链效率、安全和韧性的重要性。我们欢迎亚太经济合作组织在海关程序数字化和海关流程现代化方面的工作。我们欢迎在亚太经济合作组织内就贸易相关人工智能标准和技术进行自愿经验分享，同时考虑并补充适当的专业国际组织、进程和其他努力的工作。我们鼓励各经济体继续讨论人工智能日益增长作用背景下的贸易规则。我们还鼓励各经济体与私营部门（包括微型、小型和中型企业）分享相关人工智能政策的国内做法，以帮助企业识别机遇和风险并提高竞争力。 21. 我们认识到跨境电子商务对国际贸易和促进微型、小型和中型企业参与并融入全球价值链日益增长的重要性。我们赞赏亚太经济合作组织在海关管理、消费者保护和企业技能提升方面的工作，并支持有效实施该领域的倡议，包括《亚太经济合作组织海关与跨境电子商务非约束性指南》。我们欢迎开展能力建设活动以弥合数字鸿沟，并支持微型、小型和中型企业参与数字平台和全球数字经济。
summaryEn: 4. We reaffirm our shared commitment to advancing economic integration in the Asia-Pacific region in a manner that is market-driven, including through the work on the Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific (FTAAP) agenda. APEC can play a role in building economies' capacity to participate in high standard and comprehensive undertakings. We will continue working together to enhance experience sharing, capacity building, business engagement and technical cooperation among members, including through the Capacity Building Needs Initiative (CBNI). As identified in the Ichma Statement, we support efforts to promote high standards and increase areas of convergence in trade agreements, including through important and meaningful conversations on state-owned enterprises, trade and labor, trade and environment, trade digitalization, digital trade, trade facilitation, MSMEs and competition policy, to improve the trade and investment environment for our businesses and people. 6. We support efforts to address supply chains issues within APEC to enhance the resilience of supply chains for sustainable economic growth and strengthen global and regional value chains. We recognize the importance of transparency with respect to measures that may affect trade or disrupt supply chains. We welcome the contributions of the Third Phase of Supply Chain Connectivity Framework Action Plan (SCFAP III, 2022-2026) to address supply chain chokepoints in the region, especially in promoting digital transformation of trade procedures and transition towards paperless trade. We instruct officials to complete the final review of SCFAP III by November this year. We encourage greater engagement of the private sector in APEC's supply chain discussions, including through public-private dialogues. We recognize the collaborative role of existing platforms in APEC that promote supply chain connectivity and trade facilitation. 9. We reiterate the importance of substantive reforms and cooperative initiatives to achieve an open and predictable environment for innovative, competitive and resilient services sectors. To further advance this objective, we support continued work by participating members on the APEC Services Index to identify barriers to services trade by integrating digital trade into the APEC Services Index. In this regard, we welcome the APEC Roadmap for Innovative, Competitive and Resilient Services (Annex), which is intended to identify and reduce barriers to services trade, drive economic growth, and fuel job creation. We support work to reduce unnecessary barriers and facilitate digital services. 15. We welcome the acceptance by 17 APEC economies of the WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies and call on the remaining economies to complete their domestic procedures, and encourage all WTO Members to conclude negotiations on additional disciplines as soon as possible. We recognize the need for constructive engagement on agriculture at the WTO. We support a moratorium on customs duties on electronic transmissions which helps keep digital markets open and predictable, and note the efforts by some economies to reach an agreement for a permanent moratorium of customs duties on electronic transmissions. 16. We recognize the positive role that plurilateral negotiations at the WTO, including the Joint Statement Initiatives (JSIs), are playing in advancing issues of interest to Members, and in addressing contemporary trade issues, fostering new ideas, facilitating economic growth, and building momentum toward multilateral outcomes. We note the efforts of participating Members of the WTO JSIs to incorporate the Investment Facilitation for Development (IFD) Agreement and WTO Agreement on Electronic Commerce (ECA) into the WTO legal framework. We also note the efforts by economies to participate in and implement the JSI on Services Domestic Regulation. 17. We affirm our commitment to growing the digital economy and to ensuring that the benefits of digital transformation are accessible to all, including by bridging digital divides, and broadening and enhancing digital connectivity. We look forward to the continued implementation of the APEC Internet and Digital Economy Roadmap (AIDER) in a way that addresses emerging opportunities and challenges in the rapidly evolving digital landscape. We encourage economies to strengthen affordable and resilient digital infrastructure, promote capacity building, accelerate interoperability, address online harms, and enhance digital literacy and skills to facilitate digital transformation. Recognizing the increasing importance of data to the digital economy, we will continue our cooperation on facilitating the flow of data across borders, and strengthening business and consumer trust in digital transactions, in addition to ensuring data protection and privacy. 18. We recognize the important role of digitalization as a driver for innovation, productivity, and economic growth across the region, and its benefit to enhancing and facilitating trade. We reaffirm our commitment to facilitating paperless trade in the region, by promoting the cross-border recognition of electronic trade-related documents, including the electronic bills of lading and electronic invoices, and through capacity-building efforts. We welcome the substantial progress towards developing a framework for cooperation on trade digitalization in order to foster an enabling ecosystem for trade digitalization. We encourage economies to ensure that the adoption of new technologies for trade digitalization is made in a considered and deliberate manner, and call on APEC to develop policy recommendations for government decision-making on trade digitalization. We encourage further engagement between the public and private sectors to advance paperless trade in the region, including through the APEC Centre of Excellence for Paperless Trade (ACCEPT). We encourage APEC economies to work towards aligning our legal frameworks with the principles of the UNCITRAL Model Law on Electronic Transferable Records (MLETR), noting the different levels of readiness and capacity, and other relevant international conventions on the use of electronic signatures and electronic authentication. 19. Recalling the APEC AI Initiative and recognizing the potential of AI to reshape international trade, we are committed to harnessing AI's benefits for trade and expanding AI-related trade in goods and services in our region. We also call for continued efforts to enhance security, accessibility, trustworthiness and reliability in realizing the benefits of AI for all, including fostering the adoption of AI in international trade and regional ICT ecosystem development, with a focus on information exchange, cooperation and capacity building. We look forward to continued discussions on AI during APEC 2026 Digital Weeks. 20. We acknowledge the importance of strengthening supply chain efficiency, security, and resilience through the use of AI and technological innovations. We welcome APEC's work on digitalizing customs procedures and modernizing customs processes. We welcome voluntary experience sharing in APEC on trade-related AI standards and technologies that takes into account and complements the work of appropriate specialized international organizations, processes and other efforts. We encourage economies to continue to discuss trade rules in the context of the growing role of AI. We also encourage economies to share domestic approaches to relevant AI-related policy with the private sector, including MSMEs, to help businesses identify opportunities and risks as well as improve competitiveness. 21. We recognize the growing importance of cross-border e-commerce for international trade and facilitation of MSMEs' participation and integration into global value chains. We commend APEC's work on customs administration, consumer protection and business upskilling and support the effective implementation of initiatives in this area including the APEC Non-Binding Guidelines for Customs & Cross-Border E-Commerce. We welcome capacity building activities to bridge digital divides, and support MSME's participation in digital platforms and the global digital economy.

en: 2026 APEC Digital and AI Ministerial Statement
cn: 2026年亚太经合组织数字与人工智能部长声明
summary: 引言： 2. 在"数字技术与人工智能赋能亚太共同体"的主题下，与APEC 2026年主题"构建亚太共同体实现共同繁荣"及中国APEC优先事项"开放、创新、合作"相一致，我们继续以《APEC布城愿景2040》所确立的集体使命为指导，致力于到2040年实现一个开放、活力、韧性和平的亚太共同体，为我们所有人民和子孙后代的繁荣，包括通过落实APEC《互联网和数字经济路线图》及《APEC人工智能（AI）倡议（2026-2030）》。 一、普惠和有意义的数字互联互通： 6. 注意到数字技术和人工智能的快速发展，我们鼓励各经济体通过APEC经济体间的信息交流和能力建设，加强合作并促进对数字连接基础设施的投资。我们还将继续在促进数据流动和加强数字交易中消费者和企业信任方面开展合作。 二、促进经济增长的数字技术与人工智能： 7. 认识到数字技术和人工智能赋能各经济体提升生产力、效率和韧性并支持经济增长，我们鼓励各经济体加速创新和负责任地采用数字技术和人工智能，以充分释放这些技术在各领域的效益。 我们鼓励各经济体推动制造业、农业和服务业等领域的数字和人工智能转型，并通过分享相关政策、经验和最佳实践加强这方面的合作。认识到数字和人工智能转型对中小微企业（MSMEs）提升竞争力至关重要，我们进一步鼓励各经济体继续通过提供经济实惠且易于部署的数字产品和解决方案来支持中小企业，并鼓励其负责任地采用。 四、可信赖的数字环境： 12. 我们承认数据泄露、网络诈骗以及蓄意滥用人工智能和其他新兴技术等风险。我们对本地区网络诈骗活动的升级深表关切，这些活动威胁个人和企业的财务安全，侵蚀公众对数字系统的信任，并削弱对我们更广泛数字经济的信心。我们认识到加大力度提升对这些风险的认识并加以缓解，对于维持信任和信心至关重要。我们呼吁各经济体推动应对这些风险的创新，包括通过各经济体之间的合作以及信息和最佳实践的交流，以建设一个安全、可靠、可信和有韧性的数字环境。 我们鼓励各经济体自愿与政府、相关专门组织、私营部门、民间社会、技术界和学术界合作，分享ICT安全、数据保护、供应链韧性、数字基础设施韧性、技术标准、反网络诈骗措施和儿童在线保护等方面的最佳实践。我们进一步鼓励业界加强问责，推动数字技术（包括AI）的安全、可靠和有韧性的使用，并增强消费者、企业和公众的隐私、信任和信心。 五、数字生态系统的投资与开源： 15. 我们注意到可信的开源方法在释放数字技术潜力和促进数字经济创新方面的重要作用。在尊重安全、数据保护和知识产权的前提下，我们鼓励各经济体支持在开发和部署中采用强有力安全保障的开源模型和项目。我们还鼓励各经济体与开源社区开展合作。
summaryEn: Introduction: 2. Under the theme of "Digital Technologies and AI for the Empowerment of an Asia-Pacific Community", which aligns with the APEC 2026 theme of "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together" and China's APEC priorities of "Openness, Innovation, Cooperation", we continue to be guided by our collective mission as set forth in the APEC Putrajaya Vision 2040 for an open, dynamic, resilient and peaceful Asia-Pacific community by 2040, for the prosperity of all our people and future generations, including through the implementation of the APEC Internet and Digital Economy Roadmap and the APEC Artificial Intelligence (AI) Initiative (2026-2030). I. Universal and Meaningful Digital Connectivity: 6. Noting the rapid advancement of digital technologies and AI, we encourage member economies to enhance cooperation and promote investment in digital connectivity infrastructure through information exchange and capacity building among APEC economies. We will also continue our cooperation on facilitating the flow of data and strengthening consumer and business trust in digital transactions. II. Digital Technologies and AI for Economic Growth: 7. Recognizing that digital technologies and AI empower member economies to enhance productivity, efficiency and resilience and support economic growth, we encourage member economies to accelerate innovation and the responsible adoption of digital technologies and AI, in order to fully unlock these technologies' benefits across diverse fields. We encourage member economies to promote the digital and AI transformation of sectors such as manufacturing, agriculture and services, and strengthen cooperation in this regard by sharing relevant policies, experiences and best practices. Recognizing that digital and AI transformation is pivotal for micro-, small- and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) to enhance their competitiveness, we further encourage member economies to continue supporting MSMEs by providing affordable and easy-to-deploy digital products and solutions, and encouraging their responsible adoption. IV. Trusted Digital Environment: 12. We acknowledge risks such as data breaches, online scams and the deliberate misuse of AI and other emerging technologies. We express deep concern over the escalation of online scam activities across our region, which threaten the financial security of individuals and businesses, erode public trust in digital systems, and undermine confidence in our broader digital economy. We recognize that stepping up efforts to promote awareness of and mitigate these risks is essential to maintaining trust and confidence. We call on member economies to promote innovation that addresses these risks, including through cooperation and the exchange of information and best practices among member economies, with the goal of building a safe, secure, reliable, trusted and resilient digital environment. We encourage member economies to voluntarily engage with governments, appropriate specialized organizations, the private sector, civil society, technical community and academia to share best practices in the areas of ICT security, data protection, supply chain resilience, digital infrastructure resilience, technical standards, anti-online scam measures and child online protection. We further encourage industry to enhance accountability, promote the secure, reliable and resilient use of digital technologies, including AI, and enhance the privacy, trust and confidence of consumers, businesses and the public. V. Investment and Open Source for Digital Ecosystem: 15. We note the important role of trusted open-source approaches in unlocking the potential of digital technologies and fostering innovation in the digital economy. While respecting security, data protection and intellectual property rights, we encourage member economies to support open-source models and projects that employ strong security assurance through development and deployment. We also encourage member economies to engage in cooperation with open-source communities.

en: Navigating Artificial Intelligence Landscape in APEC: Balancing Development and Oversight
cn: APEC人工智能格局导航：平衡发展与监管
summary: 1. AI发展现状： 在全球和APEC范围内，AI发展和采用快速推进。根据麦肯锡的全球调查，将AI能力整合到业务流程中的组织比例从2018年的47%飙升至2024年的78%。对AI日益增长的兴趣也推动了APEC区域内投资大幅增长。自2018年以来，该地区对私营AI公司的股权投资增长了156.9%，2024年达到1649亿美元的高点。2024年按投资金额排名前三的AI应用领域为：数据与分析（777亿美元）、软件（747亿美元）和通用应用（730亿美元）。 2022年11月OpenAI ChatGPT的发布催化了AI的广泛采用。GenAI现已广泛用于创建内容，包括文本、图像和视频。反映GenAI技术进步的是，该领域的专利族数量在过去10年中从约700项激增至超过14,000项。根据专利申请中提供的发明人地址，APEC经济体（中国、日本、韩国和美国）在2014至2023年间位列这些专利的前四大来源经济体。GenAI领域的科学出版物数量增长更大，从2014年的约100篇呈指数级增长至2023年的超过34,000篇。 2. AI对贸易的影响： AI正通过其对全球价值链的影响日益重塑贸易格局。企业可以利用AI工具提升对直接供应商和二级供应商之外的可视性，从而更好地管理供应链风险。AI进步可能导致生产环节重组，因为自动化程度提高改变了跨境劳动分工，并可能鼓励生产回流。企业还可以利用AI优化物流流动并应对复杂贸易规则，从而降低贸易成本。海关机关可以利用AI征收税费、进行商品归类并开展货运风险评估。 AI的出现和激增还创造了AI产品的新需求，支持AI相关货物和服务的贸易，并吸引熟练人才。GPU等核心组件对AI系统的开发、测试和部署至关重要，而ICT服务和网络设备是实现无缝连接的必要条件。此外，AI系统需要高质量训练数据，这使得便利跨境数据流动的政策更加重要。 3. AI的风险与挑战： 尽管AI带来显著效益，但其兴起也带来若干挑战。一个是其决策过程的不透明性。AI系统使用多层算法和庞大数据集，使其输出背后的原理甚至对开发者也不清楚。 更隐蔽的是，AI可被用于便利非法活动和侵犯权利。在商业领域，AI模型的复杂性使企业能够在反竞争行为中声称合理的否认。此外，AI还被用于通过自动机器人和深度伪造传播虚假信息，影响社交媒体上的公众舆论。AI还可能成为歧视和非法监控的工具。此外，AI在知识产权侵权方面的作用也引起关注，对创意经济构成相当大的风险。 加剧AI风险的另一个方面是开发AI系统通常成本高昂，尤其是随着模型变得更加复杂。例如，OpenAI GPT-3的训练成本估计超过400万美元，而GPT-4的训练成本据报道已超过1亿美元。这可能导致更高的市场集中度，近期发现超过90项合作和战略投资涉及相同的少数几个主要参与者。AI支持服务领域也受到此类市场整合的影响。例如，云计算市场由三家科技巨头主导，控制约三分之二的市场。 获取数据对于在开发者之间实现公平竞争也至关重要，并已成为AI开发的关键瓶颈之一。有限的数据获取与高昂的AI开发成本相结合，可能加深数字鸿沟，加剧经济体之间和内部、社区之间以及社会经济群体之间的差距。例如，AI的采用可能通过提高效率减少对大量低成本劳动力的依赖，从而加速发展中经济体的过早去工业化。 4. FTA和DEA中的AI专项条款： 2020年《澳大利亚-新加坡数字经济协定》是首个包含AI专项条款的协定。此后，AI条款至少出现在另外8项FTA或DEA中。值得注意的是，9项协定中有6项至少涉及一个APEC经济体。 FTA和DEA中的AI条款突显了以下关键监管趋势： AI的经济效益：许多协定强调AI提供的经济优势。 以可信、安全和负责任地使用AI为核心的伦理治理框架：9项协定中有8项将伦理治理作为"尽最大努力"条款。 与国际原则保持一致：OECD AI原则被明确提及；DEPA列出可解释性、透明度、公平性和以人为本等原则。 基于风险的监管方法：三项协定强调基于风险的监管方法的重要性。 总体而言，这些协定强调合作而非严格规则制定。 5. APEC经济体的监管活动： 随着APEC经济体中各行业和消费者加速采用AI，跨境监管合作仍处于早期阶段。尽管若干APEC经济体已出台国内战略和立法，以监管AI发展及其应用，但这些框架如何实现互操作仍缺乏清晰性。新出现的监管碎片化可能提高AI采用成本，并可能影响贸易和投资流动。 在已通过AI专项法律、法规或指南的经济体（如中国、韩国、秘鲁、俄罗斯和美国），通常纳入受国际文书启发的原则。常被引用的原则包括问责制、透明度和可解释性，反映了AI治理在原则层面的趋同。然而，其范围和实施存在显著差异。差异特别体现在监管范围（如法规是否仅适用于私营实体还是也适用于政府使用）、AI系统提供者的具体义务以及执法机制力度等方面。 6. APEC的角色： 作为首要区域论坛，APEC在协调亚太地区AI监管方法方面发挥关键作用。随着AI技术快速发展，对可互操作法规的需求前所未有地迫切。APEC在数据治理方面建立有利框架（即APEC跨境隐私规则（CBPR）系统）的经验，使其有良好条件应对这一挑战。 分享将AI原则付诸实践的良好做法：APEC可以集中力量帮助各经济体将理论原则转化为可行动的政策和实践。这包括制定示范指南和框架，确保AI使用符合伦理、透明和问责。 作为提高AI监管活动透明度的论坛：类似于数据隐私子组关于数据隐私的定期报告机制，在新兴AI治理方面也可以建立类似报告机制。 扩大FTA和DEA中的AI承诺：通过纳入AI专项条款，APEC经济体可以统一监管目标，包括就共同原则达成一致、建立AI技术标准、促进互操作性以及便利AI应用所必需的跨境数据流动。 促进AI相关问题（如AI标准化、知识产权）的相互理解和共识：APEC可以在促进各成员经济体讨论方面发挥重要作用，分享为AI调整知识产权法律框架的方法。 确保AI相关政策和倡议中的包容性：APEC可以倡导增强基础设施和可负担性的政策和倡议，以实现更广泛获取AI技术。
summaryEn: 1. AI Development Status: Globally and within APEC, AI development and adoption have progressed rapidly. According to a global survey by McKinsey, the proportion of organisations integrating AI capabilities into business processes surged from 47 percent in 2018 to 78 percent in 2024. This growing interest in AI has also spurred a significant increase in investment within APEC. Since 2018, equity investment in private AI firms in the region has risen by 156.9 percent, reaching a high of USD 164.9 billion in 2024. The top three AI application fields by investment value in 2024 were data and analytics (USD 77.7 billion), software (USD 74.7 billion), and general-purpose applications (USD 73.0 billion). The release of OpenAI's ChatGPT in November 2022 has catalysed widespread AI adoption. GenAI is now widely used for creating content, including text, images and videos. Reflecting technological advancements in GenAI, the number of patent families in this field has surged from around 700 to more than 14,000 just in the past 10 years. Based on the inventor addresses provided in patent applications, APEC economies (China; Japan; Korea; and the United States) made up the top four source economies for these patents between 2014 and 2023. The number of scientific publications on GenAI has seen an even greater increase, exponentially rising from about 100 in 2014 to more than 34,000 in 2023. 2. AI's Impact on Trade: The trade landscape is increasingly being reshaped by AI through its impacts on the global value chains. Firms can leverage AI tools to better manage their supply chain risks by enhancing visibility beyond direct and second-tier suppliers. Advancements in AI may lead to the restructuring of production links as increased automation alters the cross-border division of labour, potentially encouraging the onshoring of production. Firms can also reduce trade costs using AI through its ability to optimise logistics flows and navigate complex trade regulations. Customs authorities can leverage AI to administer tax and duty collection, classify products, and conduct risk assessments of shipments. The emergence and surge of AI also creates new demand for AI products, supporting the trade of AI-related goods and services, and attracting skilled talents. Core components such as graphics processing units (GPUs) are essential for developing, testing and deploying AI systems, while ICT services and network equipment are necessary for seamless connectivity. Furthermore, AI systems require high-quality training data, making policies to facilitate cross-border data flows even more important. 3. AI Risks and Challenges: Despite its significant benefits, the rise of AI presents several challenges. One issue is its opaque decision-making process. AI systems use layers of algorithms and vast datasets, making the rationale behind their outputs unclear, even to developers. More insidiously, AI can be used to facilitate illegal activities and rights violations. In the business world, the complexity of AI models enables firms to claim plausible deniability in anti-competitive practices. Additionally, AI has been employed to spread misinformation through automated bots and deepfakes, influencing public opinion on social media. AI can also be a tool for discrimination and unlawful surveillance. Besides, concerns have been raised about AI's role in intellectual property (IP) infringement, posing considerable risks to the creative economy. Another aspect that heightens AI risks is the generally high cost of developing AI systems, especially as models become more complex. For example, the training cost of OpenAI's GPT-3 was estimated to be over USD 4 million while GPT-4's training cost has reportedly exceeded USD 100 million. This could lead to higher market concentration, with recent findings showing that over 90 partnerships and strategic investments involve the same few major players. Sectors in AI-supporting services are also subject to such market consolidation. The cloud computing market, for instance, is dominated by three tech giants controlling about two-thirds of the market. Access to data is also crucial to level the playing field among developers and has become one of the key bottlenecks in AI development. The combination of limited data access and high AI development costs could deepen the digital divide, exacerbating disparities between and within economies, communities, and socioeconomic groups. For example, the adoption of AI may accelerate premature deindustrialisation in developing economies by reducing dependence on large pool of low-cost labour through improved efficiency. 4. AI-specific Provisions in FTAs and DEAs: The Australia-Singapore Digital Economy Agreement of 2020 is the first agreement which includes an AI-specific provision. Since then, AI provisions have appeared in at least eight additional FTAs or DEAs. Notably, six out of the nine agreements involve at least one APEC economy as a participant. The AI provisions in FTAs and DEAs underscore key regulatory trends: Economic benefits of AI: Many agreements emphasise the economic advantages that AI offers. Ethical governance frameworks centred around trusted, safe, and responsible use of AI: Eight of the nine agreements present ethical governance as "best endeavour" provision. Alignment with international principles: The OECD AI Principles are explicitly mentioned; DEPA outlines principles such as explainability, transparency, fairness, and human-centred values. Risk-based regulatory approaches: Three agreements highlight the importance of risk-based regulatory approaches. Overall, agreements emphasise cooperation over strict rulemaking. 5. Regulatory Activity in APEC Economies: As AI adoption by industries and consumers in APEC economies accelerates, cross-border regulatory cooperation is still in its early stages. Although several APEC economies have introduced domestic strategies and legislation to regulate AI development and its applications, there remains limited clarity on how these frameworks can be interoperable. The emerging regulatory fragmentation could raise costs of AI adoption, potentially affecting trade and investment flows. Where AI-specific laws, regulations, or guidelines have been passed (e.g., China; Korea; Peru; Russia; and the United States), they typically incorporate principles inspired by international instruments. Commonly referenced principles include accountability, transparency, and explainability, reflecting a convergence in AI governance at the level of principles. However, significant differences exist in their scope and implementation. Variations are particularly evident in aspects such as the regulatory scope (e.g., whether regulations apply solely to private entities or also to government use), specific obligations for AI system providers, and the strength of enforcement mechanisms. 6. Role for APEC: As a premier regional forum, APEC plays a crucial role in coordinating AI regulatory approaches across the Asia-Pacific region. With the rapid advancement in AI technologies, the need for interoperable regulations has never been more pressing. APEC's experience in creating an enabling framework for data governance (i.e., the APEC Cross-Border Privacy Rules (CBPR) System) puts it in good stead to take this challenge head on. Share good practices on putting AI principles into practice: APEC can focus its efforts on helping economies translate theoretical principles into actionable policies and practices. This includes developing model guidelines and frameworks to ensure that AI use is ethical, transparent, and accountable. Act as a forum for increased transparency on AI regulatory activity: A similar reporting mechanism [to the DPS data privacy reporting] could be beneficial in the context of emerging AI governance. Expand commitments on AI in FTAs and DEAs: By integrating AI-specific provisions, APEC economies can align their regulatory goals, including agreeing on common principles, establishing standards for AI technologies, promoting interoperability, and facilitating cross-border data flows essential for AI applications. Foster mutual understanding and build consensus around AI-related issues (e.g., AI standardisation, IP): APEC can play a vital role in facilitating discussions among member economies to share approaches for adapting IP legal frameworks for AI. Ensure inclusion in AI-related policies and initiatives: APEC can advocate for policies and initiatives that enhance infrastructure and affordability to enable broader access to AI technologies.

en: Building an Enabling Environment for FinTech
cn: 构建金融科技有利环境
summary: 摘要 （一）区块链领域的机遇、局限与新兴趋势 现代贸易价值链结构复杂、环节分散，在信息准确性、可追溯性、透明度方面面临诸多挑战。对此，区块链应用可从三大维度破解现代贸易核心难题： 第一，区块链推动经过核验、安全性更高、成本更低的贸易交易； 第二，区块链推动贸易融资流程现代化、精简优化； 第三，区块链助力成本更低、速度更快的跨境支付，推动尽职调查流程更加顺畅高效。 尽管区块链应用具备重塑现代贸易价值链的巨大潜力，但应当客观认识到，区块链在国际贸易与贸易融资领域的大量现实应用仍处于起步阶段，相关技术尚在持续发展。搭建区块链解决方案对资源消耗较大，要求经济体或机构具备基础互联网接入条件之外、更高水平的数字基础设施与数字技能。在部分场景下，若现有方案运行良好，采用区块链带来的额外效益十分有限。 （二）环境、社会和治理标准与金融科技 可持续金融，即在投资决策中纳入环境、社会和治理评价标准，现已成为愈发重要的工具，引导金融资源助力落实联合国可持续发展目标、《巴黎协定》目标等国际承诺。 金融科技可从三大方面成为发展可持续金融的重要支撑： 第一，金融科技所运用的技术能够提供更丰富、精准的环境、社会和治理数据，更好核算可持续发展目标相关风险与影响； 第二，金融科技有助于引导大规模资金流向更具可持续性的投资项目； 第三，智能投顾、线上借贷、众筹平台等金融科技服务快速兴起，降低绿色项目、社会责任项目、可持续发展主题项目的募资难度。 企业在投资决策、合规管理中纳入环境、社会和治理评价标准，推动各地陆续出台多元化的环境、社会和治理标准及信息披露框架。为解决标准碎片化问题，监管机构与政府部门采取多项创新举措，推动在国内、区域、全球层面建立更加统一的环境、社会和治理会计标准，具体包括：在各国层面推出统一信息披露标准；在区域层面出台可持续发展战略；在全球层面搭建基准标准体系。 政策建议与后续举措 本报告探讨的金融科技创新产品与服务，正推动现代贸易价值链、可持续金融领域加速落地各类新技术与新应用。亚太经合组织及其成员经济体可参考以下政策建议，促进服务贸易、可持续金融领域新兴技术发展，充分释放上述金融科技应用带来的社会经济效益。 推动贸易与可持续金融领域新兴技术发展：五大宏观路径 ——结合各国数字能力建设行动（数字技能提升、现有技术基础设施升级），培育政府内部关键创新领域专业人才队伍。 ——搭建公私合作伙伴关系，促进公私部门加强协作，共同研发前沿技术。 ——设立创新基金等研发专项资金，支持突破性技术推向市场。 ——鉴于本报告探讨的相关技术应用尚不成熟，探索监管沙盒模式的实践运用。 ——设立创新中心，培育市场发展，打造一站式枢纽，汇总新兴技术相关各类信息。 充分释放金融科技社会经济效益：五项可行举措 ——将便利贸易、推动经济可持续发展的金融科技应用纳入各国政策议程。 ——制定清晰且具备灵活性的监管规则，提振投资者信心，降低新技术与创新模式的落地成本。 ——面向行业相关主体开展公众咨询，确保各类非政府主体的意见与诉求纳入政策制定流程。 ——营造环境，助力技术国际化发展，支持通用标准落地推行。 ——搭建知识共享渠道，协助亚太经合组织各经济体梳理各方可协同推进的优先事项，探索跨境试点项目。
summaryEn: Summary (i) Opportunities, Limitation, and Emerging Trends in Blockchain Modern trade value chains are complex, fragmented, and face challenges in accuracy, traceability, and transparency. To this end, applications of blockchain can help address key challenges in modern day trade in three major ways: i) blockchain can facilitate verified, more secured, and cheaper trade transactions; ii) blockchain can modernise and streamline the trade finance process; and iii) blockchain can facilitate faster and cheaper cross-border payments, and enabler smoother and faster due diligence processes. While there is immense potential for blockchain applications to transform the modern trade value chains, it is important to acknowledge that much of its real-life applications international trade and trade finance are relatively nascent, and the technology is still developing. Implementing blockchain solutions can be a resource intensive undertaking and require economies or organisations to have more than a baseline level of internet connectivity or digital skills. In some instance, the adoption of blockchain may even prove to have limited additional benefits over an existing solution, particularly if the existing solution functions well. (ii) ESG Standards and FinTech Sustainable finance is the practice of integrating ESG criteria in an investment decision and is an increasingly important lever to help drive finance towards achieving international commitments such as the UN SDG and the Paris Agreement targets. FinTech has the potential to be a critical enabler of sustainable finance in three major ways: (i) Technologies used in FinTech can provider richer, more accurate ESG data for better accounting of SDG related risks and impact; (ii) Fintech can help reorient capital flows towards more sustainable investments at scale; (iii) the rise of FinTech services like robo-advising/ -investing, marketplace lending, and crowdfunding platforms have made it easier to raise funds for green, socially responsible, or sustainability-themed projects. The integration of ESG criteria in investment decisions or as part of compliance requirements for companies, has contributed to the varied development of ESG standards and reporting frameworks. To address this fragmented expansion, regulatory authorities and government bodies have taken several innovative approaches that promote more uniform accounting standards on ESG criteria at the domestic, regional, and global level. This includes introducing common reporting standards at a domestic level, implementing a sustainability strategy at a regional level, and establishing base-line standards at a global level. Policy Recommendations and Next Steps Innovative product and services that draw on advancements in FinTech as discussed in this report are driving greater adoption and new applications in modern-day trade value chains and sustainable financing. APEC and its member economies could consider the following policy recommendations to help advance the development of emerging technologies for trade and sustainable finance, and to realise the socioeconomic benefits from the FinTech applications discussed above. Specifically: To advance development of emerging technologies for trade and sustainable finance, APEC and its member economies could consider the following five high-level approaches: • Develop in-house government expertise on key innovations, in line with domestic capacity-building initiatives on digital upskilling and upgrading of existing technology infrastructures. • Establish public-private partnership to allow greater collaboration between public and private sector in the development of cutting-edge technologies. • Provide capital for research and development such as an innovation fund, that is dedicated to helping bring breakthrough technologies to market. • Evaluate the use of regulatory sandboxes given the nascency of the technology applications discussed in this report. • Establish innovation centres to foster market growth and serve as a one-stop hub for relevant information on emerging technologies. To help realise socioeconomic gains from FinTech, APEC and its member economies could consider the following five actionable steps: • Incorporate applications that facilitate trade and promote a more sustainable economy as part of domestic agendas. • Establish clear and flexible regulations that boost investor confidence and reduce adoption cost of new technologies and innovation. • Launch public consultation processes with industry stakeholders to ensure that views and needs of relevant non-state actors are incorporated in the policy development process • Create an environment that enables and strengthens internationalisation, including supporting the adoption of common standards. • Create channels for knowledge sharing that help APEC economies identify areas of mutual priorities for collaboration and potential cross-border pilots.
impact: 本报告总结了2022年9月举办的“为金融科技打造有利环境”虚拟研讨会的成果。 金融科技正迅速成为经济体金融部门成熟和增长的关键元素，社会经济的发展和技术进步为金融科技的广泛采用和创新奠定了基础。新冠疫情加速了金融科技的普及，因为它能够及时且包容地提供金融服务。 报告聚焦于金融科技的两个关键应用，探讨区块链在促进更好贸易实践和贸易融资中的作用，以及金融科技在推动可持续金融和环境、社会、治理标准制定或满足中的作用。最后，会议还提出了政策建议，供APEC成员经济体考虑，以促进贸易和可持续金融新兴技术的发展，并实现金融科技应用带来的社会经济效益。
impactEn: This report summarizes the findings of the virtual workshop on Building an enabling environment for FinTech held in September 2022. FinTech is rapidly becoming a key element to the maturity and growth of an economy’s financial sector, with socioeconomic developments and technological advancements laying the foundation for greater FinTech adoption and innovation. The COVID-19 pandemic accelerated the adoption of FinTech, due to its ability to provide financial services in a timely and inclusive manner. Focusing on two critical applications of FinTech, the report considers the role of blockchain in enabling better trade practices and trade finance, and FinTech’s role in enabling sustainable finance and the development or meeting of environmental, social, governance standards. It concludes with policy recommendations for APEC member economies to consider that help advance the development of emerging technologies for trade and sustainable finance, and to realize the socioeconomic benefits from FinTech applications.

en: Workshop on Use of International Instruments to Legally Enable End- to-End Digitalization of Trade
cn: 关于使用国际工具合法实现贸易端到端数字化的研讨会
summary: 执行摘要 本次研讨会汇集了来自8个亚太经济合作组织经济体的30名参与者，讨论数字贸易交易中法律协调日益增长的重要性，这与亚太经济合作组织长期以来的优先事项相一致：促进贸易数字化的互操作生态系统，正如《奥特亚罗瓦行动计划》、《亚太经济合作组织互联网与数字经济路线图》和《强化的亚太经济合作组织结构改革议程》所强调的。 在亚太经济合作组织区域已大量采纳联合国国际贸易法委员会框架支持贸易端到端数字化的基础上，进一步采纳和实施联合国国际贸易法委员会文本可促进数字贸易和无纸化贸易的更广泛使用，从而提高效率、降低成本并促进贸易增长，有望推动亚太经济合作组织各经济体乃至更广泛地区的贸易量、就业和实际工资的提升。 开幕致辞 安娜·朱宾-雷特女士，联合国国际贸易法委员会秘书 多年来区域利益相关方反复关切的一个问题是，区域和双边数字贸易规则的激增——即"面条碗"效应——可能导致代价高昂的碎片化，尤其对微型、小型和中型企业及发展中经济体而言。为应对这一问题，联合国国际贸易法委员会已制定统一法律文书，不仅支持政府对数字化商业文件的认可和使用，而且在全链条上为贸易数字化提供法律保障——从贸易融资到运输、无纸化贸易、电子商务、数字经济争端解决以及数字资产追踪与追回。 展望未来，朱宾-雷特女士提请关注联合国国际贸易法委员会关于数字平台的新的立法项目，该项目邀请亚太经济合作组织各经济体考虑制定新的统一规则，旨在重新调整参与者的权利和义务，以确保公平性和法律确定性。 虽然各政府在制定数字化政策和法律应对方面处于不同阶段，但这些差异本身并不妨碍在国际层面寻求协调一致的解决方案，而在国际层面找到解决方案可以防止碎片化的管辖权法律应对的产生，这些碎片化的法律应对可能构成贸易障碍。正在进行的无纸化贸易探索性工作表明，联合国国际贸易法委员会关于电子商务的立法"工具箱"对于实现真正的端到端贸易数字化具有高度相关性，联合国国际贸易法委员会邀请亚太经济合作组织各经济体继续积极参与塑造数字贸易法的未来。 詹姆斯·丁博士，亚太经济合作组织经济委员会主席 他强调，除技术之外，法律确定性和协调统一的框架同样不可或缺。他还强调，采纳国际文本和标准可以增强互操作性。这些努力对于支持微型、小型和中型企业、增强融资渠道以及在亚太地区培育具有韧性、面向未来的贸易生态系统至关重要。 各场次总结 第一场：迈向端到端数字贸易交易 艾伦·戴维森博士，联合国国际贸易法委员会第四工作组主席，澳大利亚昆士兰大学高级讲师 戴维森博士强调了联合国国际贸易法委员会在国际贸易法协调方面的长期努力，指出已被170个司法管辖区采纳的《电子商务示范法》为电子商务的法律确定性奠定了基础。他进一步解释说，该示范法在电子文件与纸质文件之间建立了功能等同，确保电子通信和电子签名不会仅因其媒介形式而被否定法律效力。 戴维森博士随后聚焦于较新的文书，特别是《电子可转让记录示范法》，该法解决了一个关键挑战：将"所有权凭证"（如提单）数字化。与标准电子文件不同，这些记录需要转移占有权以传递权利，而《电子可转让记录示范法》通过将电子"控制"等同于实物占有、将控制权转移等同于实物交付来解决这一问题。 他还讨论了《跨境身份管理与信任服务认可示范法》和《自动缔约示范法》，分别涉及数字身份验证和人工智能驱动的合同订立。这些文书回应了区块链和人工智能等新兴技术，这些技术在早期示范法起草时是未被预见到的。 戴维森博士援引一份亚太经济合作组织报告预测，如果《电子可转让记录示范法》及相关法律文书得到广泛采用，未来十年可节省约2万亿美元，强调了法律协调背后的经济理据。 第三场：贸易融资与数字资产数字化 孔萨克·端吉先生，泰国银行家协会秘书长，泰国 他认为，新技术——区块链、应用程序接口和人工智能——能够实现企业对企业、企业对政府和政府对政府交易中可信、无缝的数据流动。然而，挑战在于建立互操作性并避免双边协议碎片化的"意大利面条碗"。他呼吁采纳国际标准，特别是《电子可转让记录示范法》和《亚洲及太平洋跨境无纸化贸易便利化框架协议》，以及数字身份系统，以创建合法性和信任。 第四场：数字经济争端解决中的问题 高桥和明先生，日本法务省国际事务科律师 数字经济争端解决项目源于日本在新冠疫情期间提出的一项提案，疫情凸显了法律框架适应全球贸易和商业快速数字化的紧迫需求。自2021年12月以来，联合国国际贸易法委员会秘书处一直在进行全面的数字经济争端解决梳理工作，以探索数字技术和技术赋能服务对争端解决的影响，旨在确定是否需要更新现有文书或制定新文书，并提出潜在解决方案。 朴在成检察官，韩国法务部国际法律政策科 《纽约公约》第4条要求寻求执行的当事方提交"经正式认证的裁决正本"或核证副本，但该条款早于数字化发展，在电子签发的裁决是否具备资格方面造成了模糊性。 为解决这一问题，联合国国际贸易法委员会第二工作组正在探索三种可能的解决方案。第一，发布一项建议，将《纽约公约》中的"裁决正本"解释为涵盖电子裁决。这一方案因其务实性而受到青睐，因为它避免了条约修订的复杂性，尽管缺乏约束力。第二，修订《联合国国际贸易法委员会国际商事仲裁示范法》，为电子仲裁裁决提供明确指引，这将依赖于国内采纳才能生效。第三，修订《纽约公约》或制定新的议定书——这是一个影响更大但更为耗时的选项，因为条约修订需要成员国批准，并可能在采纳方和非采纳方之间造成双层体系。 特蕾莎·罗德里格斯·德拉斯·埃拉斯·巴列尔教授，西班牙马德里卡洛斯三世大学 平台被描述为基于合同的组织模式，通过平台运营者与用户之间的协议形成，用户可包括企业、消费者或非专业用户。这些协议管辖平台内的所有关系和活动，使运营者成为监管者和监督者，并可能成为争端解决机制的提供者或促进者。 在人工智能和自动化方面，在基于平台的争端解决背景下，需要考虑自动化和人工智能系统可以在多大程度上被使用。借鉴现有的自动决策原则，三个方面特别相关：它是否可解释、是否有适当的推理，以及是否接受司法审查。 丹尼·翁先生，新加坡盛德律师事务所董事总经理 翁先生指出，数字资产——如加密货币——不能整齐地归入"财产"或"有形资产"等传统法律类别，其可执行性存在模糊性。这种模糊性因管辖权差异而加剧：中国香港和新加坡等普通法管辖区通常依赖"控制"概念来确定对数字资产的权利，而其他管辖区可能不认可此类资产作为可依法执行的担保物或可扣押标的，从而削弱了跨境执行。 翁先生在结论中建议，可以通过制定一部新的《联合国国际贸易法委员会数字资产执行示范法》来解决这些问题，从而实现一致且有效的跨境执行实践。 结论 统一的法律框架（如联合国国际贸易法委员会文本）可在整个贸易生命周期中作为有用参考，以法律确定性实现贸易的"端到端"数字化，包括无纸化流程、数字担保物和跨境执行。此外，国际合作对于促进微型、小型和中型企业实现经济潜力并达成亚太经济合作组织数字转型目标至关重要。 展望未来，鼓励各经济体—— a）考虑利用国际文书使国内制度与国际标准接轨； b）加强能力建设，使微型、小型和中型企业、贸易平台和政策制定者跨边境参与； c）利用技术进步，同时考虑互操作性、可信数据的需求以及支持数字贸易的数字能力。
summaryEn: Executive Summary This workshop drew 30 participants from 8 APEC economies to discuss the increasing significance of legal harmonization in digital transactions for trade, which aligned with APEC's long-standing priorities: facilitating an interoperable ecosystem for trade digitalization as highlighted by Aotearoa Plan of Action, the APEC Internet and Digital Economy Roadmap (AIDER) and the Enhanced APEC Agenda for Structural Reform (EAASR). Building on the existing significant regional uptake of the UNCITRAL framework supporting end-to-end trade digitalization, further adoption and implementation of UNCITRAL texts may promote broader use of digital and paperless trade, leading to improved efficiency, lower costs, and a boost in trade, potentially driving up trade volumes, employment, and real wages across APEC economies and beyond. Opening Remarks Ms. Anna Joubin-Bret, Secretary of UNCITRAL A main concern reiterated by regional stakeholders across the years was that the proliferation of regional and bilateral digital trade rules —the "noodle bowl" effect —risks creating costly fragmentation, especially for micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) and developing economies. To address this, UNCITRAL has developed uniform law instruments not only for the purpose of supporting the recognition and use of digitalized commercial documents by governments, but also to legally enable digitalization of trade across the board – from trade finance to transport, paperless trade, e-commerce, dispute resolution in the digital economy and digital asset tracing and recovery. Looking ahead, Ms. Joubin-Bret flagged UNCITRAL's new legislative project on digital platforms, which invites consideration by APEC economies of new harmonized rules aimed at recalibrating the rights and obligations of participants to ensure fairness and legal certainty. While governments may be at different stages of formulating policies and legal responses to digitization, these differences are themselves no impediment to striving to find harmonized solutions at an international level, and finding solutions at an international level can forestall the development of fragmented jurisdictional legal responses, which can constitute an obstacle to trade. Ongoing exploratory work on paperless trade is showing just how relevant UNCITRAL's legislative "toolkit" on electronic commerce can be to realizing true end-to-end trade digitalization, and UNCITRAL invites APEC economies to continue to actively engage in shaping the future of digital trade law. Dr. James Ding, Chair of the APEC Economic Committee He stressed that in addition to technology, legal certainty and harmonized frameworks are essential. He also stressed that adoption of international texts and standards could enhance interoperability. These efforts can be critical to supporting MSMEs, enhancing access to credit, and fostering a resilient, future-ready trade ecosystem across the Asia-Pacific. b) Summary of Sessions Session 1: Towards End-to-End Digital Trade Transactions Dr. Alan Davidson, Chair of UNCITRAL Working Group IV and Senior Lecturer at the University of Queensland (Australia) Dr. Davidson highlighted UNCITRAL's long-standing efforts in harmonizing international trade law, noting that the MLEC, adopted by 170 jurisdictions, laid the groundwork for legal certainty in electronic commerce. He further explained that this model law established functional equivalence between electronic and paper documents, ensuring electronic communications and signatures were not denied validity solely because of their medium. Dr. Davidson then focused on newer instruments, particularly the MLETR, which addresses a key challenge: digitizing "documents of title" like bills of lading. Unlike standard electronic documents, these records require transfer of possession to convey rights, and MLETR resolves this by equating electronic "control" to physical possession and by equating transfer of control to physical delivery. He also discussed the MLIT and the MLAC, which address digital identity verification and AI-driven contract formation, respectively. These instruments respond to emerging technologies like blockchain and AI, which were unforeseen when earlier model laws were drafted. Dr. Davidson referenced an APEC report projecting USD 2 trillion in savings over the next decade if the MLETR and related legal instruments are widely adopted, emphasizing the economic rationale behind legal harmonization. Session 3: Digitalization of Trade Finance and Digital Assets Mr. Kobsak Duangdee, Secretary General, Thai Bankers' Association (Thailand) He argued that new technologies —blockchain, APIs, and AI —can enable trusted, seamless data flows across B2B, B2G, and G2G transactions. However, the challenge lies in building interoperability and avoiding a fragmented "spaghetti bowl" of bilateral agreements. He called for adoption of international standards, notably the MLETR and the Framework Agreement on Facilitation of Cross-border Paperless Trade in Asia and the Pacific (CPTA), along with digital identity systems, to create legitimacy and trust. Session 4: Issues arising from Dispute Resolution in the Digital Economy (DRDE) Mr. Kazuaki Takahashi, Attorney, International Affairs Division, Ministry of Justice (Japan) The DRDE project emerged from a proposal submitted by Japan amid the COVID-19 pandemic, which underscored the urgent need for legal frameworks to adapt to the rapid digitalization of global trade and commerce. Since December 2021, the UNCITRAL secretariat has been conducting a comprehensive DRDE stocktaking exercise to explore the impact of digital technologies and technology-enabled services on dispute resolution, with a view to identifying whether there is a need to update existing instruments, or to develop new ones as well as to suggest potential solutions. Mr. Jae Sung Park, Prosecutor, International Legal Affairs Policy Division, Korea Ministry of Justice (Republic of Korea) Article 4 of the New York Convention requires parties seeking enforcement to submit a "duly authenticated original award" or a certified copy, but this provision predates digital advancements, creating ambiguity about whether electronically issued awards qualify. To resolve this, UNCITRAL Working Group II is exploring three potential solutions. First, issuing a recommendation to interpret the New York Convention as encompassing electronic awards within the definition of "original award." This approach is favored for its practicality, as it avoids the complexity of treaty revision, though it lacks binding force. Second, revising the UNCITRAL Model Law on International Commercial Arbitration to provide explicit guidance on electronic arbitral awards, which would rely on domestic adoption to take effect. Third, amending the New York Convention or developing a new protocol —a more impactful but time-consuming option, as treaty revisions require ratification by member states and risk creating a two-tier system between adopters and non-adopters. Ms. Teresa Rodriguez de las Heras Ballell, Professor, Universidad Carlos III de Madrid (Spain) Platforms are described as contract-based organizational models, formed through agreements between platform operators and users, which may include businesses, consumers, or non-professional users. These agreements govern all relationships and activities within the platform, making the operator a regulator and supervisor, and potentially a provider or facilitator of dispute resolution mechanisms. On AI and automation, in the context of platform-based dispute resolution, there is a need to consider the extent to which the automation and artificial intelligence (AI) systems can be used. Drawing from existing principles on automated decision-making, three aspects are particularly relevant: whether it is explainable, whether it has proper reasoning, and whether it is subject to judicial review. Mr. Danny Ong, Managing Director, Setia Law (Singapore) Mr. Ong pointed out that digital assets —such as cryptocurrencies —do not fit neatly into traditional legal categories of "property" or "tangible assets," creating ambiguity in their enforceability. This ambiguity is compounded by jurisdictional differences: common law jurisdictions like Hong Kong, China and Singapore, often rely on the concept of "control" to determine rights over digital assets, while other jurisdictions may not recognize such assets as legally enforceable collateral or subject to seizure, undermining cross-border enforcement. Mr. Ong concluded by suggesting that these issues could be addressed through a new UNCITRAL Model Law on Digital Assets Enforcement, enabling consistent and effective cross-border enforcement practices. d) Conclusion Harmonized legal framework such as UNCITRAL texts could be useful reference in the whole trade lifecycle to enable "end-to-end" digitalization of trade, including paperless processes, digital collateral & cross-border enforcement, with legal certainty. Besides, international collaboration is important to facilitate MSMEs to achieve economic potential and meet APEC's digital transformation goals. Looking ahead, economies are encouraged to — a) consider making use of the international instruments to align domestic regimes with international standards; b) strengthen capacity building to engage MSMEs, trade platforms and policymakers across borders; and c) leverage technology advancement taking into account interoperability, the need for trusted data and digital capabilities to support digital trade.
impact: 研讨会聚焦于国际文书在整个业务生命周期中的实际应用，得出结论，统一的法律框架如UNCITRAL文本可作为促进贸易“端到端”数字化的有用参考。此外，国际合作对于促进中小微企业实现经济潜力和实现亚太经合组织数字化转型目标也非常重要。
impactEn: Focusing on practical applications of international instruments through the whole business lifecycle, the Workshop concluded that harmonized legal framework such as UNCITRAL texts could be useful reference to enable “end-to-end” digitalization of trade. Besides, international collaboration is important to facilitate MSMEs to achieve economic potential and meet APEC’s digital transformation goals.

en: APEC Data for Growth High-level Roundtable Chair’s Statement
cn: APEC增长数据高级别圆桌会议主席声明
summary: 亚太经济合作组织数据促增长高级别圆桌会议于2026年7月25日在中国四川成都举行。亚太经济合作组织各成员经济体重申我们在《2040年亚太经合组织布城愿景》下的共同承诺，到2040年建设一个开放、充满活力、具有韧性且和平的亚太共同体，为我们所有人民和子孙后代的繁荣而努力。我们认识到数字技术为促进创新、提高生产力和推动经济增长带来了重大机遇，以及数据在支持数字技术发展中的重要作用。我们认识到加强区域合作以增强数据可用性、消除数字服务壁垒和支持数据利用的重要性。我们还认识到亚太经济合作组织自愿的、非约束性的、凝聚共识的原则。为更好地发挥数据在创新、生产力和经济增长方面的价值，并促进各成员经济体之间的合作，包括反映各成员经济体多样化需求的合作，我们致力于： 一、培育数据获取和使用的开放与有利环境 ——加强政策对话，包括通过现有机制和自愿经验交流，促进数据的使用、互操作性、可及性和应用，同时确保信任、安全、数据保护和隐私，并尊重知识产权。 ——支持有利的政策环境以促进创新和市场信心。我们还将致力于促进跨境数据流动，同时增强企业和消费者信任。 ——鼓励多方利益相关者参与，包括政策制定者、监管机构和企业参与数据治理，以促进自愿信息共享和不同数据治理方式之间的互操作性。 二、加强数据驱动创新与应用 ——促进数据的负责任使用，以支持科学研究、技术创新、产业发展和公共服务现代化。培育数据驱动的创新和经济增长，并推动新兴技术的商业化和应用，以发挥其变革潜力。 ——支持提升数字技能和创新能力，使微型、小型和中型企业以及社会各阶层的相关利益相关者能够更好地利用数字工具和数据资源促进创新和经济增长，包括通过能力建设和自愿分享信息和最佳实践。 三、深化数据互联互通合作 ——推进关于发展可靠、可及、可扩展、可信、安全和具有韧性的数据基础设施的对话，提高各数据系统之间的互操作性，以减少碎片化、避免不必要的数据孤岛，并促进区域内数据资源的价值创造。 ——加强关于跨境数据政策的沟通与对话，以促进各成员经济体之间的理解与信任。 ——支持企业、研究机构和其他利益相关者通过经验分享和能力建设活动就相关问题开展合作，以最大化为我们的人民实现数字化的收益。 结论 我们相信，通过持续的对话与合作，亚太经济合作组织能够更好地发挥数据在推动亚太地区经济增长中的作用。鼓励各成员经济体继续在此方面交流经验、最佳实践和所取得的进展，并在亚太经济合作组织框架下探索潜在的合作领域，包括通过数字经济指导组及其下属的数据隐私小组等。
summaryEn: The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Data for Growth High-level Roundtable was held in Chengdu, Sichuan, China on July 25, 2026. APEC member economies reaffirm our shared commitment under the APEC Putrajaya Vision 2040 to build an open, dynamic, resilient and peaceful Asia-Pacific community by 2040, for the prosperity of all our people and future generations. We recognize that digital technologies present significant opportunities to foster innovation, enhance productivity, and promote economic growth and the vital role of data in supporting the development of digital technologies. We recognize the importance of strengthening regional cooperation to enhance the availability of data, remove barriers to digital services, and support data utilization. We also recognize the voluntary, non-binding, consensus-building principles of APEC. To better harness the value of data for innovation, productivity and economic growth, and to promote cooperation among member economies, including those that reflect the diverse needs of member economies, we endeavor to: I. Foster an Open and Enabling Environment for Data Access and Use — Strengthen policy dialogue, including through existing mechanisms, and the voluntary exchange of experiences, and promote the use, interoperability, accessibility and application of data while ensuring trust, security, data protection and privacy, and respect for intellectual property rights. — Support an enabling policy environment to boost innovation and market confidence. We will also work to facilitate cross-border data flows, while strengthening business and consumer trust. — Encourage multistakeholder engagement, including with policymakers, regulators, and businesses on data governance, with a view to promoting voluntary information sharing and interoperability across different approaches to data governance. II. Strengthen Data-Driven Innovation and Application — Facilitate the responsible use of data to support scientific research, technological innovation, industrial development and public service modernization. Foster data-driven innovation and economic growth, and promote the commercialization and application of emerging technologies, to harness its transformative potential. — Support the enhancement of digital skills and innovation capabilities, enabling MSMEs and relevant stakeholders in all segments of our societies to better utilize digital tools and data resources to foster innovation and economic growth, including through capacity building and the voluntary sharing of information and best practices. III. Deepen Cooperation on Data Connectivity — Advance dialogue on the development of reliable, accessible, scalable, trusted, secure and resilient data infrastructure and improve interoperability among data systems to reduce fragmentation, avoid unnecessary data silos, and facilitate value creation of data resources across the region. — Enhance communication and dialogues on cross-border data policies to foster understanding and trust among member economies. — Support collaboration among businesses, research institutions and other stakeholders on relevant issues through experience-sharing and capacity building activities, to maximize the benefits of digitalization for our people. Conclusion We believe that, through sustained dialogue and cooperation, APEC can better harness the role of data in driving economic growth across the Asia-Pacific region. Member economies are encouraged to continue to exchange experiences, best practices and progress made in this regard, and explore potential areas of cooperation under the APEC framework, including through the Digital Economy Steering Group (DESG) and its subgroup the Data Privacy Subgroup (DPS), among others.

en: APEC Economies Advance AI Standards for Trust and Innovation
cn: 亚太经合组织经济体推动信任与创新的人工智能标准
summary: 随着人工智能重塑亚太地区的经济和社会，亚太经济合作组织正在加大力度确保这一转型是安全的、包容的和可持续的。100多名政策制定者、技术专家和标准专家齐聚仁川，参加亚太经济合作组织人工智能标准会议，以推动区域内人工智能治理和技术趋同。 韩国技术与标准院院长裴珍硕博士表示："人工智能带来了巨大的机遇，也带来了任何单一经济体都无法独自应对的复杂挑战。" 裴博士补充道："人工智能正在迅速改变我们的产业和日常生活，但如果没有共同标准，我们面临碎片化和不信任的风险。这次会议为亚太经济合作组织各经济体协调努力、交流知识、支持国际合作提供了机会，以塑造安全、包容且具有前瞻性的人工智能治理。" 国际标准化组织副秘书长西尔维奥·杜林斯基在会议开幕式上强调了国际标准在建立人工智能信任、公平和安全方面的作用。他强调，标准提供了可扩展的、以共识为驱动的工具，用于协调监管并确保人工智能治理的多样性和包容性。 国际标准化组织和国际电工委员会人工智能联合技术委员会主席威尔·威廉·迪亚卜强调了同时应对人工智能技术和社会层面的重要性。迪亚卜指出，为国内产业和监管机构进行能力建设非常重要，并强调全球人工智能标准仍在发展中，现在积极参与的经济体可以帮助塑造未来。 与会者讨论了跨行业的人工智能应用案例，审查了指导测试、合格评定和实施的新兴框架，并审查了人工智能标准在伦理、人机交互、风险管理和环境影响等领域的实际应用。 负责监督该倡议的亚太经济合作组织标准与合格评定分委会主席姜炳九博士总结道："标准化不仅仅是一个技术过程，它是可持续创新和包容性增长的基础。" "我们希望这次研讨会为亚太经济合作组织各经济体在人工智能标准方面的合作提供了机会。通过共同努力，亚太经济合作组织各经济体可以确保人工智能系统不仅有效，而且与我们的共同价值观保持一致。"
summaryEn: As artificial intelligence (AI) reshapes economies and societies across the Asia-Pacific, APEC is stepping up efforts to ensure this transformation is safe, inclusive and sustainable. More than 100 policymakers, technologists and standards experts convened in Incheon for the APEC AI Standards Conference to drive convergence in AI governance and technical alignment across the region. "AI presents both enormous opportunities and complex challenges that no single economy can resolve alone," said Dr Jin-seok Bae, Director of the Korean Agency for Technology and Standards (KATS), which hosted the conference. "AI is rapidly transforming our industries and daily lives, but without common standards, we risk fragmentation and mistrust," Dr Bae added. "This conference is a chance for APEC economies to align efforts, exchange knowledge and support international cooperation to shape safe, inclusive and forward-looking AI governance." Speaking at the opening session of the conference, Silvio Dulinski, Deputy Secretary General of the International Organization for Standardization (ISO), highlighted the role of international standards in building trust, fairness and security in AI. He emphasized that standards offer scalable, consensus-driven tools for aligning regulation and ensuring diversity and inclusion in AI governance. Wael William Diab, Chair of the ISO and IEC's Joint Technical Committee on Artificial Intelligence underscored the importance of addressing both technical and societal dimensions of AI. Diab noted the importance of capacity building for domestic industries and regulators, highlighting that global AI standards are still evolving and economies that actively engage now can help shape the future. Participants discussed AI use cases across sectors and examined emerging frameworks to guide testing, conformity assessment and implementation and examined real-world applications of AI standards in areas such as ethics, human-AI interaction, risk management and environmental impact. "Standardization is not just a technical process, it is a foundation for sustainable innovation and inclusive growth," concluded Dr Kang Byung-Goo, Chair of the APEC Sub-Committee on Standards and Conformance (SCSC), which oversees the initiative. "We hope that the workshop provided an opportunity for collaboration among APEC economies on AI standards. By working together, APEC economies can ensure AI systems are not only effective, but also aligned with our shared values."

en: 2025 APEC Digital and AI Ministerial Statement
cn: 2025年亚太经济合作组织数字与人工智能部长声明
summary: 引言 3. 今天，我们正目睹数字技术以前所未有的程度融入我们的日常生活和社会。人工智能等技术，以及通过可及的宽带连接实现的数字基础设施和智能网络，将成为数字化转型的关键驱动力，对企业运营方式以及人们在经济中的互动和运作方式产生深远影响。 4. 我们相信，此类数字技术具有巨大潜力，能够赋能我们的人民和企业，提高各领域的效率、生产力和互操作性，并彻底改变公共和私人服务。在认识到数字化转型潜力的同时，我们也注意到技术应以负责任的方式使用，以促进所有人的可持续增长，增进全体人民的福祉，并降低风险——包括与安全、信任、可靠性和可及性相关的风险——同时响应各经济体的具体需求。 促进数字与人工智能创新以应对社会经济挑战 7. 我们鼓励各成员经济体利用信息通信和数字技术（如人工智能）抓住增长机遇，同时注意到这些技术的采用需要对我们的人力资源、教育和能力建设政策采取积极的、平衡的、以人为本的方法，包括终身学习计划，以兼顾其带来的益处和挑战。我们支持在信息通信和数字政策方面开展合作和信息共享，以加速区域经济合作并促进跨境贸易和投资。我们还鼓励各成员经济体加强合作，增进和促进各经济体最新信息通信和数字技术发展的益处。 增强全民数字互联互通 8. 我们认识到，随着信息通信和数字技术对各经济体日益重要，普惠且有意义的数字互联互通比以往任何时候都更为重要。我们特别强调需要弥合各经济体内部和之间的数字鸿沟——包括阻碍个人充分参与数字经济的数字鸿沟。因此，我们强调深化各成员经济体之间合作和能力建设努力的价值，以应对持续的数字鸿沟，包括通过推行培养数字能力和促进创新的政策，使我们所有的人民和经济体都能充分参与数字经济并从中受益。 创建安全、可靠和可信的数字与人工智能生态系统 10. 我们认识到，随着数字化转型的推进，确保安全、保障、可及性、可信度和可靠性是实现数字化惠及所有人的关键。我们强调制定健全的政策和风险管理策略的重要性，以保护企业、个人和劳动者免受各种数字威胁，并增强对数字和人工智能生态系统的信任和信心，从而充分利用最新信息通信和数字技术带来的机遇。为实现这些目标，我们支持各成员经济体继续开展工作，增强信息通信和数字技术（如人工智能）使用中的信任、安全、公平和信心，以及知识和信息的传播。我们还将继续合作促进数据流动，并增强消费者和企业在数字交易中的信任。 结论 13. 随着2025年《互联网与数字经济路线图》实施工作计划即将完成，我们认识到需要系统地制定一种方法，以在2025年之后继续推进该路线图的目标，以应对快速演变的数字格局中出现的新挑战和机遇。我们鼓励各成员经济体利用适用的数字治理机制促进对话，以推进亚太经济合作组织的目标，并承诺探索协作方法，确保信息通信和数字创新造福我们的人民和地区。在此方面，我们赞赏在韩国领导下于年底前制定亚太经济合作组织人工智能倡议的正在进行的工作。
summaryEn: Introduction 4. We believe that such digital technologies offer enormous potential to empower our people and businesses to improve efficiency, productivity and interoperability in various sectors, and revolutionize private and public services. While recognizing the potential of digital transformation, we also note that technology should be used responsibly to promote sustainable growth for all, enhance the well-being of all our people, and mitigate risks - including those related to safety, trust, reliability and accessibility - while being responsive to the specific needs of individual economies. Facilitating Digital and AI Innovation to Address Socio-economic Challenges 7. We encourage member economies to harness growth opportunities by leveraging ICT and digital technologies such as AI, mindful that adoption of these technologies requires a proactive, balanced, and human-centered approach to our workforce, education, and capacity-building policies, including lifelong learning initiatives, in light of both the benefits and the challenges they present. We support cooperation and information sharing on the ICT and digital policies that accelerate regional economic cooperation and facilitate cross border trade and investment. We also encourage member economies to collaborate toward greater understanding and promotion of the benefits of the latest developments in ICT and digital technologies in each of our economies. Enhancing Digital Connectivity for All 8. We recognize that as ICT and digital technologies become increasingly essential to our economies, universal and meaningful digital connectivity is more important than ever. In particular, we highlight the need to bridge digital divides within and between economies - including the digital divides that hinder individuals' full participation in the digital economy. We therefore emphasize the value of deepening cooperation and capacity-building efforts among member economies to address persistent digital divides, including by promoting policies that build digital competencies and advance innovation, so that all our people and economies can fully participate in, and benefit from, the digital economy. Creating a Safe, Secure and Reliable Digital and AI Ecosystem 10. We recognize that as digital transformation advances, ensuring safety, security, accessibility, trustworthiness and reliability are key to realizing the benefits of digitalization for all. We emphasize the importance of developing robust policy and risk management strategies to protect business, individuals and workers from a range of digital threats and to strengthen trust and confidence in digital and AI ecosystems so that the opportunities offered by the latest ICT and digital technologies are fully leveraged. In line with these objectives, we support continued work among member economies to enhance trust, safety, fairness and confidence in the use of ICT and digital technologies such as AI, as well as the dissemination of knowledge and information. We will also continue our cooperation on facilitating the flow of data and strengthening consumer and business trust in digital transactions. Conclusion 13. As we approach the completion of the Work Program for the Implementation of AIDER in 2025, we recognize the need to systematically develop an approach for the continued advancement of AIDER's objective beyond 2025, in a way that addresses emerging challenges and opportunities in the rapidly evolving digital landscape. We encourage member economies to utilize applicable digital governance mechanisms to promote dialogue that advances the objectives of APEC, and commit to exploring collaborative approaches to ensure the use of ICT and digital innovations for the benefit of our people and the region. In this regard, we commend the work underway to develop an APEC AI initiative, under the leadership of Korea, by the end of the year.
