en: Emerging Approaches for Measuring and Estimating Digital Trade
cn: 衡量和估算数字贸易的新兴方法
summary: 一、引言 我们经济的数字化持续改变着我们交易的内容和方式。许多服务的数字可交付性和电子商务平台的激增，使亚太经济合作组织地区消费者和企业之间实现了前所未有的跨境活力和互联互通。这持续刺激数字和传统产业的增长，降低贸易成本，并推动促进数字贸易有利环境的政策发展。以往的工作估计，2020年亚太经济合作组织内部数字贸易达到2.12万亿美元，占区域内贸易总额的28%。 然而，数字贸易数据的可用性未能跟上步伐。与数字经济的许多方面一样，捕捉数字贸易数据的统计方法仍在发展中。近年来在建立跨境数字贸易统计的国际统一概念框架方面取得了进展。然而，各经济体的数据制约因素通常阻碍了"一刀切"的方法，往往需要创新性和有针对性的方法来收集、编制和应用数据。数字贸易的快速演变性质也意味着，随着新数据来源和方法论的出现以及政策讨论的推进，测量和估算方法也在不断演变。 随着数字交易对国际贸易日益重要，提高数字贸易数据的可用性对于为理解、分析和政策制定提供信息至关重要。这对于支持《2040年亚太经济合作组织布城愿景》和《亚太经济合作组织奥特亚罗瓦行动计划》的实施也至关重要，通过促进有效措施、互操作性方法的发展以及数字技术的采用来便利亚太经济合作组织地区的贸易和投资。 二、测量数字贸易 2.2 测量数字贸易的挑战 尽管已建立了数字贸易的概念测量框架，但编制全面的数字贸易数据仍然具有挑战性，部分原因是它加剧了国际交易中涉及的若干测量挑战。一个关键挑战是，国际贸易统计传统上是围绕"什么"被交易来编制的——即货物或服务是什么。虽然这对数字贸易分析仍然有意义，但定义数字贸易交易的重点最终在于"如何"购买或交付，这传统上在海关数据或企业调查等贸易数据来源中未得到充分记录。数字订购的增长也导致了低值货物贸易的快速增长，当货物贸易测量基于较高的价值门槛时，这可能带来进一步挑战。 数字化也改变了国际贸易中的参与主体。它使家庭作为海外直接购买者的参与度大幅提高，也使家庭和小企业作为卖方的参与度大幅提高。这些主体在传统数据来源中往往代表性不足，传统数据来源通常聚焦于大型企业。数字化还导致在线购物平台和数字中介平台的作用迅速上升，这些平台以收费方式促进货物和服务的交易，是以数字方式订购的贸易的关键促进者。这可能通过在交易中增加第三方而进一步使测量复杂化，该第三方可能不居住在买方或卖方经济体，且其数据通常不易获取。 尽管存在这些挑战，以往的工作表明，当前货物或服务的国际贸易统计并未显著低估数字贸易的规模，尽管这可能因经济体而异。相反，主要测量挑战在于识别以数字方式订购或交付的交易，并在贸易统计中使这些数字贸易更加可见。这对于更好地测量和理解现有国际贸易流量中以数字方式订购或以数字方式交付的组成部分至关重要。 三、近期数字贸易测量和估算方法 3.1 国际组织的工作 近年来，已开发了一系列旨在解决数字贸易常见数据挑战的方法论和方法。虽然各经济体的底层数据制约、方法论挑战和不同的数据可用性意味着每种方法都有局限性，但这些经验为希望改善数字贸易数据的分析人员和政策制定者提供了宝贵的信息、示例和工具。 自数字贸易政策早期以来，经济合作与发展组织和世界贸易组织等国际组织在引领这些方法和数据集的开发方面发挥了关键作用。如前所述，由经济合作与发展组织、世界贸易组织和国际货币基金组织编制的《数字贸易测量手册》建立了定义和测量数字贸易的概念框架，并为许多国际组织近期的研究工作奠定了基础。一个共同的起点是估算以数字方式交付的服务贸易。由于以数字方式交付的贸易是各经济体服务贸易的子集，而服务贸易的国际可比数据集通常按经济体层面产生和提供，世界贸易组织和联合国贸易和发展会议均发布了公开的跨经济体估算数据。 展望未来，编制国民统计账户和国际收支统计的国际框架近期更新将有助于未来几年数字贸易测量方法的发展。《2025年国民账户体系》和《第七版国际收支手册》均于2025年3月经联合国统计委员会通过，旨在确保核心宏观经济统计反映数字化等领域的最新发展。这包括改进对数字经济的核心方面（如数据、人工智能、电子商务、云计算和数字中介平台）的测量。新标准的目标实施时间为2029-2030年，最佳实践指南将在未来几年发布。 四、经验教训和建议 随着数字贸易的测量和估算方法不断发展，通过分享方法论可以学到很多。本文概述的经验表明，虽然编制全面的数字贸易统计可能仍是一个中长期目标，但亚太经济合作组织各经济体可以通过利用现有数据来源和统计方法取得实际进展。在许多情况下，即使是部分的或替代性的数字贸易估算，也为各经济体提供了关于跨境数字贸易规模和性质的重要见解，对数字贸易政策的制定和理解具有价值。 根据本文概述的案例研究，可以为寻求开发数字贸易数据的经济体和政府主管部门总结出若干经验教训： • 从现有数据来源和基础设施开始——虽然开发新数据来源可能资源密集，但在许多情况下，通过利用和调整现有数据和调查可以取得进展。这些现有来源可以提供部分或替代性指标，在其他数据来源开发的同时改善数字交付和数字订购在国际贸易中的数据可用性。例如，一些经济体已在现有的国际服务贸易调查或信息通信技术获取和使用调查中引入问题，以更好地识别跨境数字交易。同样，税务机关、海关机构和其他经济机构持有的行政数据集为家庭和企业的数字贸易活动提供了有用的见解。 • 充分利用国际组织提供的资源和框架——经济合作与发展组织、世界贸易组织和联合国贸易和发展会议等国际组织近年来在开发数字贸易的共同概念和测量框架方面做了大量工作。虽然各经济体的情况不同，但采纳这些定义和概念可以为统计工作计划提供有价值的框架和方向。同样重要的是，确保各经济体内部开发的数字贸易数据在采用不同方法应对共同数据挑战时保持国际一致性和可比性。国际组织提供的资源，如跨经济体数据集、调查设计的示范问题和模块、以及指南和研究，对于资源有限的政府也很有价值。 • 跨政府合作与私营部门参与很重要——鉴于数字贸易涉及的经济活动和参与者的广泛性，在公共和私营部门利益相关方之间进行广泛参与很有价值。对于公共部门利益相关方，协作工作计划有助于识别可能的数据来源、政策兴趣和资源。同时，与企业行业协会的参与可以为调查问卷的有效设计、数据收集方法和指南材料的清晰度提供有价值的信息。鉴于数字贸易统计的相对新近性以及各方对数字贸易定义和概念熟悉程度的发展，这一点尤为重要。 • 数字贸易的性质本身适合渐进式数据开发——在许多情况下，各经济体将改善数字贸易数据作为渐进式工作计划，逐步开发数字贸易不同方面的数据。通常，初始重点是改善数字交付服务贸易数据，因为利用现有国际服务贸易数据的能力使其成为自然的起点。而与数字订购贸易、数字中介平台和家庭活动相关的更普遍的方法论挑战意味着这些领域的数据范围和粒度往往是随着时间推移而逐步解决的。 • 需要持续关注数字贸易数据开发以支持全面和可靠的统计——虽然近年来数字贸易数据开发取得了很大进展，但即使对于拥有相对先进数据生态系统的经济体而言，它仍然是一个持续工作和新兴最佳实践的领域。这表明虽然"早期胜利"是可能的，但改善数字贸易统计的质量和覆盖面最好通过持续的长期努力来支持。这包括开发国内数据来源以及国际分享专业知识和支持协作方法以增强数字贸易的测量和估算。 随着亚太经济合作组织各经济体继续开发必要的数据来源以产生数字贸易估算和测量，亚太经济合作组织作为一个论坛可以在分享专业知识、支持能力建设和增强数据集之间的可比性方面发挥关键作用。支持各经济体之间的对话和分享实践经验仍然很有价值，因为亚太经济合作组织各经济体数据开发水平不同，意味着跨经济体分享经验和专业知识仍有很多可以获得的。同样，保持亚太经济合作组织与经济合作与发展组织、世界贸易组织和联合国贸易和发展会议等国际组织之间的对话很重要，以保持与国际框架的一致性并了解开发国际数据集和统计框架的更广泛工作。 亚太经济合作组织还提供了一个有价值的论坛，以推进更好地了解亚太经济合作组织各经济体现有和潜在数字贸易数据来源的合作和进一步工作。虽然本项目试图突出若干经济体的案例研究，但对亚太经济合作组织数字贸易数据格局的更深入了解将支持讨论现有更好地使用、开发和报告数字贸易数据的机会。这反过来将为亚太经济合作组织内部旨在消除壁垒和促进跨境数字贸易的政策制定提供信息。未来的工作可以编制亚太经济合作组织各经济体数字贸易数据实践的更完整图景，以及更好地了解可由统计机构调整以更好捕捉数字贸易数据的常见统计调查，如国际服务贸易调查或信息通信技术获取和使用调查。编制这一数据格局的更清晰图景将支持为亚太经济合作组织各经济体制定未来指南和建议，并促进改善亚太经济合作组织地区完整、可比和定期数字贸易数据可用性的可能路径。
summaryEn: 1. Introduction The digitalisation of our economies continues to transform what and how we trade. The digital deliverability of many services and the proliferation of e-commerce platforms has enabled an unprecedented degree of cross-border dynamism and connectivity between consumers and businesses across the APEC region. This continues to stimulate growth in both digital and traditional industries, lower trade costs, and incentivise policy development to foster an enabling environment for digital trade. Past work has estimated that intra-APEC digital trade reached USD 2.12 trillion in 2020, comprising 28% of total intra-regional trade. However, the availability of data on digital trade has not kept pace. As with many aspects of the digital economy, statistical approaches for capturing data on digital trade are still developing. Progress has been made in recent years with the establishment of an internationally agreed conceptual framework for cross-border digital trade statistics. However, data constraints within economies typically prevents a "one size fits all" approach, and innovative and targeted approaches are often needed to collect, compile, and apply data. The fast-evolving nature of digital trade also means that measurement and estimation approaches are evolving as new data sources and methodologies emerge and policy discussions progress. As digital transactions become increasingly important for international trade, improving the availability of digital trade data is crucial to inform understanding, analysis, and policy development. It is also essential to support implementation of the APEC Putrajaya Vision 2040 and APEC's Aotearoa Plan of Action by contributing to the development of effective measures, interoperable approaches, and the adoption of digital technologies to facilitate trade and investment across the APEC region. 2. measuring digital trade 2.2 Challenges measuring digital trade Despite the establishment of a conceptual measurement framework for digital trade, compiling comprehensive data on digital trade remains challenging, partly because it exacerbates several measurement challenges involved in international transactions. A key challenge is that international trade statistics have traditionally been compiled around "what" is being traded —that is, what the good or service is. While this remains of interest for digital trade analysis, the focus for defining a digital trade transaction is ultimately on "how" it is purchased or delivered, which has traditionally not been well captured in trade data sources such as customs data or business surveys. The growth of digital ordering has also seen a rapid rise in low-value trade in goods, which can present further challenges where measurement of merchandise trade is based on higher value thresholds. Digitalisation has also transformed the actors involved in international trade. It has enabled significantly higher participation by households as direct purchasers from overseas, as well as households and small businesses as sellers. These actors have tended to be underrepresented in traditional data sources, which have typically focused on large firms. Digitalisation has also resulted in a rapid rise in the role of online shopping platforms and digital intermediation platforms, which facilitate transactions in goods and services for a fee and are key facilitators of digitally ordered trade. This can further complicate measurement by adding a third party to the transaction which may not be resident in the buyer's or seller's economies and for which data is typically not readily available. Despite these challenges, past work has suggested that current international trade statistics for goods or services do not significantly undervalue the amount of digital trade, although this may vary across economies. Rather, the main measurement challenge lies in identifying the transactions that are digitally ordered or delivered and making this digital trade more visible within trade statistics. This is essential for better measuring and understanding the component of existing international trade flows that are being digitally ordered or digitally delivered. 3. Recent digital trade measurement & estimation approaches 3.1 Work by international organisations In recent years, a range of methodologies and approaches have been developed that aim to address some of the common data challenges surrounding digital trade. Although underlying data constraints, methodological challenges, and varied data availability across economies mean that each approach has limitations, these experiences provide valuable information, examples, and tools that can be emulated or learned from by analysts and policymakers wanting to improve data on digital trade. Since the early days of digital trade policy, international organisations such as the OECD and the WTO have played a critical role in leading the development of these approaches and datasets. As mentioned, the 'Handbook on Measuring Digital Trade' produced by the OECD, WTO, and IMF established a conceptual framework for defining and measuring digital trade and has provided the foundation for more recent research efforts by many international organisations. A common starting point has been estimating trade in digitally delivered services. As digitally delivered trade is a subset of economies' trade in services, for which internationally comparable datasets are routinely produced and available at an economy level, the WTO and UNCTAD both publish publicly available cross-economy estimates. Looking ahead, recent updates to the international frameworks for compiling national statistical accounts and balance of payments statistics should further support development of digital trade measures over coming years. The '2025 System of National Accounts' and '7th Edition Balance of Payments Manual', both adopted by the UN Statistical Commission in March 2025, have been developed to ensure core macroeconomic statistics reflect recent developments in areas like digitalisation. This includes improvements to better measure fundamental aspects of the digital economy, such as data, AI, e-commerce, cloud computing, and digital intermediation platforms. Implementation of the new standards is aimed for 2029-2030, with best practice guidelines to be released in coming years. 4. Lessons learned & recommendations As measurement and estimation approaches for digital trade continue to develop, there is much that can be learnt by sharing methodologies. The experiences outlined in this paper demonstrate that while the production of comprehensive digital trade statistics is likely to remain a medium-to-long term goal, practical progress can be made by APEC economies by using existing data sources and statistical approaches. In many cases, even partial or proxy estimates of digital trade have provided economies with important insights about the scale and nature of cross-border digital trade that have been valuable to inform digital trade policy and understanding. Based on the case studies outlined in this paper, a number of lessons can be drawn for economies and government authorities seeking to develop digital trade data: • Begin with existing data sources and infrastructure – While developing new data sources can be resource intensive, in many cases progress can be made by leveraging and adapting existing data and surveys. These existing sources can provide partial or proxy indicators to improve the availability of data on digital delivery and digital ordering in international trade as other data sources are developed. For example, several economies have introduced questions to existing International Trade in Services Surveys or ICT Access and Use Surveys to better identify digitally enabled cross-border transactions. Similarly, administrative datasets held by tax authorities, customs agencies, and other economic agencies have provided useful insights on digital trade activities by households and businesses. • Make the most of the resources and frameworks offered by international organisations – Significant work has been done by international organisations such as the OECD, WTO, and UNCTAD in recent years to develop a shared conceptual and measurement framework for digital trade. Although circumstances for individual economies vary, adopting these definitions and concepts can provide a valuable framework and direction for statistical work programmes. It is also important to ensure that digital trade data developed within individual economies' remains internationally coherent and comparable as different approaches are adopted for addressing common data challenges. Resources provided by international organisations such as cross-economy datasets, model questions and modules for survey design, and guidance and research are also valuable for governments with more limited resources. • Cross-government collaboration and engagement with the private sector is important – Given the breadth of economic activity and the actors involved in digital trade, broad engagement across both public and private sector stakeholders can be valuable. For public sector stakeholders, a collaborative work programme can help to identify possible data sources, policy interests, and resources. Meanwhile, engagement with businesses and industry organisations can be valuable to inform the effective design of survey questions, data collection approaches, and the clarity of guidance material. This can be particularly important given the relative newness of digital trade statistics and as familiarity with digital trade definitions and concepts develop. • The nature of digital trade can lend itself towards an incremental approach to data development – In many cases, economies have approached the improvement of digital trade data as an incremental work programme, developing data on different aspects of digital trade gradually over time. Typically, an initial focus has been on improving digitally delivered services trade data as the ability to use existing international trade in services data makes it a natural starting point. Whereas the more prevalent methodological challenges associated with digitally ordered trade, digital intermediation platforms, and the activities of households mean that the scope and granularity of data efforts in these areas have tended to be addressed over time. • A consistent focus on developing digital trade data is needed to support comprehensive and robust statistics – While much progress has been made in the development of digital trade data in recent years, it remains an area of ongoing work and emerging best practice even for economies with relatively advanced data ecosystems. This suggests that while "early wins" are possible, improving the quality and coverage of digital trade statistics can best be supported by a sustained long-term effort. This includes the development of domestic data sources as well as international efforts to share expertise and support collaborative approaches to enhance the measurement and estimation of digital trade. As APEC economies continue to develop the data sources necessary to produce estimates and measures of digital trade, APEC as a forum can play a critical role in sharing expertise, supporting capacity building, and enhancing comparability across datasets. Supporting dialogue between economies and sharing practical experiences remains valuable, as varied levels of data development across APEC economies means there is still a lot to be gained from sharing lessons and expertise across economies. Similarly, maintaining dialogue between APEC and international organisations such as the OECD, WTO, and UNCTAD is important to maintain coherence with international frameworks and to stay informed of wider work to develop international datasets and statistical frameworks. APEC also provides a valuable forum to advance collaboration and further work to better understand existing and potential digital trade data sources across APEC economies. While this project has sought to highlight case studies from a number of economies, a deeper understanding of the digital trade data landscape across APEC would support discussions on opportunities that exist to better use, develop, and report digital trade data. This in turn would inform policy development within APEC aimed at removing barriers and promoting cross-border digital trade. Future work could compile a more complete picture of digital trade data practices in APEC economies along with a better understanding of common statistical surveys, such as international trade in services surveys or ICT access and use surveys that could be adapted by statistics agencies to better capture data on digital trade. Compiling a clearer picture of this data landscape would support the development of future guidance and recommendations for APEC economies, as well as promote a possible pathway to improve the availability of complete, comparable, and regular digital trade data across the APEC region.
impact: This report explores emerging approaches to measuring and estimating digital trade across APEC economies. It provides an overview of the commonly used conceptual framework for defining digital trade and highlights persistent data gaps and challenges associated with the compilation of digital trade data. The report outlines a number of recent methodological advances and datasets developed by international organisations, including work from the OECD, WTO, and UNCTAD, and presents case studies from selected APEC economies to illustrate how individual economies are developing practical solutions. Drawing on these experiences, it identifies key lessons, such as the value of leveraging existing data and frameworks, fostering cross-sector collaboration, adopting incremental approaches to data development, and promoting international dialogue and collaboration on measurement and estimation approaches.
impactEn: 本报告探讨了亚太经合组织经济体中衡量和估算数字贸易的新兴方法。它概述了定义数字贸易的常用概念框架，并强调了数字贸易数据汇编过程中存在的持续数据缺口和挑战。报告概述了包括经合组织、世贸组织和联合国贸易和发展会议（UNCTAD）在内的多项近期方法学进展和数据集，并展示了部分APEC经济体的案例研究，展示各经济体如何制定切实可行的解决方案。借鉴这些经验，报告指出关键经验教训，如利用现有数据和框架的价值、促进跨部门合作、采用渐进式数据开发方法，以及促进国际间关于测量与估计方法的对话与合作。

en: AI’s Future Depends on the Accessibility of Data: APEC Roundtable
cn: 人工智能的未来取决于数据的可获取性：APEC圆桌会议
summary: 周六在成都举行的“数据促进增长”高级别圆桌会议上，部长们和高级代表强调了数据作为创新、生产力和增长驱动力日益重要的重要性，呼吁加强合作，以释放其在亚太地区的潜力。 圆桌会议开幕时，中国国家数据局局长刘立宏表示，数据已成为基础资源和创新引擎，重塑经济的生产、治理和增长方式。 刘称：“数据为经济和社会发展开辟了新的空间，已经深度融入科研、公共服务和基础设施中。”“数据的价值不断扩大，但如何利用它来赋能发展并造福我们的人民，是我们所有人共同的任务。” 他补充道：“加强围绕增长数据的交流与合作，将有助于进一步丰富APEC数字经济合作。” 讨论强调了在确保数据负责任使用的同时，提高数据的可用性，认识到高质量数据已成为日益由人工智能（AI）驱动的经济中不可或缺的资源。 “数据资源的开发和使用方式多样，没有单一模型适用于所有经济体。开放交流增进理解，经验共享促进互学，务实合作实现共赢，“刘振兴补充道。 讨论强调了互操作性数据治理在增强企业使用和共享数据的信心中的重要性。当数据以安全且负责任的方式融入商业模式和决策时，部长们强调了它如何提升效率、创造力和竞争力。 发言人呼吁不同系统在数据跨区域流动时安全协作，从而加快贸易速度和更具韧性的供应链。 “推进增长数据应成为APEC经济体未来共同努力的重要方向。随着数字技术的不断发展，数据相关问题已超越单一领域，越来越多地涵盖创新、工业、贸易、物流、公共服务及其他多个领域，刘强强调。 与会者还强调了在共享公共数据方面为企业和社会带来益处的实际工作。天气数据是一个关键例子，结合预测AI模型，可以帮助农民保护作物，物流运营商为中断做好准备，紧急服务响应更快。 “数据创造价值，合作释放潜力。刘氏总结道，今天的圆桌会议不是讨论的结束，而是APEC深化围绕增长数据交流与合作、加强政策沟通、分享数字时代益处的新起点。
summaryEn: Ministers and senior representatives at the Data for Growth High-Level Roundtable in Chengdu on Saturday highlighted the growing importance of data as a driver of innovation, productivity and growth, calling for deeper collaboration to unlock its potential across the Asia-Pacific. Opening the roundtable, Liu Liehong, Administrator of China's National Data Administration said data has become a foundational resource and an engine of innovation reshaping how economies produce, govern and grow. “Data is opening new spaces for economic and social development, it is already deeply integrated in scientific research, public services and infrastructures,” Liu said. “The value of data keeps expanding but how to harness it to empower development and benefit our people is a common task for all of us.” “Strengthening exchange and cooperation around data for growth will help further enrich APEC’s digital economy cooperation,” he added. Discussions highlighted the need to make data more accessible while ensuring it is used responsibly, recognizing that high-quality data has become an essential resource for an economy increasingly powered by artificial intelligence (AI). “The ways in which data resources are developed and used are diverse, and no single model is applicable to all economies. Open exchange can enhance understanding, experience-sharing can promote mutual learning, and practical cooperation can deliver win-win outcomes,” Liu added. Discussions underscored the importance of interoperable data governance in giving businesses more confidence to use and share data. When data is integrated into business models and decision-making in a secure and responsible manner, ministers highlighted how it can increase efficiency, creativity and competitiveness. Rather than identical rules, speakers called for different systems to work together securely as data moves across the region, delivering faster trade and more resilient supply chains. “Advancing data for growth should become an important direction for the future joint efforts of APEC economies. As digital technologies continue to develop, data-related issues have moved beyond any single field and increasingly span innovation, industry, trade, logistics, public services and many other areas,” Liu emphasized. Participants also highlighted practical work on sharing public data to deliver benefits for businesses and society. Weather data was one key example, when integrated with predictive AI models, it can help farmers protect crops, logistics operators prepare for disruptions and emergency services respond faster. “Data creates value, and cooperation unlocks potential. Today’s roundtable is not the end of a discussion, but a new starting point for APEC to deepen exchange and cooperation around data for growth to strengthen policy communication and share the benefits of the digital era,” Liu concluded.

en: AI Forum Shifts Focus from Breakthroughs to Adoption
cn: 人工智能论坛将焦点从突破转向采用
summary: 部长、政策制定者、行业代表和学者于周五参加了亚太经合组织人工智能高级别论坛，就人工智能的机遇与挑战展开公开对话。 参与者表示，人工智能面临的下一个挑战不再是开发更强大的模型，而是将技术转化为企业和社区的实际利益。 论坛开幕式上，中国网络空间局部长庄荣文呼吁各国经济体加强合作，支持以开放、安全、以人为本的人工智能（AI）发展。 庄表示：“全球人工智能创新进入了前所未有的活跃时期，带来了重大机遇与现实挑战。”“如何引导人工智能朝着惠及所有人的方向发展，是一个需要APEC经济体之间密切合作的问题。” 在论坛中，发言人强调，人工智能的经济影响将越来越依赖于其采用，而不仅仅是底层技术的进步。 讨论重点包括扩大人工智能工具的可及性、加强数字基础设施、培养技能，以及帮助企业将人工智能融入日常运营，使不同发展阶段的经济体能够从人工智能中受益。 企业领袖指出，人工智能应用涵盖从小城市医疗服务、更安全的交通管理，到面向微型、小型和中型企业（MSMEs）的跨境支付系统。 亚太经合组织秘书处执行董事爱德华多·佩德罗萨在论坛上表示：“人工智能已经在提升生产力，加快研究进程，并为亚太地区的企业创造新机遇。” “虽然APEC经济体在人工智能发展上处于不同阶段，但这种多样性为各国经济体提供了交流经验和相互学习的机会。佩德罗萨补充道，APEC人工智能倡议为各国经济体提供了一个切实可行的框架，共同分享专业知识、建设能力并推动负责任的人工智能发展。 该倡议支持负责任的人工智能、创新、能力建设和技能发展的合作，体现了APEC帮助各国利用人工智能的同时，认可各经济体不同准备水平的做法。 论坛还强调，人工智能的广泛采用将依赖于公众的信任。与会者呼吁人工智能开发者提高透明度，采用互操作性的治理方法，以及政府、产业界和研究人员之间持续合作，以增强对该技术的信心。 “人工智能的发展与治理关系到该地区所有人的未来。所有经济体都需要抓住机遇，共同应对挑战，使人工智能成为积极力量，为建设亚太社区注入持续动力，“庄总结道。 论坛促成了一份关于促进人工智能发展的声明，阐述了继续区域人工智能合作的优先事项。
summaryEn: Ministers, policymakers, industry representatives and academics joined the APEC High-Level Forum on AI on Friday for an open dialogue on the opportunities and challenges of artificial intelligence. Participants said the next challenge for AI is no longer developing more powerful models but translating the technology into real-world benefits for businesses and communities. Opening the forum, China’s Minister of the Cyberspace Administration of China Zhuang Rongwen called for closer cooperation among economies to support artificial intelligence (AI) development that is open, safe and people-centered. "Global innovation in AI has entered an unprecedented period of activity, bringing major opportunities alongside real challenges," said Zhuang. "How to guide AI to develop in a direction that benefits everyone is a question that requires close cooperation between APEC economies." Throughout the forum, speakers highlighted that the economic impact of AI will increasingly depend on its adoption, rather than solely on advances in the underlying technology. Discussions focused on expanding access to AI tools, strengthening digital infrastructure, building skills and helping businesses integrate AI into day-to-day operations so that economies at different stages of development can benefit from AI. Business leaders pointed to AI applications ranging from healthcare access in smaller cities and safer traffic management to cross-border payment systems for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs). “AI is already improving productivity, accelerating research and creating new opportunities for businesses across the Asia-Pacific,” said APEC Secretariat Executive Director Eduardo Pedrosa in his remarks at the forum. “While APEC economies are at different stages of AI development, that diversity is an opportunity for economies to exchange experiences and learn from one another. The APEC Artificial Intelligence Initiative gives economies a practical framework to share expertise, build capability and advance responsible AI together,” Pedrosa added. The initiative supports cooperation on responsible AI, innovation, capacity building and skills development, reflecting APEC’s approach of helping economies harness AI while recognizing their different levels of readiness. The forum also underscored that wider AI adoption will depend on public trust. Participants called for greater transparency from AI developers, interoperable governance approaches and continued cooperation among governments, industry and researchers to build confidence in the technology. "The development and governance of AI concerns the future of all within the region. All economies need to seize opportunities and address challenges together, so that AI becomes a positive force, injecting sustained momentum into building an Asia-Pacific community,” Zhuang concluded. The forum resulted in the issuance of a statement on promoting AI development, which outlines priorities for continued regional cooperation on AI.

en: Business Leaders Call for Urgent Action to Restore Trade Stability and Growth Across the Asia-Pacific
cn: 商界领袖呼吁紧急采取行动，恢复亚太地区的贸易稳定和增长
summary: 推进数字贸易与转型，建立数字产品永久免关税，通过新设立的亚太经济合作组织无纸化贸易卓越中心实现普遍无纸化贸易，促进互操作性监管，推动负责任的人工智能，打击在线欺诈，并支持量子技术治理和素养培养。
summaryEn: Advance digital trade and transformation by establishing a permanent ban on tariffs for digital products, along with enabling universal paperless trade via the new APEC Centre of Excellence for Paperless Trade, fostering interoperable regulations, promoting responsible AI, combating online fraud and supporting quantum technology governance and literacy.

en: PEC Data for Growth High-level Roundtable Chair’s Statement
cn: APEC增长数据高级别圆桌会议主席声明
summary: 一、营造一个开放且有利的数据访问和使用环境 ——加强政策对话，包括通过现有机制和自愿经验交流，促进数据的使用、互操作性、可访问性和应用，同时确保信任、安全、数据保护与隐私，以及知识产权的尊重。 — 支持有利的政策环境，以提升创新和市场信心。我们还将推动跨境数据流动，同时加强企业和消费者的信任。 ——鼓励多方利益相关者参与数据治理，包括与政策制定者、监管机构和企业的合作，旨在促进不同数据治理方法间的自愿信息共享和互操作性。 二、加强数据驱动的创新与应用 — 促进数据的负责任使用，以支持科学研究、技术创新、工业发展和公共服务现代化。推动数据驱动的创新和经济增长，推动新兴技术的商业化和应用，以发挥其变革潜力。 —— 支持提升数字技能和创新能力，使中小微企业及社会各领域的相关利益相关者能够更好地利用数字工具和数据资源，促进创新和经济增长，包括通过能力建设以及自愿分享信息和最佳实践。 三、深化数据互联合作 ——推进关于可靠、可访问、可扩展、可信、安全且有韧性的数据基础设施开发的对话，提升数据系统之间的互操作性，减少碎片化，避免不必要的数据孤岛，促进区域内数据资源的价值创造。 ——加强跨境数据政策的沟通与对话，以促进成员经济体之间的理解与信任。 — 通过经验分享和能力建设活动，支持企业、研究机构及其他利益相关方在相关议题上的协作，最大化数字化对我们人民的益处。 结论 我们相信，通过持续的对话与合作，APEC能够更好地利用数据在推动亚太地区经济增长中的作用。鼓励成员经济体继续交流经验、最佳实践和取得的进展，并在APEC框架下探索潜在合作领域，包括通过数字经济指导小组（DESG）及其子组织数据隐私小组（DPS）等。
summaryEn: I. Foster an Open and Enabling Environment for Data Access and Use — Strengthen policy dialogue, including through existing mechanisms, and the voluntary exchange of experiences, and promote the use, interoperability, accessibility and application of data while ensuring trust, security, data protection and privacy, and respect for intellectual property rights. — Support an enabling policy environment to boost innovation and market confidence. We will also work to facilitate cross-border data flows, while strengthening business and consumer trust. — Encourage multistakeholder engagement, including with policymakers, regulators, and businesses on data governance, with a view to promoting voluntary information sharing and interoperability across different approaches to data governance. II. Strengthen Data-Driven Innovation and Application — Facilitate the responsible use of data to support scientific research, technological innovation, industrial development and public service modernization. Foster data-driven innovation and economic growth, and promote the commercialization and application of emerging technologies, to harness its transformative potential. — Support the enhancement of digital skills and innovation capabilities, enabling MSMEs and relevant stakeholders in all segments of our societies to better utilize digital tools and data resources to foster innovation and economic growth, including through capacity building and the voluntary sharing of information and best practices. III. Deepen Cooperation on Data Connectivity — Advance dialogue on the development of reliable, accessible, scalable, trusted, secure and resilient data infrastructure and improve interoperability among data systems to reduce fragmentation, avoid unnecessary data silos, and facilitate value creation of data resources across the region. — Enhance communication and dialogues on cross-border data policies to foster understanding and trust among member economies. — Support collaboration among businesses, research institutions and other stakeholders on relevant issues through experience-sharing and capacity building activities, to maximize the benefits of digitalization for our people. Conclusion We believe that, through sustained dialogue and cooperation, APEC can better harness the role of data in driving economic growth across the Asia-Pacific region. Member economies are encouraged to continue to exchange experiences, best practices and progress made in this regard, and explore potential areas of cooperation under the APEC framework, including through the Digital Economy Steering Group (DESG) and its subgroup the Data Privacy Subgroup (DPS), among others.

en: APEC High-Level Forum on AI
cn: APEC人工智能高级别论坛
summary: 由中国主办的亚太经合组织人工智能高级别论坛，主题为“促进人工智能发展，惠及全民”，于2026年7月24日在中国四川成都举行。APEC成员经济体重申我们致力于深化交流、凝聚共识、促进合作和推动人工智能创新，同时进一步落实APEC布城愿景2040、APEC互联网与数字经济路线图（AIDER）以及APEC人工智能倡议（2026-2030）。 鉴于APEC成员经济体的多样化需求，我们鼓励各国经济体参与经验分享，促进亚太地区负责任的人工智能发展与应用，并期待在以下人工智能领域推动合作： 推动人工智能的安全开发与部署。我们鼓励优先考虑安全的人工智能开发，推动能够解决风险的创新，造福我们的员工。鼓励成员经济体交流促进可靠、可访问、可扩展、可信、安全且具韧性的人工智能基础设施发展及提升数字基础设施可及性的最佳实践。我们将致力于促进跨境数据流动，这对人工智能发展至关重要，同时加强消费者和企业的信任。 加速人工智能应用的负责任采用。我们鼓励实施各种形式的人工智能驱动经济增长，为人工智能在经济部门和社会中的整合营造有利环境。我们推动为社会各阶层提供可及的教育和培训资源，以提升人工智能素养和技能。我们认识到人工智能在促进贸易、现代化海关程序和提升企业竞争力方面的日益重要作用，并鼓励在这些领域进一步交流最佳实践，以支持经济增长。 营造有利于人工智能创新的环境。 我们赞赏推动市场导向和创新驱动的政策，推动人工智能的发展和广泛采用。我们鼓励成员经济体考虑应对风险并促进负责任AI采用的政策。在尊重安全、数据保护和知识产权的同时，我们鼓励会员经济体支持通过开发和部署实现强大安全保障的开源模型和项目。 促进广泛的合作，以最大化APEC的参与和利益。我们欢迎亚太地区成员经济体间的能力建设和知识共享，并通过开放对话和合作努力，包括与公共和私营部门，促进创新和经济增长。我们将继续支持所有APEC成员国参与人工智能驱动的经济，最大化人工智能为我们人民带来的益处。 鉴于亚太经合组织数字经济指导组（DESG）、电信与信息工作组及其他亚太经合组织分会在加强亚太地区人工智能合作中的重要作用，我们致力于在DESG全体会议期间组织人工智能政策对话，促进人工智能造福人民并探索人工智能创新。 采用、获取及其他新兴问题，同时保持对人工智能发展新发展的开放态度。我们感谢中国主办本次论坛，并感谢成都市和四川省在本次会议上给予的卓越款待。我们期待未来继续与DESG就人工智能展开对话。
summaryEn: The APEC High-Level Forum on AI, hosted by China under the theme of “Promoting AI Development for Good and for All,” was held in Chengdu, Sichuan, China on July 24, 2026. APEC member economies reaffirmed our commitment to deepening exchanges, building consensus, forging cooperation and promoting innovation on AI, while further implementing the APEC Putrajaya Vision 2040, the APEC Internet and Digital Economy Roadmap (AIDER), and the APEC AI Initiative (2026-2030). While bearing in mind the diverse needs of APEC member economies, we encourage economies to engage in experience sharing to foster responsible development and adoption of AI across the Asia-Pacific and look forward to promoting cooperation in the following areas of AI: Promote the secure development and deployment of AI. We encourage AI development that prioritizes security and promotes innovation that addresses risks for the benefit of our people. Member economies are encouraged to exchange best practices on fostering the development of reliable, accessible, scalable, trusted, secure and resilient AI infrastructure and enhancing the accessibility of digital infrastructure. We will work to facilitate cross-border data flows, which are critical to AI development, while strengthening consumer and business trust. Accelerate the responsible adoption of AI applications. We encourage the implementation of various forms of AI-enabled economic growth to build an enabling environment for the integration of AI across economic sectors and throughout our societies. We promote the provision of accessible educational and training resources for all segments of our societies to improve AI literacy and skills. We recognize the growing role of AI in facilitating trade, modernizing customs procedures, and enhancing business competitiveness, and encourage the further exchange of best practices in these areas to support economic growth. Foster an enabling environment for AI innovation. We commend policies that promote market-oriented and innovation-driven approaches for the development and broad adoption of AI. We encourage member economies to consider policies that address risks and promote responsible AI adoption. While respecting security, data protection and intellectual property rights, we encourage member economies to support open-source models and projects that employ strong security assurance through development and deployment. Foster broad-based cooperation to maximize participation and benefits across APEC. We welcome capacity building, and knowledge sharing across member economies in the Asia-Pacific region and fostering innovation and economic growth through open dialogue and collaborative efforts, including with the public and private sectors. We will continue support for all APEC member economies to participate in the AI-driven economy and maximize the benefits of AI for our people. Recognizing the important role of the APEC Digital Economy Steering Group (DESG), the Telecommunications and Information Working Group, and other APEC sub-fora in strengthening AI cooperation in the Asia-Pacific region, we are committed to organizing policy dialogues on AI during the DESG plenary to promote AI for the benefit of our people and explore AI innovation, adoption, access, and other emerging issues while remaining open to new developments as AI evolves. We express our gratitude to China for hosting this Forum and our appreciation to the City of Chengdu and Sichuan Province for the exceptional hospitality extended at this meeting. We look forward to continued DESG dialogues on AI in the future.

en: G20 Osaka Leaders' Declaration
cn: 大阪G20领导人宣言
summary: 创新：数字化，数据自由流动与信任 10. 创新是经济增长的重要驱动力，同时也能推动实现可持续发展目标和提升包容性。我们将通过数字化和推动新兴技术的应用，致力于实现一个包容、可持续、安全、值得信赖且富有创新性的社会。我们共同倡导以人为本的未来社会，这一理念被日本以“社会5.0”形式推广。随着数字化正在改变我们经济和社会的各个方面，我们认识到有效利用数据作为促进经济增长、发展和社会福祉的关键因素。我们致力于推动国际政策讨论，充分发挥数据的潜力。 11. 跨境数据、信息、思想和知识的流动带来更高的生产力、更强的创新和改善的可持续发展，同时也带来了隐私、数据保护、知识产权和安全方面的挑战。通过持续应对这些挑战，我们可以进一步促进数据自由流通，增强消费者和企业的信任。在这方面，必须尊重国内外的法律框架。这种数据自由流通和信任将抓住数字经济的机遇。我们将合作促进不同框架的互操作性，并肯定数据在开发中的作用。我们重申贸易与数字经济接口的重要性，并注意到电子商务联合声明倡议下的持续讨论，并重申世贸组织电子商务工作计划的重要性。 12. 为进一步促进数字经济创新，我们支持分享有效政策和监管方法及框架的良好实践，这些方法既创新又灵活，并适应数字时代，包括通过监管沙盒的应用。负责任地开发和使用人工智能（AI）可以成为推动可持续发展目标（SDGs）实现可持续和包容社会的动力。为了增强公众对人工智能技术的信任与信心，充分发挥其潜力，我们承诺采用以人为本的人工智能方法，并欢迎采纳来自经济合作与发展组织（OECD）人工智能推荐的非约束性G20人工智能原则。此外，我们认识到推动数字经济安全、解决安全漏洞和漏洞的重要性日益提升。我们重申知识产权保护的重要性。随着物联网（IoT）等新兴技术的快速扩展，关于数字经济中安全问题持续讨论的价值也在不断增长。作为G20成员，我们确认需要进一步应对这些紧迫挑战。我们重申弥合数字鸿沟、促进微型、小型和中型企业（MSMEs）及所有个人，尤其是弱势群体，采用数字化的必要性，同时鼓励城市间的网络交流和经验分享，以推动智慧城市的发展。
summaryEn: Innovation: Digitalization, Data Free Flow with Trust 10. Innovation is an important driver for economic growth, which can also contribute to advancing towards the SDGs and enhancing inclusiveness. We will work toward achieving an inclusive, sustainable, safe, trustworthy and innovative society through digitalization and promoting the application of emerging technologies. We share the notion of a human-centered future society, which is being promoted by Japan as Society 5.0. As digitalization is transforming every aspect of our economies and societies, we recognize the critical role played by effective use of data, as an enabler of economic growth, development and social well-being. We aim to promote international policy discussions to harness the full potential of data. 11. Cross-border flow of data, information, ideas and knowledge generates higher productivity, greater innovation, and improved sustainable development, while raising challenges related to privacy, data protection, intellectual property rights, and security. By continuing to address these challenges, we can further facilitate data free flow and strengthen consumer and business trust. In this respect, it is necessary that legal frameworks, both domestic and international, should be respected. Such data free flow with trust will harness the opportunities of the digital economy. We will cooperate to encourage the interoperability of different frameworks, and we affirm the role of data for development. We also reaffirm the importance of interface between trade and digital economy, and note the ongoing discussion under the Joint Statement Initiative on electronic commerce, and reaffirm the importance of the Work Programme on electronic commerce at the WTO. 12. To further promote innovation in the digital economy, we support the sharing of good practices on effective policy and regulatory approaches and frameworks that are innovative as well as agile, flexible, and adapted to the digital era, including through the use of regulatory sandboxes. The responsible development and use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) can be a driving force to help advance the SDGs and to realize a sustainable and inclusive society. To foster public trust and confidence in AI technologies and fully realize their potential, we commit to a human-centered approach to AI, and welcome the non-binding G20 AI Principles, drawn from the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) Recommendation on AI. Further, we recognize the growing importance of promoting security in the digital economy and of addressing security gaps and vulnerabilities. We affirm the importance of protection of intellectual property. Along with the rapid expansion of emerging technologies including the Internet of Things (IoT), the value of an ongoing discussion on security in the digital economy is growing. We, as G20 members, affirm the need to further work on these urgent challenges. We reaffirm the importance of bridging the digital divide and fostering the adoption of digitalization among micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and all individuals, particularly vulnerable groups and also encourage networking and experience-sharing among cities for the development of smart cities.

en: G20 Bali Leaders' Declaration
cn: G20巴厘岛峰会领导人宣言
summary: 24.新冠肺炎疫情加速了数字生态系统和数字经济的转型。我们认识到数字转型对实现可持续发展目标的重要性。我们承认可及且高质量的数字互联互通对于数字包容和数字转型至关重要，而强韧、安全、可靠的网络环境对于增强对数字经济的信心和信任是必要的。我们认识到制定政策以打造有利、包容、开放、公平和非歧视的数字经济的重要性，该数字经济促进新技术的应用，使企业和企业家蓬勃发展，保护并赋能消费者，同时应对与数字鸿沟、隐私、数据保护、知识产权和在线安全相关的挑战。我们承认打击虚假信息活动、网络威胁、在线滥用以及确保互联互通基础设施安全的重要性。我们致力于进一步实现基于信任的数据自由流动并促进跨境数据流动。我们将推进更加包容、以人民为中心、赋能和可持续的数字转型。我们亦重申数据对发展、经济增长和社会福祉的作用。 27.我们支持继续实施《G20完善跨境支付路线图》，包括未来交付关键绩效指标的初步估算和设定下一阶段工作重点的2022年进展报告。我们鼓励各国央行、其他公共当局和支付行业继续就这些重要举措开展协作，以完善跨境支付。我们欢迎国际清算银行（BIS）支付与市场基础设施委员会（CPMI）关于支付系统互联互通和应用程序接口（API）作用的报告。我们也欢迎BIS CPMI、BIS创新hub、国际货币基金组织和世界银行关于央行数字货币（CBDC）跨境支付准入和互操作性方案的联合报告。
summaryEn: 24.The COVID-19 pandemic has accelerated the transformation of the digital ecosystem and digital economy. We recognize the importance of digital transformation in reaching the SDGs. We acknowledge that affordable and high-quality digital connectivity is essential for digital inclusion and digital transformation, while a resilient, safe and secure online environment is necessary to enhance confidence and trust in the digital economy. We recognize the importance of policies to create an enabling, inclusive, open, fair and non-discriminatory digital economy that fosters the application of new technologies, allows businesses and entrepreneurs to thrive, and protects and empowers consumers, while addressing the challenges, related to digital divides, privacy, data protection, intellectual property rights, and online safety. We acknowledge the importance to counter disinformation campaigns, cyber threats, online abuse, and ensuring security in connectivity infrastructure. We remain committed to further enable data free flow with trust and promote cross-border data flows. We will advance a more inclusive, human-centric, empowering, and sustainable digital transformation. We also reaffirm the role of data for development, economic growth and social well-being. 27.We support continued implementation of the G20 Roadmap for Enhancing Cross-Border Payments, including the future delivery of the initial estimates for key performance indicators and 2022 Progress Report that sets out priorities for the next stage of work. We encourage central banks, other public authorities and the payments industry to continue to work collaboratively on these important initiatives to enhance cross-border payments. We welcome the report by the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) Committee on Payments and Market Infrastructures (CPMI) on interlinking payment systems and the role of Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) that was presented in a joint workshop by the Indonesian G20 Presidency in coordination with the BIS CPMI and the BIS Innovation Hub (BISIH) on cross-border payments and interoperability at the Festival Ekonomi Keuangan Digital Indonesia (FEKDI) 2022. We also welcome the joint report by the BIS CPMI, BISIH, IMF, and World Bank on options for access to and interoperability of Central Bank Digital Currencies (CBDCs) for cross-border payments.

en: G20 New Delhi Leaders' Declaration
cn: G20新德里峰会领导人宣言
summary: 19. 我们重申以WTO为核心的、基于规则的、非歧视性、公平、开放、包容、平等、可持续和透明的多边贸易体系不可或缺。 iv. 欢迎《贸易文件数字化高级原则》，将努力推动实施，并鼓励其他国家考虑这些原则。 55. 技术能够实现快速转型，弥合现有数字鸿沟，加速包容性和可持续发展进程。数字公共基础设施（DPI）作为一个不断发展的概念，是一系列共享数字系统，由公共和私营部门共同建设和利用，以安全和强韧的基础设施为基础，可建立在开放标准和规范以及开源软件之上，能够实现社会规模的服务交付。在我们使数字公共基础设施实现互操作性的自愿努力中，我们认识到基于信任的数据自由流动和跨境数据流动的重要性，同时尊重适用的法律框架。我们亦重申数据对发展的作用。 56. 我们认识到，安全、可靠、可信、问责和包容的数字公共基础设施，尊重人权、个人数据、隐私和知识产权，能够促进韧性，实现服务交付和创新。为此，我们： i. 欢迎《G20数字公共基础设施系统框架》，这是一个用于DPI开发、部署和治理的自愿和建议性框架。 57. 有利、包容、开放、公平、非歧视和安全的数字经济对所有国家和利益相关方日益重要，同时尊重适用的法律框架。我们将分享各自的方法和良好实践，以建设安全、可靠和强韧的数字经济。为此，我们： i. 欢迎非约束性的《G20支持企业建立数字经济安全、韧性、安全和信任高级原则》。 59. 我们欢迎关于引入和采用央行数字货币（CBDC）可能产生的宏观金融影响的讨论，特别是对跨境支付以及国际货币和金融体系的影响。 61. AI的快速发展有望带来全球数字经济的繁荣和扩张。我们致力于以负责任、包容和以人为本的方式利用AI解决挑战以造福公众，同时保护人们的权利和安全。为确保负责任的AI开发、部署和使用，必须解决人权保护、透明度和可解释性、公平性、问责制、监管、安全性、适当的人工监督、伦理、偏见、隐私和数据保护等问题。为释放AI的全部潜力、公平分享其收益并降低风险，我们将共同努力促进国际合作，并进一步讨论AI的国际治理。为此，我们： i. 重申对2019年G20 AI原则的承诺，努力分享利用AI支持数字经济解决方案的方法信息。 ii. 将采取促进创新的监管/治理方式，在最大化收益的同时考虑到使用AI相关的风险。
summaryEn: 19. We reaffirm that a rules-based, non-discriminatory, fair, open, inclusive, equitable, sustainable and transparent multilateral trading system, with WTO at its core, is indispensable. iv. Welcome the High-Level Principles on Digitalization of Trade Documents and will make efforts to encourage implementation, and encourage other countries to consider these principles. 55. Technology can enable rapid transformations for bridging the existing digital divides and accelerate progress for inclusive and sustainable development. Digital public infrastructure (DPI), as an evolving concept and as a set of shared digital systems, built and leveraged by both the public and private sectors, based on secure and resilient infrastructure, and can be built on open standards and specifications, as well as open-source software can enable delivery of services at societal-scale. In our voluntary efforts to make digital public infrastructure interoperable, we recognize the importance of data free flow with trust and cross-border data flows while respecting applicable legal frameworks. We also reaffirm the role of Data for Development. 56. We recognize that safe, secure, trusted, accountable and inclusive digital public infrastructure, respectful of human rights, personal data, privacy and intellectual property rights can foster resilience, and enable service delivery and innovation. To this end, we: i. Welcome the G20 Framework for Systems of Digital Public Infrastructure, a voluntary and suggested framework for the development, deployment and governance of DPI. 57. An enabling, inclusive, open, fair, non-discriminatory and secure digital economy is increasingly important for all countries and stakeholders while respecting applicable legal frameworks. We will share our approaches and good practices to build a safe, secure and resilient digital economy. To this extent, we: i. Welcome the non-binding G20 High-level Principles to Support Businesses in Building Safety, Security, Resilience, and Trust in the Digital Economy. 59. We welcome discussions on the potential macro-financial implications arising from the introduction and adoption of Central Bank Digital Currencies (CBDCs), notably on cross-border payments as well as on the international monetary and financial system. 61. The rapid progress of AI promises prosperity and expansion of the global digital economy. It is our endeavour to leverage AI for the public good by solving challenges in a responsible, inclusive and human-centric manner, while protecting people's rights and safety. To ensure responsible AI development, deployment and use, the protection of human rights, transparency and explainability, fairness, accountability, regulation, safety, appropriate human oversight, ethics, biases, privacy, and data protection must be addressed. To unlock the full potential of AI, equitably share its benefits and mitigate risks, we will work together to promote international cooperation and further discussions on international governance for AI. To this end, we: i. Reaffirm our commitment to G20 AI Principles (2019) and endeavour to share information on approaches to using AI to support solutions in the digital economy. ii. Will pursue a pro-innovation regulatory/governance approach that maximizes the benefits and takes into account the risks associated with the use of AI.

en: G20 Maceió Ministerial Declaration on Digital Inclusion for All
cn: G20马塞约数字包容部长级宣言
summary: 数字包容、普遍和有意义互联互通 4. 我们承诺为所有人实现普遍和有意义的互联互通，考虑到尽管数字互联度不断增长，但全球仍有三分之一的人口——其中大多数在发展中国家，特别是在最不发达国家——由于缺乏可及性、可负担性、数字素养和技能，仍然无法接入互联网。我们重申2023年G20领导人承诺到2030年将性别数字鸿沟缩小一半。我们认识到，弥合这一互联差距需要采取协调和有针对性的努力，解决服务不足和未互联人群的具体需求，不仅通过可靠、强韧和高性能基础设施提供普遍接入，还要提供一种安全、可持续和高质量的互联水平，使用户（包括弱势群体）能够以可负担的成本获得安全、满意、丰富和高效的在线体验：即有意义的互联互通。 数字政府与包容性数字公共基础设施 8. 我们重申推动包容、开放、可及、公平、以人为本、安全、可靠、可信、可持续、发展导向的数字转型的重要性，其中基于数字公共基础设施的数字政府服务可以在数字时代发挥关键作用，提高公共部门的响应能力、有效性、透明度和可靠性，同时保护隐私、个人数据、人权和基本自由。在这方面，我们回顾"G20数字公共基础设施系统框架"。 9. 我们认识到，数字身份作为基本的数字公共基础设施，往往是数字包容的切入点，也是实现可持续发展目标16.9（即到2030年"为所有人提供法律身份"）的机制。我们认识到，在符合安全、隐私和个人数据保护适用法律框架下实施的可信数字身份和有效认证政策，有助于减少获取服务和商业机会的障碍，从而促进政府服务的透明度、问责性、效率和数字经济信任，且不歧视。考虑到G20成员和受邀国家在数字身份和认证政策方面可能采取不同方法并处于不同实施阶段，我们欢迎与经合组织合作制定的《G20数字身份治理通用原则》。 10. 我们认识到，在符合适用法律框架（包括安全、隐私和个人数据保护、人权和知识产权）的前提下，通过互操作性实现管辖区内的数据获取和数据共享，能够释放数据对公共和私营部门的公共利益潜力。在这方面，我们还认识到开源软件、开放应用程序接口及支持它们的国际标准（包括开放标准）以及安全设计解决方案的重要作用。在数据共享方面，我们重申促进跨境数据流动和基于信任的数据自由流动的重要性，同时尊重国内和国际适用的法律框架，并承认数据对发展的作用。巴西主席国提出的《G20公共机构之间及与私营部门之间的数据获取与共享汇编》，构成了一份在适当保障措施下部署和加强数据获取和共享解决方案的参考文件。 11. 我们认识到，基于安全和隐私保护的数字公共基础设施的数字政府服务，可以作为数字经济包容的催化剂，因为它们有潜力提供全社会范围的数字能力，促进创新和可持续发展。G20数字经济工作组巴西主席国组织的"数字政府与包容"虚拟研讨会，将以数字包容及数字公共基础设施对公平数字转型的贡献为核心的对话置于中心位置。 在线信息完整性与数字经济信任 12. 我们认识到数字平台通过放大信息传播和促进跨地理边界的交流，重塑了数字生态系统和在线互动。然而，信息领域的数字化以及人工智能等新技术的加速发展，极大地影响了虚假信息和错误信息、仇恨言论和其他形式的在线危害的速度、规模和范围，这一现象因数字领域各种经济激励而加剧。我们强调数字平台需要根据相关政策和适用法律框架保持透明度和责任感，并寻求与平台和相关利益相关方在这方面开展合作。 13. 我们因此认识到促进信息完整性的相关性，信息完整性被理解为一个允许及时获取可靠、多元、准确信息和知识的信息生态系统的结果。在缺失信息完整性的情况下，对数字经济、公共机构以及治理和民主进程的信任可能受到影响，对社会凝聚力和经济繁荣以及行使人权的能力产生负面影响。保护信息完整性对于维持对信息生态系统以及科学和历史知识的信心也至关重要，并可能最小化特别影响弱势群体的极化趋势。它还可能有助于缓解政治、社会和经济不稳定、极端化和暴力极端主义，同时促进对环境退化的应对。作为更好地评估这一现象全球范围的努力，巴西主席国承认联合国教科文组织为这一辩论提供的贡献。 14. G20成员及其他国家可以通过不同方式促进信息完整性，方式应符合国际法和适用法律框架，让所有利益相关方有意义地参与，并考虑到不同国家的具体情况。由于获取和分析信息的能力对于建立社会抵御虚假信息和错误信息的韧性至关重要，我们鼓励投资在线安全教育和数字媒体及信息素养，以提高认识并帮助用户识别和降低在线危害风险，这些风险不成比例地影响妇女和女童。同时，促进可持续和强健的数字生态系统以及多元和强韧的信息环境也很重要，包括通过获取独立、事实和循证信息来对抗虚假和错误信息。在承认适用法律框架的同时，我们鼓励各国按照附件3促进数字环境中的信息完整性和信任，该附件汇编了旨在增强数字平台透明度和问责制以降低在线危害风险的政策和治理措施示例，同时保障人权和基本自由。 15. 为保护和促进信息完整性，在信息生态系统中开发和部署人工智能解决方案时，特别是用于个性化、审核和生成内容时，应具有伦理性、透明度、可审计性和问责性，并在人工监督下进行，符合适用法律框架，以确保隐私、个人数据保护以及尊重人权、基本自由和知识产权。有效缓解偏见也很重要，特别是那些可能不成比例地影响弱势群体的偏见。我们认为，内容认证和来源机制及相关技术标准有助于识别人工智能生成的内容，并使用户能够识别信息操纵。在适当保障措施下的透明度和关于数据、算法和内容审核的可解释性，尊重知识产权以及隐私和数据保护，是构建健康信息生态系统的关键。G20成员和受邀国家鼓励在应对信息完整性侵蚀及其对数字经济影响的倡议和最佳实践方面开展合作和信息共享。 16. G20成员、受邀国家、国际组织以及来自民间社会和私营部门的参与者有机会在数字经济工作组 sidelines活动"促进信息完整性：打击虚假信息、仇恨言论和对公共机构的在线威胁"上审查信息完整性全球讨论的现状。在该活动期间，巴西主席国宣布了"气候变化信息完整性全球倡议"，将与联合国、联合国教科文组织和有兴趣的国家合作开展。 人工智能促进包容可持续发展和减少不平等 17. 我们认识到，安全、可靠和可信的人工智能在以透明、合乎伦理、负责任和可靠的方式应用时，可以作为实现经济增长和包容性可持续发展的催化剂，涵盖社会、经济和环境三个维度。我们重申G20人工智能原则和联合国教科文组织《人工智能伦理建议书》。基于《G20新德里领导人宣言》反映的领导人共识，并在历届主席国工作基础上，我们重申致力于为善、为全民利用人工智能，释放人工智能的全部潜力，为所有人分享其收益并降低风险。 18. 我们承认人工智能领域正在进行的国际努力和倡议，特别是联合国大会协商一致通过的决议"抓住安全、可靠和可信的人工智能系统促进可持续发展的机遇"和"加强人工智能能力建设方面的国际合作"，并期待秘书长人工智能高级别咨询机构报告的发布。 19. 我们重申致力于为善利用人工智能，并决心采取平衡方式，释放人工智能的全部潜力，促进公平获取和分享其收益。我们还强调致力于通过采取基于风险、以人为本、发展导向、促进创新的人工智能政策和治理方式来促进收益并降低风险，这些方式与安全、隐私和个人数据保护、人权和知识产权方面的适用法律框架保持一致。我们还强调承诺共同努力促进国际合作，并进一步讨论人工智能促进包容可持续发展和减少不平等。在此意义上，我们欢迎《促进人工智能为善、为全民的开发、部署和使用资源支持》文件，该文件利用了联合国教科文组织的工作并与其合作完成。 21. 关切地注意到人工智能可能在国家内部和国家之间扩大数字鸿沟的风险，我们呼吁在该领域促进包容性国际合作，特别是在能力建设、联合研究和自愿技术转让及知识共享方面，在双方同意的条件下进行，以扩大所有国家特别是发展中国家在数字转型中的参与，以利用收益并有效参与安全、可靠和可信的人工智能系统的开发、部署和使用，以负责任和合乎伦理的方式进行。在此意义上，我们强调增强所有国家特别是发展中国家发展技术专长和能力、利用数据和计算资源以及实现开源技术和系统和开放数据在规模化交付人工智能收益方面的潜力的重要性。巴西主席国展示了与联合国教科文组织支持制作的《人工智能准备度与能力评估工具包》。
summaryEn: Digital inclusion, universal and meaningful connectivity 4. We affirm our commitment to achieving universal and meaningful connectivity for all, considering that, despite growing digital connectivity, one third of the world’s population — the majority of which in developing countries, particularly in least developed countries —, remains unconnected to the Internet, due to the lack of accessibility, affordability, digital literacy and skills. We reaffirm the G20 leaders commitment in 2023 to cut the gender digital divide in half by 2030. We recognize that closing this connectivity gap requires coordinated and targeted efforts to address the specific needs of the underserved and unconnected, providing not only universal access through reliable, resilient and high performance infrastructure but also a level of secure, sustainable and high-quality connectivity that enables users, including those in vulnerable situations, to have a safe, satisfying, enriching and productive online experience at an affordable cost: in other words, meaningful connectivity. Digital government and inclusive digital public infrastructure 8. We reaffirm the importance of promoting an inclusive, open, accessible, equitable, human-centric, safe, secure, trusted, sustainable, development-oriented digital transformation, in which digital government services, including those based on Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI), can play a key role in improving the responsiveness, effectiveness, transparency and reliability of the public sector in the digital era, while protecting privacy, personal data, human rights and fundamental freedoms. In this regard, we recall the “G20 framework on systems of DPI”. 9. We acknowledge that digital identification, a basic DPI, can often be an entry point to digital inclusion and a mechanism to reach target 16.9 of the Sustainable Development Goals, namely to “provide legal identity for all” by 2030. We recognize that trustworthy digital identity and effective authentication policies implemented in compliance with applicable legal frameworks on security, privacy and personal data protection can help reduce barriers to accessing services and business opportunities, thus promoting transparency, accountability, efficiency of government services and trust in the digital economy, without discrimination. Taking into account and acknowledging that G20 members and invited countries may have diverse approaches and stand at different implementation stages of policies regarding digital identification and authentication, we welcome the “G20 General Principles on the Governance of Digital Identity”, developed in collaboration with the OECD. 10. We recognize that data access and data sharing within jurisdictions, including through interoperability, and in compliance with applicable legal frameworks, including on security, privacy and the protection of personal data, human rights and intellectual property rights, can unleash the potential of data to both public and private sectors for public interest. In this regard, we also recognize the important role of open-source software, open Application Programming Interfaces (API) and the international standards that support them, including open standards, as well as secure-by-design solutions. In the context of data sharing, we reaffirm the importance of enabling cross-border data flows and data free flow with trust, while respecting domestic as well as international applicable legal frameworks and acknowledging the role of data for development. The “G20 Compendium on data access and data sharing across public institutions and with the private sector for public interest”, introduced by the Brazilian presidency, constitutes a reference document for the deployment and enhancement of data access and data sharing solutions, with appropriate safeguards. 11. We acknowledge that digital government services, including those based on secure and privacy-preserving digital public infrastructure, may act as catalysts to inclusion in the digital economy, as they have the potential to provide society-wide digital capabilities that promote innovation and sustainable development. The virtual workshop “Digital Government and Inclusion”, organized by the G20 DEWG Brazilian presidency, placed at its center the dialogue regarding digital inclusion and the contribution of digital public infrastructure to an equitable digital transformation. Integrity of information online and trust in the digital economy 12. We recognize that digital platforms have reshaped the digital ecosystem and online interactions by amplifying information dissemination and facilitating communication within and across geographical boundaries. However, the digitization of the information realm and the accelerated evolution of new technologies, such as artificial intelligence, has dramatically impacted the speed, scale, and reach of misinformation and disinformation, hate speech and other forms of online harms, a phenomenon exacerbated by a variety of economic incentives in the digital domain. We emphasize the need for digital platforms’ transparency and responsibility in line with relevant policies and applicable legal frameworks and seek to work with platforms and relevant stakeholders in this regard. 13. We thus recognize the relevance of promoting information integrity, understood as the result of an information ecosystem that allows for reliable, diverse, accurate information and knowledge, in a timely fashion. In its absence, trust in the digital economy, in public institutions, as well as in governance and democratic processes may be affected, with negative effects on social cohesion and economic prosperity and the ability to exercise human rights. The protection of information integrity is also vital for maintaining confidence in the information ecosystem and scientific and historical knowledge and may minimize polarization trends that particularly impact people in vulnerable situations. It may also contribute to mitigating political, social and economic instability, radicalization and violent extremism, while also facilitating responses to environmental degradation. As an effort to better assess the global extent of this phenomenon, the Brazilian presidency acknowledges the contributions of UNESCO to inform this debate. 14. G20 members and beyond may promote information integrity through different approaches, in manners that are consistent with international law and applicable legal frameworks, with meaningful participation of all stakeholders, and taking into account the specific contexts of different countries. Since the ability to access and analyze information is critical for building societal resilience against disinformation and misinformation, we encourage investments in online safety education and in digital media and information literacy, in order to raise awareness and assist users in identifying and mitigating risks of online harms, which disproportionally affect women and girls. In parallel, promoting a sustainable an robust digital ecosystem and diverse and resilient information environment is key, including through access to independent, factual and evidence-based information to counter mis- and disinformation. While acknowledging applicable legal frameworks, we encourage countries to promote information integrity and trust in the digital environment, which compiles examples of policies and governance measures aimed at enhancing digital platforms’ transparency and accountability to mitigate the risks of online harms, while safeguarding human rights and fundamental freedoms. 15. In order to protect and promote information integrity, the development and deployment of Artificial Intelligence (AI) solutions in information ecosystems, especially when aimed at personalizing, moderating and generating content, should be ethical, transparent, auditable and accountable, with human oversight and in compliance with applicable legal frameworks to ensure privacy, personal data protection and the respect of human rights, fundamental freedoms and intellectual property. It is also important to effectively mitigate biases, in particular those that may disproportionally affect people in vulnerable situations. We believe that content authentication and provenance mechanisms and related technical standards may help identify AI-generated content, and enable users to identify information manipulation. Transparency, with appropriate safeguards, and explainability regarding data, algorithms and content moderation, that respects intellectual property rights, and privacy and data protection, can be key for building healthy information ecosystems. G20 members and invited countries encourage cooperation and information sharing on initiatives and best practices addressing the erosion of information integrity and its impact on the digital economy. 16. G20 members, invited countries, international organizations and participants from the civil society and the private sector had the opportunity to review the current stage of global discussions on information integrity at the DEWG side event “Promoting information integrity: combating disinformation, hate speech and threats to public institutions online”. During that event, Brazil’s presidency announced the “Global Initiative for Information Integrity on Climate Change”, to be developed in partnership with the United Nations (UN), United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) and interested countries. Artificial intelligence for inclusive sustainable development and inequality reduction 17. We recognize that safe, secure and trustworthy Artificial Intelligence (AI), when applied in a transparent, ethical, responsible and reliable manner, may act as a catalyst for achieving economic growth and inclusive sustainable development within its three dimensions: social, economic and environmental. We reaffirm the G20 AI principles and the UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI. Building upon our Leaders’ consensus as reflected in the G20 New Delhi Leaders’ Declaration and building upon previous presidencies, we reaffirm our commitment to leverage AI for good and for all, as well as to unlock the full potential of AI, share its benefits for all and mitigate its risks. 18. We acknowledge the ongoing international efforts and initiatives on AI, particularly the adoption by consensus of the U.N. General Assembly resolutions “Seizing the opportunities of safe, secure and trustworthy artificial intelligence systems for sustainable development” and “Enhancing International Cooperation on Capacity Building of Artificial Intelligence”, and look forward to the publication of the report of the Secretary-General’s High-Level Advisory Body on Artificial Intelligence. 19. We reaffirm our commitment to leverage AI for good and our determination to take a balanced approach that unlocks the full potential of AI, promoting an equitable access to and sharing of its benefits. We also underline our engagement to promote the benefits and mitigate risks derived from this technology by committing to risk-based and human-centric, development-oriented, innovation-friendly AI policy and governance approaches that are consistent with applicable legal frameworks on security, privacy and protection of personal data, human rights and intellectual property rights. We also highlight our commitment to work together to promote international cooperation and further discussions on AI for inclusive sustainable development and inequality reduction. In this sense, we welcome the document “Enabling resources for the development, deployment, and use of AI for good and for all”, leveraging the work of and in collaboration with UNESCO. 21. Noting with concern the potential risk presented by AI in widening digital divides within and between countries, we call for the promotion of inclusive international cooperation in this domain, notably on capacity building, joint research and voluntary technology transfer and knowledge sharing, on mutually agreed terms, in order to expand participation of all countries, in particular developing countries, in digital transformation to harness the benefits and effectively participate in the development, deployment and use of safe, secure and trustworthy artificial intelligence systems, in a responsible and ethical manner. In that sense, we underscore the importance of enhancing the ability of all countries, in particular the developing ones, to develop technical expertise and capacities, harnessing data and compute resources and realizing the potential of open-source technologies and systems and open data in delivering AI benefits at scale. The Brazilian presidency presented a Toolkit for Artificial Intelligence Readiness and Capacity Assessment, produced with the support of UNESCO.

summary: 四、政策支撑：打造开放安全的环境 二十国集团致力于鼓励观点交流、增进相互理解，加强政策制定与监管领域合作。为此鼓励成员国落实以下工作： 12. 知识产权 正如二十国集团安塔利亚峰会公报第26段所重申，充分、有效的知识产权保护与执法，对数字经济发展至关重要。 13. 推动发展道路自主选择方面的合作 开展国际合作，减少、消除、防范监管要求方面不必要的差异，释放数字经济发展活力。各成员国可在恪守自身国际法律义务的前提下，结合本国发展实际、历史文化传统、国内法律制度以及国家发展战略，选择适合自身的发展道路。 14. 建设透明的数字经济政策制定机制 - 制定并维护开放、包容、以实证为基础的数字经济政策，充分吸纳公共和私营部门所有利益相关方意见。法律、法规、政策及其他文件在审议、制定、实施之前，公开征求社会意见。 - 鼓励发布可公开获取的政府相关数据，挖掘数据赋能新技术、新产品、新服务的潜力。 - 推行智能化公共采购机制，在坚持市场导向的前提下，支持私营部门创新数字服务与数字产品。 15. 支持制定与应用国际标准 支持制定并采用符合世界贸易组织规则及原则等国际规则的技术产品与服务国际标准。 16. 增强信心与信任 - 保障在线交易的可用性、完整性、保密性与真实性。鼓励建设安全信息基础设施，支撑可信、稳定、可靠的互联网应用。 - 应对信息通信技术（含信息通信技术关键基础设施）使用过程中的安全风险、威胁与漏洞，加强国际协作、能力建设以及公私合作伙伴关系，包括在相关国际论坛开展建设性对话。支持公共与私营部门采用基于风险的技术标准、指引与最佳实践，识别、评估、处置安全风险。 - 加强在线交易领域打击网络犯罪的国际合作，共同维护信息通信技术环境安全。 17. 无线电频谱管理助力创新 认识到高效管理无线电频谱，能够充分释放数字经济时代移动革命的全部潜力。 五、未来行动：务实举措 当前数字化变革正在重塑经济与社会，并将持续产生深远影响。二十国集团同意就此开展合作，保持密切协作。为此，二十国集团将： - 推动政府、私营部门、民间社会、国际组织、技术和学术社群，以及行业组织、劳工组织等多方利益相关方开展多层次交流，交流观点，促进数字经济合作。 - 鼓励二十国集团成员国交流政策制定与立法经验，分享最佳实践。 - 开展数字经济相关培训与研究合作，惠及二十国集团内的发展中国家。 - 欢迎并支持联合国、联合国贸易和发展会议、联合国工业发展组织、国际劳工组织、国际货币基金组织、国际电信联盟、经合组织、世界银行集团等国际组织开展相关工作，针对数字经济信任、电子商务、跨境数据流动、物联网等重要政策议题，开发实用、贴切、适宜的衡量指标。 - 期待经合组织等国际组织及感兴趣的成员国进一步推进数字经济宏观统计测度工作：面向各国统计机构开展自愿性“最佳实践”问卷调查；为统计人员与数字企业举办数字经济数据源专题研讨会。 - 积极与B20工商峰会、L20劳工峰会、T20智库峰会等配套参与团体互动，推动产业界、企业、民间社会、学术界交换意见，凝聚共识，促进数字经济健康发展。
summaryEn: IV. Policy Support: For an Open and Secure Environment The G20 aims to encourage exchange of views, promote mutual understanding and strengthen cooperation in policy making and regulation. To this end, members are encouraged to: 12. Intellectual Property Recognize the key role of adequate and effective protection and enforcement of intellectual property rights to the development of the digital economy, as reaffirmed by paragraph 26 of the G20 Antalya Communique. 13. Promote cooperation with respect to independent choice of development path Encourage members engaging in international cooperation to reduce, eliminate, or prevent unnecessary differences in regulatory requirements to unleash the digital economy, recognizing that all members should chart development paths that are consistent with their international legal obligations and their development situations, historical and cultural traditions, national legal systems, and national development strategies. 14. Cultivate transparent digital economy policy-making  Develop and maintain open, transparent, inclusive, evidence-based digital economy policy making which takes into account the full input of all public and private stakeholders. Solicit their comments publicly before laws, regulations, policies and other instruments are deliberated, developed and implemented.  Encourage publishing of relevant, publicly available government data, recognizing the potential to boost new technology, products and services.  Encourage intelligent public procurement schemes to support the production of innovative digital services and products by the private sector, whilst keeping the need to be market led. 15. Support the development and use of international standards Support the development and their use of the international standards for technological products and services that are consistent with the international rules including WTO rules and principles. 16. Strengthen confidence and trust  Promote the availability, integrity, confidentiality and authenticity of online transactions. Encourage the development of secure information infrastructure to promote trusted, stable, and reliable internet applications.  As part of our efforts to address security risks, threats and vulnerabilities in the use of ICT, including those to ICT-enabled critical infrastructures, endeavor to strengthen international collaboration, capacity building and public-private partnerships, including through constructive discussions in relevant international fora. Support and encourage the use of risk-based technical standards, guidelines, and best-practices to identify, assess, and manage security risk by both the public and private sectors.  Jointly combat cybercrime and protect ICT environment by strengthening international cooperation on these issues in online transactions. 17. Manage radiofrequency spectrum to promote innovation Recognize the importance of efficient management of radiofrequency spectrum to achieve the full potential of the mobile revolution in the time of digital economy. V. Way Forward: Actions to Make a Difference Recognizing that the digital shifts underway are reshaping economies and societies today and will continue to do so in the future, the G20 agrees to cooperate and continue to work closely on these matters. In this regard, the G20 will:  Encourage multi-level exchanges, involving stakeholders such as governments, the private sector, civil society, international organizations, technical and academic communities as well as other parties such as industry organizations and worker organizations to share views and promote cooperation in digital economy.  Encourage G20 members to exchange experience on policy making and legislation, and share best practices among members.  Encourage training and research cooperation in digital economy issues to benefit the developing countries of the G20.  Welcome and encourage efforts made by the United Nations, UNCTAD, UNIDO, ILO, IMF, ITU, OECD, World Bank Group and other international organizations to develop better metrics for important policy issues like trust in the digital economy, e-commerce, cross-border data flows, and the Internet of Things, as practical, relevant and appropriate.  Look forward to IOs including the OECD and interested members, intensifying efforts to measure the digital economy in macroeconomic statistics through conducting a voluntary "good practices" survey of national statistical organizations, and organizing and hosting a workshop for statisticians and digital companies on source data to measure the digital economy.  Interact actively with other engagement groups such as the B20, L20 and T20 to exchange views among industry, business, civil society, and academia to pool ideas on how to promote a sound digital economy.
